latest.title: Friend advice influences mate choice through brain-to-brain synchrony and computational decision processes
latest.abstract: Abstract Individuals often rely on friends’ advice when facing ambiguous cues in mate-choice decisions, yet how such advice optimizes outcomes remains unclear. Using fNIRS hyperscanning, we simultaneously recorded neural and behavioral activity from 66 adult friend dyads (33 female dyads) during interactive advice phases. Computational modeling quantified the decision optimization parameter ( β ). It showed that only the bidirectional Social Information Processing (SIP) model—best fit behavioral data, indicating that optimization arises from reciprocal adaptation rather than one-way influence. Behaviorally, positive advice from in the relationship advisors increased mate-choice intention, whereas negative advice from single advisors more effectively promoted optimization. Both conditions elicited enhanced interpersonal neural synchrony (INS) in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), linked to risk evaluation, and in the left superior and middle temporal gyri (l-STG, l-MTG), associated with semantic processing and value transformation. Machine learning analyses showed that trial-level INS predicted momentary optimization, while task-level INS robustly forecasted overall decision improvement. Together, these findings demonstrate that decision optimization emerges from dynamic brain-to-brain alignment in control and semantic networks—reflecting emotional sharing during positive advice and risk re-evaluation during negative advice. This study extending SIP theory to interactive decision-making and revealing how friend advice enhances decision quality and social well-being.

latest.title: Uncovering the unseen: a multi-scalar scoping review of short-term rentals and urban transformation
latest.abstract: Abstract This critical scoping review examines how short-term rentals (STRs) have transformed urban tourism research and proposes an integrated sustainability framework bridging economic, social, spatial, and governance dimensions. Building on PRISMA-ScR guidelines, it systematically maps 161 studies published between 2009 and 2025, identifying key patterns in the economic, environmental, spatial, and regulatory analysis of STRs. The findings reveal that while STRs foster tourism growth and local development, they also exacerbate housing unaffordability, gentrification, and overtourism. The literature remains dominated by data-driven methods, spatial analysis, econometric modelling, and machine learning yet exhibits strong geographic biases and limited integration across disciplines. Results highlight the growing professionalisation of hosts, the role of digital technologies in reshaping governance, and the urgent need for adaptive, sustainability-oriented regulation. By consolidating fragmented debates, this review offers a multidimensional synthesis that informs smart city planning, digital governance, and the pursuit of the Sustainable Development Goals in contemporary tourism destinations.

latest.title: ปจจยทมอทธพลตอการยอมรบผลตภณฑสเตกไกคอลอนลกผสมซอสพรกไทยดำของผบรโภคในจงหวดพทลง
latest.venue: Warasan Wichai Lae Songserm Wichakan Kaset
authors: เสาวณีย์ เล็กบางพง
latest.abstract: This research aimed to study: 1) consumers’ personal characteristics; 2) consumer acceptance; 3) the level of importance of marketing mix factors; and 4) the factors influencing consumer acceptance of hybrid chicken steak with black pepper sauce in Phatthalung province. Data were collected from 400 respondents using questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations) and stepwise multiple regression analysis. The results were as follow: 1) The findings revealed that most consumers were female, aged 21–40 years, held a bachelor’s degree, were single, and worked in government agencies or state enterprises. 2) Consumers accepted it due to its appetizing aroma, pleasant taste, and deliciousness. Most preferred a price range of 50–100 Baht and a package weight of 101–200 grams, and showed an intention to continue purchasing the product in the future. 3) The overall marketing mix factors were rated at the highest level (\bar{x}=4.56), with product factors receiving the highest importance, followed by distribution channels, sales promotion, and price. 4) Age had a statistically significant negative effect on product acceptance at the 0.05 level, while product and distribution channel factors were the key determinants influencing consumer acceptance. These findings highlight consumers’ emphasis on product quality and accessibility. They may serve as guidelines for developing processed livestock products, adding value to agricultural products, and improving marketing strategies for community products in Phatthalung province.

latest.title: When Does Transparency Matter for Consumers’ Circular Decisions? Visibility and Traceability in Closed-Loop Supply Chains
latest.abstract: Markets are increasingly demanding greater supply chain transparency, yet this remains a significant challenge for many companies. Understanding whether and what type of information to disclose represents a significant challenge for companies, particularly when the information pertains to circular initiatives, such as those involved in closed-loop activities. This study, grounded in signaling theory, explores the effect of disclosing closed-loop supply chain information on consumers' intentions. We selected consumers as our unit of analysis for the active role they can play when referring to companies’ closed-loop initiatives, such as purchasing recycled products or participating in take-back programs. To test the hypotheses, two scenario-based experiments are conducted. The primary aim of the studies is to operationalize supply chain transparency through its visibility and traceability components in a closed-loop supply chain context. A second objective is to examine the effectiveness of transparency in closed-loop supply chains, analyzing how the two components influence consumer outcomes across different phases of the customer journey. The findings contribute to the growing literature on supply chain transparency, identifying the boundaries of signaling theory and offering insights for managers on strategic investments in transparency.

latest.title: Parasocial Interaction and Perceived Value as Determinants of Intention to Buy Made-in-Thailand Products through Live- Streaming Personal Shoppers
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This research investigates the rising trend of live shopping and jasa titipan (jastip) in Southeast Asian digital commerce, focusing on the growing popularity of Made in Thailand products among Indonesian consumers. Livestream commerce has changed consumer behaviour by offering immediacy, interactivity, and immersive digital experiences that lessen psychological distance between sellers and buyers. In Indonesia, live personal shopper sessions have become a key method for cross-border purchases of Thai cosmetics, fashion items, herbal supplements, and packaged foods, which are widely viewed as authentic and high-quality. Despite the market's rapid growth, previous research has mostly examined individual aspects like interactivity, trust, or entertainment, with limited attention to understanding the combined psychological factors influencing purchase intentions in livestream shopping. This study develops and tests a structural equation model (SEM) that includes social presence, parasocial interaction, perceived trust, perceived value, and perceived enjoyment to explain Indonesian consumers’ willingness to buy Thai products via live personal shoppers. The model captures both utilitarian and hedonic evaluation aspects, showing how relational bonding, immediacy, credibility cues, and experiential enjoyment collectively reduce uncertainty in cross-border transactions. This work contributes to theory by providing a comprehensive framework for understanding purchase intention formation in livestream commerce. Practically, the findings suggest strategic approaches for personal shoppers and digital platforms to enhance credibility and build consumer trust. latest.title: L'intelligence écologique et la consommation verte : le rôle médiateur de la conscience environnementale
latest.venue: Revue Internationale des Sciences de Gestion
latest.abstract: Cette étude examine l’effet de l’intelligence écologique sur la consommation verte, en intégrant la conscience environnementale comme mécanisme intermédiaire. Elle répond au décalage persistant entre connaissance des enjeux écologiques et adoption effective de comportements responsables. Une enquête quantitative menée auprès de 300 répondants a été analysée par la méthode PLS-SEM. Les résultats montrent que le modèle explique 54,8 % de la variance de la consommation verte. La conscience environnementale présente l’effet le plus important sur celle-ci (f² = 0,732), devant l’intelligence écologique (f² = 0,190). Ces résultats soulignent que la compréhension des enjeux écologiques ne suffit pas à elle seule et que leur intériorisation sous forme de conscience environnementale joue un rôle central dans l’adoption de comportements de consommation durable.

latest.title: Beyond Stimulation: A Motivation-Based Segmentation of Coffee Purchasing and Drinking Behaviour
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study aims to segment Turkish coffee consumers residing in Northern Cyprus by their motivations for coffee consumption and to examine how these segments differ in coffee attributes, information sources, consumption and purchasing behaviours, and socio-demographic characteristics. Data were collected using a structured online questionnaire and purposive sampling between April and June 2025. A total of 649 valid responses were analysed. Exploratory factor analysis was employed to identify underlying motivational dimensions of coffee consumption, followed by hierarchical and K-means cluster analysis to classify consumers into homogeneous segments. Five distinct motivational consumer segments were identified. Chi-square tests and ANOVA results revealed significant differences among these segments in preferred coffee attributes, information sources, consumption occasions, purchasing behaviour, consumption frequency, and socio-demographic characteristics. The findings demonstrated that motivations for coffee consumption in Northern Cyprus are multidimensional and strongly associated with behavioural and demographic profiles. Although coffee consumption has been widely examined in global literature, limited research has addressed it from a motivational segmentation perspective within a Mediterranean cultural context. By providing a comprehensive characterisation of consumer segments, this study contributes to the literature on coffee consumption and purchasing behaviour from a consumer psychology perspective.

latest.title: Social Media Marketing, Personal Selling, and Price Perception on Purchase Decision through Purchase Intention with Experience Environment as a Moderator
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of social media marketing, personal selling, and price perception on purchase decision, mediated by purchase intention and moderated by experience environment, within the Indonesian residential property sector. Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior, Servicescape theory, and the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, an integrative model is tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) on data collected from 304 confirmed buyers at CitraLand Tallasa City Makassar. Results confirm that price perception constitutes the dominant predictor of purchase intention, followed by social media marketing, while personal selling yields a non-significant sufficiency-based effect. Purchase intention and experience environment both exert significant direct effects on purchase decision. Purchase intention fully mediates the effects of price perception and social media marketing on purchase decision, whereas the hypothesised moderating role of experience environment is not supported. NCA establishes that all five constructs represent necessary conditions of medium magnitude, with experience environment imposing the most binding prerequisite constraint. The integrated NCA–PLS-SEM approach reveals that achieving superior purchase decision outcomes demands simultaneously adequate performance across all conditions. These findings advance theoretical understanding of high-involvement consumer decision-making and provide actionable guidance for property developers in emerging residential markets.

latest.title: Impact of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love: Evidence from the Luxury Fashion Industry in Egypt
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love in the luxury fashion industry in Egypt, building upon literature on the effect of packaging attributes as a multidimensional concept that extends beyond its protective function to include visual, functional, environmental, and experiential attributes on brand love towards luxury fashion brands. This study is theoretically grounded in the combination of the Cue Utilization Theory, Signaling Theory, and Attachment Theory to examine how packaging attributes shape consumers' emotional responses and strengthen brand love. This research employed a quantitative approach, using an online questionnaire to collect data from 440 luxury fashion consumers via River sampling, and the relationships were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics software using Multiple linear regression. Results demonstrated that packaging attributes have significant impact on brand love, with each packaging attribute contributing differently to brand love; thereby, visual, functional, and experiential packaging attributes positively impact brand love, whereas environmental packaging attributes were not a statistically significant predictor of brand love. Findings contribute evidence from the Egyptian market, offering practical implications for luxury fashion brands and marketers, highlighting packaging as a strategic tool to strengthen consumers’ emotional attachment to the brand, and supporting competitiveness in the luxury fashion market.

latest.title: Advancing Digital Banking in Albania: Trust, Financial Literacy and Regulatory Readiness in the FinTech Ecosystem
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping banking systems worldwide, yet the pace and depth of adoption remain uneven across emerging financial markets. Albania has made visible progress in electronic payments, online banking access and regulatory alignment with European digital finance standards; however, the transition from formal access to sustained digital banking adoption remains incomplete. This study examines the factors influencing digital banking and FinTech adoption in Albania, with a specific focus on consumer trust, financial literacy, perceived barriers and regulatory readiness. The paper applies a mixed-methods research design. Quantitative data were collected through a structured consumer survey with 151 respondents and analyzed through descriptive statistics and Spearman correlation analysis. Qualitative evidence was gathered through 15 semi-structured interviews with representatives from commercial banks, electronic money institutions, public institutions, regulators, sectoral organizations and academic experts. Thematic analysis was used to identify common institutional, technological and regulatory patterns. The findings show that digital banking services are widely accessible, but usage intensity remains moderate. Weekly and monthly use are more common than daily use, while trust, financial knowledge and perceived barriers significantly shape adoption patterns. The correlation analysis indicates a positive relationship between financial knowledge and digital banking use, and a negative relationship between perceived barriers and usage. latest.title: The Indonesian hedonic trap: Exploring consumer attitudes and legal risks in counterfeit luxury purchases
latest.abstract: The relationship between hedonism, the impression of legal danger, and customer attitudes about luxury fashion counterfeit products is explored in this study. Data was collected from 385 respondents in East Java, Indonesia, using multistage sampling and using structural equation modelling (SEM) analysis, with a focus on those who had previously purchased counterfeit products. The results show that consumer perceives and intention to buy for counterfeit luxury products are positively influenced by hedonism. However, this effect is considerably moderated by legal risk perception, which lowers intention to buy among individuals who are legally risk orientated. This study provides an overview of the consumption of counterfeit products by integrating legal (risk perception) and psychological (hedonism) perspectives. Further psychological and socioeconomic elements influencing the purchase of counterfeit products should be investigated in future studies. These results can be used by policymakers and brand owners to create effective consumer education initiatives and legal enforcement strategies to minimise the use of counterfeit products.

latest.title: Innovative Operation Ideas of Guangxi Agricultural Assistance Platform from a Demand-Side Orientation: A Case Study of "Mang Xiaozhong"
latest.abstract: In recent years, with the deep penetration of the digital economy into rural areas and the rapid development of agricultural e-commerce in Guangxi, the demand-side oriented agricultural assistance model has emerged as an innovative form of agricultural product circulation. In response to problems in the upward distribution of characteristic agricultural products in Guangxi—including disconnection between production and marketing, high loss in circulation links, difficulties in brand transformation, and seasonal capital shortage at the production end—the "Mang Xiaozhong" platform constructs four interconnected operation strategies: customized pre-sale, two-way exchange among production areas, rule-based trust design, and consumer-side pre-purchase crowdfunding. These strategies adapt to the industrial reality of decentralized smallholder production and staggered listing of multiple categories in Guangxi. The research shows that the demand-side oriented, asset-light third-party service model can address the practical bottlenecks of county-level agricultural assistance e-commerce in Guangxi, and has reference value for the construction of similar platforms.

latest.title: Mindful consumption in a Hyper-connected world: Digital detox as a moderator of consumer behavior
latest.abstract: The modern consumer ecosystem is portrayed by constant connectivity, algorithmic personalization, and digital action among various platforms. Although digital technologies have transmuted consumer involvements by cumulative convenience, information availability, and personalized communications, hyper-connectivity has instantaneously contributed to cognitive burden, compulsive consumption pattern, digital exhaustion, and reduced cognizant decision-making. In these circumstances, mindful consumption has surfaced as an essential context for understanding intentional and value-driven consumption behaviors. Mindful consumption lays emphasis on perception, intentional, and importance of the broader consequences of consumption decisions on individuals, society, and the environment. Contemporary research implies that consumers gradually obtain profound and stable consumption experiences that associate with psychological well-being and sustainability goals [1]. Digital detox, defined as the intended decline or temporary detachment from digital devices and social media platforms, has obtained attention as a behavioral intrusion capable of rebuilding cognitive and emotional equilibrium. Evolving evidence reveals that digital detox practices can enhance psychological well-being, lower information overload, and boost self-regulation among consumers [2]. This chapter observes the association linking mindful consumption and consumer behavior in a hyper-connected environment and intends digital detox as a moderating mechanism that controls consumer decision-making processes. Particularly, the chapter investigates how decreased digital exposure can modify impulsive purchasing trends, boost conscious assessment of consumption substitutes, and stimulate sustainable behavioral consequences

latest.title: Pengaruh Harga dan Kualitas Rasa Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian di Hayu Nyeblak Dengan Konsep Seblak Prasmanan
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh harga dan kualitas rasa terhadap keputusan pembelian konsumen pada Hayu Nyeblak yang menawarkan konsep seblak prasmanan. Konsep ini memberikan kebebasan konsumen dalam memilih topping dan tingkat kepedasan, sehingga menghasilkan pengalaman makan yang lebih personal. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan pendekatan survei korelasional. Data diperoleh dari 103 responden melalui kuesioner daring dan diolah menggunakan analisis regresi linear berganda, uji t, dan uji F. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa harga dan kualitas rasa berpengaruh signifikan baik secara parsial maupun simultan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Koefisien determinasi (R²) sebesar 0,584 menunjukkan bahwa kedua variabel menjelaskan 58,4% variasi keputusan pembelian. Temuan ini menunjukkan pentingnya kombinasi harga kompetitif dan kualitas rasa unggul dalam meningkatkan keputusan pembelian. Penelitian ini diharapkan menjadi acuan praktis bagi pelaku usaha kuliner dalam merancang strategi pemasaran yang lebih efektif.

latest.title: THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL DEPENDENCY, ONLINE IMPULSE BUYING, AND SOCIAL MEDIA ENGAGEMENT ON PURCHASE INTENTION: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF CONSUMER TRUST
latest.abstract: This study aims to investigate the relationship between digital dependency, online impulse buying tendency and purchase intention mediated by consumer trust as a mediator. The study is based on Stimulus-Organism-Response framework and trust-transfer theory; and is conducted on adult online consumers in Sindh province in Pakistan. The quantitative cross-sectional survey design is applied with the help of well-established multi-item measures and SPSS analysis. Descriptive statistics, reliability testing, Pearson correlations, hierarchical regression and mediation analysis using Hayes' PROCESS Model 4 are included in the analysis. The results show that digital dependency positively influences purchase intention, as does the tendency to buy online impulsively and social media engagement. The three predictors also significantly impact consumer trust, with social media engagement having the greatest impact on trust (β = .307, p < .001). The final regression model accounts for 37.2% of the variance in purchase intention and consumer trust significantly predicts purchase intention (β = .261, p < .001). Mediation analysis also reveals that the relationships between digital dependency and online impulse buying tendency, social media engagement and purchase intention are mediated in part by consumer trust. Social media engagement has the highest mediation effect in terms of indirect effects, mediated by consumer trust (indirect effect = .091, 95% CI [.057, .130]). Overall, the findings reflect the critical role of consumer trust in increasing their online purchasing intentions among online consumers in Sindh based on their digital engagement and online purchasing tendency.

latest.title: Peran Kredibilitas Ulasan Online dan Persepsi Risiko Kinerja Produk Dalam Membentuk Niat Beli Ulang melalui Citra Toko Online
latest.venue: MENAWAN Jurnal Riset dan Publikasi Ilmu Ekonomi
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationships of online review credibility and perceived product performance risk with repurchase intention through online store image in the context of EMC Official, a bookstore on Shopee. A quantitative explanatory survey simulation with a cross-sectional and nonexperimental design was used. Four hundred synthetic observations containing 16 items on a seven-point Likert scale were generated computationally; no field survey was conducted. The model was estimated using a custom Mode A PLS implementation with path weighting in Python and 10,000 bootstrap samples. All indicators met the specified measurement criteria in the synthetic dataset. Review credibility was positively related to store image (β = 0.375) and repurchase intention (β = 0.227). Product performance risk was negatively related to store image (β = −0.263), while its direct relationship with repurchase intention was not significant (β = 0.002; p = 0.963). Store image was positively related to repurchase intention (β = 0.478). The indirect effect of credibility through store image was 0.179, indicating complementary mediation. The indirect effect of risk was −0.126, indicating indirect-only mediation. Six of seven hypotheses were supported in the simulation. The model explained 24.98% of the variation in store image and 37.20% in repurchase intention. The study demonstrates how store image can statistically connect information and risk assessments with intentions to purchase again. The results depend on the data-generating assumptions and do not constitute empirical evidence about EMC Official customers. Validation using actual customers and subsequent transaction records is required.

latest.title: Coordinating Individual and System Change in the Marketing System: The TISI Framework for a Circular Plastics Economy
latest.abstract: Single-use plastics (SUPs) remain a major obstacle to a circular plastics economy. Interventions to reduce them have typically pursued either system-level (S-level) measures or individual-level (I-level) behaviour change campaigns, and participatory work has tended to engage consumers or stakeholders at only one of these levels. Building on macromarketing's systems perspective and on macro-social marketing, we develop the Theory-Individual-System-Intervention (TISI) framework, which specifies how marketing can use consumer insight, organised through the COM-B model, to coordinate change across the micro, meso and macro levels of the plastics marketing system. The framework distinguishes consumers’ market role at the I-level (purchase, use, return and refill) from their citizen role at the S-level (acceptance, perceived fairness, willingness to comply and collective support). We validate its four steps empirically with SUP milk packaging in New Zealand, drawing on 20 consumer interviews and a best-worst scaling survey of 400 consumers. Most barriers consumers reported were opportunity constraints rooted in the marketing system, and respondents preferred incentives and regulation to information-only approaches. The study offers macromarketing an operational account of how marketing can sequence consumer-informed action across levels, and offers practitioners a route to SUP reduction that does not place the burden on consumers alone.

latest.title: The Impact of Digital Marketing on Impulse Buying and Post-Purchase Dissonance
latest.venue: Murray State's Digital Commons (Murray State University)
latest.abstract: Modern digital marketing strategies often have the upper hand when it comes to psychological triggers, such as flash sale countdowns, promotional pop-up ads, and one-click checkouts, to encourage immediate, unplanned purchases. Extending Festinger’s (1957) Cognitive Dissonance Theory to consumer behavior as conceptualized by Sweeney et al. (2000), this study examines how exposure to digital marketing stimuli and individual impulsivity levels influence post-purchase cognitive dissonance. Specifically, this study investigates whether more intense marketing triggers elicit greater levels of post-purchase dissonance and whether an individual’s baseline impulsivity acts as a key predictor of psychological discomfort. Sixty undergraduate students (N = 60) from Murray State University’s Department of Psychology will be recruited through the SONA system. Participants will complete a single-session online study with three parts. First, participants will be randomly assigned to low and high digital marketing stimuli conditions and will complete a simulated purchasing task where they must choose between two different housing options. Immediately following the task, participants will complete the Multidimensional Cognitive Dissonance Scale (Sweeney et al., 2000) to measure their post-purchase dissonance. Finally, participants will complete the Impulse Buying Tendency Scale (IBTS; Verplanken & Herabadi, 2001) to evaluate cognitive and affective trait impulsivity as a predictor of dissonance scores. Data collection is actively in progress following Institutional Review Board approval. latest.title: Customer Focus Program (CFP) in a Regulation-Constrained Category: A Field-Based Qualitative Study of Distribution and Merchandising Execution in India's Organized Cigarette Trade
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose: In categories where mass advertising and open promotion are legally prohibited, the sales and distribution system becomes the main route through which a firm can express customer orientation. This paper examines how a Customer Focus Program (CFC) operates at the point of sale in the cigarette sales and distribution network of a large Indian fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) organisation. Design/methodology/approach: The study is a descriptive, qualitative, field-observation-based case study conducted over a two-month period (15 May to 15 July 2026) in the Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) territory of Maharashtra. Observations were recorded during accompanied market visits across convenience, grocery, wholesale, sub-wholesale, stockist, moped and van direct-selling channels, using a four-field recording format (objective, activity observed, practical observation, relevance to customer focus). Observations were mapped to an Availability–Visibility–Freshness (AVF) framework and to an eight-step CFC field-execution flow. Findings: Four findings emerge. (1) Availability is produced by layered, complementary coverage formats rather than by any single actor. (2) Effective execution must be segment-aware and margin-aware, because retailers' stocking and promotion choices respond jointly to product segment and trade pricing structure. (3) Merchandising and planogram discipline is the primary visibility lever when above-the-line promotion is unavailable. (4) The salesman–retailer relationship is the mechanism that sustains the program. Originality/value: The paper offers a field-grounded account of customer orientation as enacted at the last mile in a heavily regulated category, an area where the marketing-channels and customer-orientation literatures rarely meet. latest.title: FACTORS AFFECTING THE SELECTED BRANDS OF RICE IN AN- NAJAF ALASHRAF PRONINCE FOR THE AGRICULTURAL SEASON 2017
The Influence of Membership Programs and Application Ease of Use on Consumer Purchasing Decisions in Modern Retail
latest.venue: International Journal of Integrated Science and Technology
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of membership programs and application ease of use on consumer purchasing decisions in modern retail. The subjects of this study were consumers using the membership application at Indomaret in Tangerang. A quantitative approach was employed using purposive sampling with 100 respondents. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares (PLS) with SmartPLS version 4.1.1.8. The results indicate that, partially, the membership program does not have a significant effect on consumer purchasing decisions, while application ease of use has a positive and significant effect. These findings indicate that although membership provides various benefits, consumers may consider other factors such as price, needs, store location, product quality, and direct promotions when making purchases. Meanwhile, an application that is easy to learn, understand, operate, flexible, and practical can facilitate the purchasing process and support consumer purchasing decisions.

latest.title: LOW-PURCHASE LONG-STAY BEHAVIOUR AT ZUS COFFEE: CROWDING, FAIRNESS AND REVISIT INTENTION
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: This study examines how low-purchase long-stay behaviour influences customer experience in urban coffee chains, using ZUS Coffee customers in Malaysia as the research context. As cafés increasingly function as informal work, study and social spaces, customers who purchase minimally but occupy seats for extended periods may affect other customers’ perceptions of crowding, service fairness, satisfaction and revisit intention. Drawing on servicescape, perceived crowding and service fairness perspectives, this study develops a conceptual model linking low-purchase long-stay behaviour to perceived crowding, perceived service fairness, customer satisfaction and revisit intention. A quantitative survey design is proposed among ZUS Coffee customers who have recently visited physical outlets in Malaysia. The study contributes to consumer behaviour and service management literature by examining café space consumption as part of the customer experience. The findings are expected to provide practical implications for coffee chain operators in managing seating, customer comfort and fairness without weakening the café’s role as a flexible third place.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: The Influence of TikTok Social media marketing and Service Quality on Purchase Decisions at De.u Coffee Dago
latest.abstract: The growth of coffee shop businesses in Indonesia shows a significant trend in line with the lifestyle changes of urban communities, where coffee shops have increasingly become places for socializing, working, or simply relaxing. One widely used strategy is social media marketing, particularly through TikTok, which is currently popular across various demographics. This study aims to examine the influence of TikTok social media marketing and service quality on consumer purchase decisions at De.u Coffee Dago. The research method employed is quantitative, with data collected through questionnaires distributed to 100 respondents. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression tests. The results indicate that TikTok social media marketing has a significant effect on purchase decisions with a significance value of 0.000 (<0.05). Similarly, service quality also has a significant effect on purchase decisions with a significance value of 0.000 (<0.05). Simultaneously, both independent variables contribute 63.9% to purchase decisions, while the remaining 36.1% is influenced by other factors outside this study. These findings highlight the importance of digital marketing strategies through TikTok and the implementation of optimal service quality in enhancing consumer purchase interest. The benefits of this research not only provide academic insights into consumer behavior but also serve as a practical reference for coffee shop businesses in designing effective marketing strategies and maintaining service quality to increase consumer loyalty.

latest.title: Analyzing the Impact of Product Quality, Brand Image, and Location on Consumer Purchase Decisions: Evidence from Tepian Kopi Semarang, Indonesia
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyse the influence of product quality, brand image, and location on consumer purchase decisions at Tepian Kopi Coffee Shop in Semarang, Indonesia. A quantitative survey approach was employed, with 103 respondents selected through purposive sampling based on the criteria of being at least 17 years old and having made a purchase within the previous six months. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analysed using multiple linear regression with SPSS version 26. The results indicate that product quality (t = 2.167; sig. = 0.033), brand image (t = 2.868; sig. = 0.005), and location (t = 4.852; sig. = 0.000) all have a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions. Location contributes the strongest relative effect, with a standardised beta coefficient of 0.426, compared to brand image (0.250) and product quality (0.199). The F-test confirms that the three variables simultaneously influence purchase decisions (F = 44.023; sig. = 0.000), while the adjusted R² of 0.559 indicates that 55.9% of the variance in purchase decisions is explained by the model. These findings suggest that location advantages serve as the most immediate source of competitive advantage for local coffee shops competing against larger chains. Managers are advised to prioritise location enhancement, brand experience consistency, and product quality reinforcement, while future research may incorporate additional variables such as price, promotion, and store atmosphere.

latest.title: Consumer Protection in Islamic Law: A Thematic Hadith Analysis of Khiyar and Its Contextualization in the Digital Era
latest.venue: MURAJA AH Journal of Islamic Studies
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze hadiths on khiyar as a basis for consumer protection in Islamic law and examine their relevance to digital transactions. The study employs a normative legal method with a descriptive-analytical qualitative approach through library research. The data are drawn from hadiths on khiyar in hadith collections and relevant fiqh literature. The analysis involves tracing hadith sources (takhrij), examining their wording and key vocabulary (mufradat al-hadith), and analyzing the concepts and types of khiyar in Islamic commercial jurisprudence (fiqh muamalah). The findings show that the hadiths reported in Sahih al-Bukhari No. 2112 and Sahih Muslim No. 1531 explain the right of choice in sales transactions and the circumstances under which a contract becomes binding. Fiqh literature also reveals differences among scholars regarding the rules governing khiyar, particularly its time limits and application. In the digital context, the principles of khiyar are conceptually relevant to order cancellation features and return policies, particularly in promoting transparency, fairness, and the protection of consumer rights. However, their application requires consideration of the characteristics of digital transactions, fiqh principles, and applicable regulations. This study concludes that khiyar can serve as a normative foundation for examining digital consumer protection from the perspective of Islamic law.

latest.title: Influence of Perceived Brand Image on Students’ Choice of Health and Allied Sciences Colleges in Tanzania: A Case of Selected Colleges in Mwanza City
latest.venue: East African Journal of Business and Economics
latest.abstract: The study investigated the influence of perceived brand image on students' choice of health and allied sciences colleges in Tanzania, focusing on selected colleges in Mwanza City. The study was guided by Brand Equity Theory to examine the influence of brand awareness, perceived quality, and brand association on students’ choice. A quantitative approach and cross-sectional design were used. The study targeted 1,993 undergraduate students, of whom 333 respondents were selected through stratified random sampling. A total of 320 questionnaires were successfully returned and analysed using SPSS version 26. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression analysis were employed to analyse quantitative data. The findings showed that perceived brand image had a positive and statistically significant influence on students’ choice of Health and Allied Sciences Colleges. Perceived quality had the strongest positive effect, with β = 0.352 and p = 0.001. Brand awareness had a positive significant effect on students’ choice, with β = 0.286 and p = 0.000. Brand association also had a positive significant effect, with β = 0.271 and p = 0.000. The model explained 62.3% of the variation in students’ choice, as shown by R Square = 0.623. The study concluded that students’ choice of Health and Allied Sciences Colleges was influenced by institutional awareness, perceived quality, and association. The study recommended that Health and Allied Sciences Colleges should strengthen institutional visibility, improve academic and clinical training quality, and build strong positive associations to attract students and strengthen marketing strategies.

latest.title: How Collaborative Marketing Communications and Aesthetic Design Influence Purchase Intention: The Sequential Mediating Roles of Nostalgic Emotion and Brand Love
latest.abstract: This study investigates how aesthetic design and collaborative marketing shape consumer purchase intention through emotional and relational mechanisms in an emerging market setting. Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework, the study develops and tests a moderated serial mediation model in which nostalgic emotion and brand love explain how marketing stimuli translate into behavioral outcomes. Data were collected from 326 Generation Y female consumers in Thailand and analyzed using structural equation modeling and conditional process analysis. The findings reveal that both aesthetic design and collaborative marketing positively influence nostalgic emotion, which subsequently strengthens brand love and enhances purchase intention. Brand love further emerges as a significant predictor of purchase intention, highlighting the importance of emotional attachment in consumer decision-making. Furthermore, aesthetic sensory consumption was found to moderate selected relationships within the proposed model rather than all structural paths, indicating that its influence is context dependent. However, although the sequential indirect effects through nostalgic emotion and brand love were significant at specific levels of aesthetic sensory consumption, pairwise comparisons revealed no significant differences across these levels. Thus, the hypothesized moderated sequential indirect effects were not supported. This study extends promotion management research by explaining how aesthetic design and collaborative marketing function as complementary promotional mechanisms that stimulate nostalgic emotion, strengthen brand love, and enhance purchase intention, while identifying aesthetic sensory consumption as a selective boundary condition rather than a uniform moderator

latest.title: Discursive Institutional Work and the Social Control of Dangerous Objects
latest.abstract: Abstract Across societies and over time, the social control of objects deemed “dangerous”—i.e., as threats to public order, morality, or physical and psychological well-being—varies, from regulation to prohibition, with implications for responsibility, potential harm, and affected communities. Drawing on U.S. Congressional hearings on the issue of cannabis regulation and prohibition (1906–1951), we examine how shifts in social control track changing configurations of discursive institutional work. Our work demonstrates how configurations of rationalization, moralization, and syncretization shaped the meaning of cannabis as a dangerous object: rationalization calculates the risk, supporting calibrated regulation; moralization absolutizes the danger, promoting prohibition; and syncretization balances these two. We refer to this reciprocal dynamic as an epistemic ratchet, whereby rationalization and moralization each weaken the epistemic foundations of the alternative regime, making movement between regulation and prohibition difficult in either direction. Our study makes three contributions: (a) it extends the organizing-of-risk account of how danger is rendered governable to the form and reversibility of control; (b) it adds to research on discursive institutional work by identifying epistemology, complexity, and responsibility as the object-level qualities through which discourse becomes consequential for governance; and (c) it contributes to debates on responsibility, ethics, and harm by showing how the discursive redistribution of responsibility shapes the scope and coerciveness of control.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: The Influence of Price, Promotion, Product Differentiation and Product Conformity with Sharia Values on Customer Interest in Gold Installments in Pinrang Regency, South Sulawesi Province
latest.venue: GoodWill Journal of Economics Management and Accounting
latest.abstract: Public interest in gold installment products has increased because they are perceived as accessible, secure, and consistent with Islamic principles. However, the factors that influence customers’ interest in gold installment products, particularly in the context of Islamic financial institutions in Pinrang Regency, require further examination. This study aimed to analyze the effects of price, promotion, product differentiation, and product conformity with Islamic values on customers’ interest in gold installment products, both individually and simultaneously. A quantitative associative research design was employed. Primary data were collected through questionnaires from 100 respondents in Pinrang Regency who were familiar with or had used gold installment products, selected using purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression, partial significance tests, simultaneous significance tests, and the coefficient of determination with the assistance of SPSS. The findings showed that price and product conformity with Islamic values had positive and significant effects on customers’ interest in gold installment products. Promotion and product differentiation also contributed positively to increasing customer interest. Simultaneously, price, promotion, product differentiation, and product conformity with Islamic values had a positive and significant effect on customer interest. These findings indicate that appropriate marketing strategies combined with consistent adherence to Islamic principles are important for increasing public interest in gold installment products. The study contributes practical insights for Islamic financial institutions in developing competitive and Sharia-compliant mar

latest.title: Responsible communication in sustainable fashion: a mixed-methods neuromarketing study of young consumers
latest.abstract: Sustainable fashion claims are communicated through labels, visual cues, traceability signals, and brand narratives that shape how consumers interpret responsibility, credibility, and product value. Their effectiveness is nevertheless constrained when sustainability information competes with aesthetic and functional product cues or when claims are perceived as vague or weakly substantiated. This study examines how young consumers process sustainable fashion claims and how visual attention, emotional response, and perceived credibility contribute to that process. Using a mixed-methods neuromarketing design, the study combines a pretest (N = 22), face-coding (N = 30), eye-tracking (N = 31), and focus groups (N = 20) with consumers aged 18–25 in Bogotá, Colombia. Each component was analysed at the method-specific level and the findings were subsequently integrated through triangulation. Results show that product and perceptual cues capture initial attention, whereas sustainability information receives greater engagement when it is visually integrated and connected to functional product value. Facial-expression analysis indicates that sadness was the most prominent average emotional category across the stimuli examined. Qualitative evidence further suggests that, within this study, socially framed sustainability messages were perceived as more concrete and emotionally accessible than more abstract environmental claims. Across methods, claim credibility and perceived congruence with the product emerged as important conditions in the interpretation of sustainability communication. By integrating attentional, affective, and interpretive evidence, the study advances understanding of how sustainability claims are processed without assuming direct effects on purchase behaviour. T

latest.title: From Free to Paid: Public Attitude Change and Mechanism Evidence around Doubao's Charging Announcement
latest.abstract: As generative AI moves from free access to paid subscription, how charging shapes public attitude bears on platform commercialization. Taking Doubao's monthly subscription as the setting, this paper builds a dual-path framework of “product experience - price perception”. Using the announcement date (May 4, 2026) as the breakpoint, we collect public Weibo discussions from 30 days before to 30 days after it (2-day periods; the 14 days on each side form the main window), measure attitude with aspect-based sentiment analysis, and test changes at the breakpoint by regression discontinuity in time. Negative evaluation is robust in direction for Payment Willingness (τ = +0.751, p < 0.001) and Corporate Brand (τ = +0.647, p = 0.011), but rests on only 27 and 7 pre-breakpoint texts, so the magnitudes are read as direction only. The negative share for Price & Charging shows no significant increase (τ = -0.161, p = 0.123), so the price-fairness path is not supported. The difference between the two aspect jumps is -0.532 (clustered SE 0.437, p = 0.245), opposite to expectation and underpowered given the small pre-breakpoint sample; we report only that no larger negative change was found for the price path than for the feature path. The overall negative share rises by 0.317 (p = 0.041) but depends on a pre-breakpoint period with 3 relevant texts and falls to 0.043 (p = 0.517) without it, so it is not robustly supported. The conclusions are limited to a marked change in attitude, with no persistent shift and no strict causal claim.

latest.title: The impact of ai recommendation systems on impulsive buying behaviour in electronic marketplaces: The mediating moderating role of fear of missing out
latest.venue: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence has spread rapidly across e-commerce, and in doing so it has reshaped how consumers reach purchase decisions. Scholarship to date concentrates mainly on what shoppers gain from algorithmic recommenders, whereas far fewer studies ask whether such systems also push buyers toward unplanned spending. The present work therefore tests how perceived attributes of AI recommendation engines relate to impulsive buying, treating fear of missing out (FOMO) simultaneously as an intervening variable and as a boundary condition. Survey evidence was gathered from 823 Vietnamese shoppers who regularly transact on AI-enabled marketplaces. Results show impulsive purchasing rising together with perceived AI authority, perceived task complexity, and with perceived personalization. FOMO carries a significant portion of each effect and, at the same time, amplifies its magnitude. These outcomes ground several managerial recommendations for platforms seeking to reconcile recommender deployment with responsible consumer conduct.

latest.title: BEYOND THE SCROLL: HOW MARKETING TURNS ATTENTION INTO TRUST
latest.abstract: The article examines how consumer attention on social media can be transformed into brand trust, laying the groundwork for lasting customer relationships. Amid information overload and competition for users’ attention, it explores marketing communication approaches that combine engaging content, practical value, and relevance to audience expectations. The article aims to explain how content and consistent consumer interaction contribute to brand trust and the transition from initial interest to a purchase decision.Particular attention is paid to the content and communication factors that sustain audience interest after the first encounter with a brand’s post. These include useful and credible messages, transparent offers, consistency between brand promises and customer experience, and timely responses to questions and feedback. The article discusses the role of social proof, including reviews, recommendations, and user-generated content, in reducing uncertainty when choosing products or services. It also stresses the need to assess such materials critically and avoid manipulative communication practices.The article further considers approaches to evaluating marketing communication effectiveness. It distinguishes reach and engagement metrics from indicators related to inquiries, conversions, repeat purchases, and customer retention. Views and reactions alone provide insufficient grounds for conclusions about trust or commercial outcomes. The practical value of the article lies in outlining principles for content creation and customer interaction that support stronger brand–consumer relationships. This approach connects the immediate goal of attracting attention with the longer-term objective of developing customer loyalty through credible communication and consistent del

Determinants of Sustainable Fast Fashion Purchase Intention Among Generation Z Consumers
latest.venue: Cureus Journal of Business and Economics.
latest.abstract: The increasing environmental concerns associated with the fast fashion industry have intensified the need to understand the factors that encourage sustainable consumption, particularly among Generation Z, one of the largest and most influential consumer segments.This study examines the determinants of purchase intention towards sustainable fast fashion by investigating the effects of sustainability awareness, perceived green value, social influence, fashion involvement, and sustainability attitude.Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behaviour and the Value-Attitude-Behaviour framework, a conceptual model was developed and empirically tested using survey data collected from 1,000 Generation Z consumers in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, India.The measurement model was validated through reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and confirmatory factor analysis, while the proposed hypotheses were tested using structural equation modelling with the diagonally weighted least squares estimation method.The findings reveal that all five constructs significantly and positively influence purchase intention towards sustainable fast fashion.Sustainability attitude emerged as the strongest predictor (β = 0.351), followed by social influence (β = 0.303), sustainability awareness (β = 0.280), green perceived value (β = 0.252), and fashion involvement (β = 0.222).The model demonstrated excellent goodness of fit (comparative fit index = 0.991; Tucker-Lewis index = 0.989; root mean square error of approximation = 0.031), confirming the robustness of the proposed framework.The study contributes to the sustainable fashion literature by integrating cognitive, social, evaluative, and attitudinal factors into a comprehensive behavioural model that explains the transition from sustainabi

latest.title: The role of crowding and decision comfort during sales periods
latest.abstract: Purpose Sales periods simultaneously attract consumers through price reductions and trigger avoidance behaviors: a paradox this study addresses by examining decision comfort as a potential mediator of the effects of human and spatial crowding on visit postponement and store-switching. Gender is also examined as a moderator of these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative approach was adopted, with data collected from 378 consumers in France during official sales periods across several retail locations. The conceptual model was tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine relationships among perceived crowding, decision comfort, visit postponement, and store-switching. Multi-group analysis assessed gender differences. Findings Both human and spatial crowding were negatively associated with decision comfort. Lower decision comfort was associated with higher levels of visit postponement and, less robustly, with store-switching. The indirect effect of spatial crowding on visit postponement through decision comfort was supported; the indirect effects of human crowding on both avoidance behaviors were also supported but modest in magnitude, whereas the indirect effect of spatial crowding on store-switching was not supported. Gender differences were detected in the crowding–decision comfort relationships, whereas no gender differences were detected in the decision comfort–avoidance paths. Originality/value This research contributes to the marketing literature by showing that the mediating role of decision comfort depends on the form of crowding and the avoidance response considered. It extends the application of decision comfort as an emerging construct in the retail context, offering new insights into how crowding shapes consumer decision-makin

latest.title: Ex-Ante Regulation of Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises: A Legal Appraisal of India's Draft Digital Competition Bill vs. the EU's Digital Markets Act
latest.venue: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
latest.abstract: As platform economies grow increasingly concentrated, competition law struggles to keep pace with the emergence of ‘Big Tech’ companies. Traditional ex-post enforcement measures are increasingly seen by regulators worldwide as too slow. This paper presents a legal appraisal of India’s draft Digital Competition Bill, focusing on its proposals for identifying Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises within the country’s digital market, and compares it with the European Union’s Digital Markets Act, 2022. Both frameworks adopt a proactive, forward-looking approach to controlling anti-competitive conduct by major technology firms. Still, the analysis reveals significant differences between the two in the designation of companies, the obligations imposed on them, and the rules of enforcement, differences that reflect distinct economic priorities. The European Union framework targets gatekeepers, that is, large technology platforms that control crucial online services, on the basis of their market position and the risk of anti-competitive behaviour, whereas India’s Digital Competition Bill focuses on preventing broader harms to the digital ecosystem. The paper suggests that although the Competition Act can deal effectively with unfair practices, a more flexible, rule-based regulatory framework would better equip authorities to handle market unpredictability, legal challenges and procedural delays, ultimately fostering fairer competition. It concludes with a series of recommendations aimed at strengthening the design of India’s digital competition framework.

latest.title: 云南咖啡商标与地理标志协同机制
latest.abstract: 为明确云南咖啡面向东南亚市场时企业商标与地理标志协同运用的条件，基于声誉、集体行动和全球价值链治理理论，采用整合性综述方法，对消费者评价、质量行为及收益分配证据进行比较与主题归纳。研究表明，标识协同包括信息互补与治理互补，分别取决于新增产地信息的购买相关性及共同规范与企业责任的衔接；消费者估价、交易成交和生产者净回报处于不同环节，组织服务、渠道控制与成本分担影响收益传递。据此提出境外权利衔接、质量责任落实、市场信息转化和成本收益协调四项条件及相应研究命题。云南咖啡应将标识运用落实到具体交易，在原料采购中衔接验收与结算，在终端销售中检验信息增量，在跨境加工中明确用标权限与责任。

latest.title: To What Extent Does the Layout of a Departmental Store Affect Consumer Decision Fatigue?
latest.venue: Reinvention an International Journal of Undergraduate Research
latest.abstract: A departmental store layout and product placement shape the consumer decision-making process. This paper begins by charting the psychological flow of decision making and identifying the critical points that lead to decision fatigue, a cognitive stage where repeated or complex choices exhaust mental resources and lead to suboptimal decisions. This paper further aims to provide a nuanced understanding of how the retail environment of a department store influences consumer behaviour and cognitive load. Three types of store layouts are analysed: free form, grid and racetrack. A free-form layout allows the consumer to explore products and integrates various departments together for higher sales; this configuration causes comparatively high levels of decision fatigue among consumers as it encourages browsing and they are left to navigate products by themselves. A grid layout eases the navigation process by arranging aisles in a parallel structure. However, retailers can achieve the best shopping experience with low levels of decision fatigue among shoppers by implementing a racetrack layout, which not only reduces the need for consumers to decide their path but also reduces cognitive overload by guiding the consumer along one main aisle.

latest.title: Comparative Financial and Strategic Analysis of Selected Companies in the Indian Auto (Four-Wheeler) Sector
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: The Indian four-wheeler automobile sector is among the largest in the world and is being reshaped by sport utility vehicle (SUV) demand, electrification, connected technologies and tighter regulation. This study presents a comparative financial and strategic analysis of five leading listed companies: Maruti Suzuki India Limited, Mahindra & Mahindra Limited, Hyundai Motor India Limited, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Ashok Leyland Limited. A descriptive, secondary-data research design was adopted. Company reports, investor presentations, exchange filings, industry publications and government sources were used to build company profiles and to compute and compare revenue, net profit, market capitalisation, earnings per share, return on equity, return on capital employed, debt–equity ratio, current ratio, net profit margin and five-year passenger vehicle market share. Strategic tools, namely PESTEL, Porter’s Five Forces and SWOT analysis, were used to interpret the financial evidence. The results show that Maruti Suzuki combines market leadership, the highest market valuation among the five firms, negligible debt and a strong distribution network, although its passenger vehicle share has eased from 47% to about 41% over five years. Mahindra & Mahindra records the largest revenue and net profit among the firms with comparable data and the fastest share gain, rising from 7% to 14%. Hyundai Motor India delivers the highest return on capital employed (38.4%) with very low leverage, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles leads electric mobility but shows weak liquidity and capital-efficiency indicators. Ashok Leyland is a commercial vehicle specialist with the highest leverage in the sample. The study concludes that scale, balance-sheet strength and portfolio fit with the SUV

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Hotel certifications are not only crucial for environmental sustainability, but also serve as

hot.title: Customer data access and fintech entry: Early evidence from open banking
hot.abstract: Open banking (OB) empowers bank customers to share their financial transaction data with fintechs and other banks. New cross-country data shows 49 countries adopted OB policies, privacy preferences predict policy adoption, and adoption spurs fintech entry. UK microdata shows that OB enables: (i) consumers to access both financial advice and credit; (ii) SMEs to establish new lending relationships. In a calibrated model, OB universally improves welfare through entry and product improvements when used for advice. When used for credit, OB promotes entry and competition by reducing adverse selection, but higher prices for costlier or privacy-conscious consumers partially offset these benefits.

hot.title: Exploring the role of health consciousness and environmental awareness in purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods: an extended TPB model
hot.abstract: Background: With the increasing rise of green consumption concepts, consumers are becoming more concerned with the health and environmental attributes of products. However, research on purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods remains relatively limited, particularly regarding the specific impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness. There is a clear gap in the literature addressing these factors. Method: Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study constructs a relationship model between health consciousness, environmental awareness, attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods. A total of 372 valid survey samples were collected, and data analysis was performed using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS 28.0 software to validate the theoretical model and research hypotheses. Results: Structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis reveals that all hypotheses are significantly supported, and the model demonstrates good fit. Mediation effect analysis further reveals the impact of health consciousness and environmental awareness on purchase intentions, indicating that they influence consumer intentions indirectly through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. Conclusion: Health consciousness and environmental awareness not only significantly affect consumers' purchase intentions for green-packaged organic foods through direct paths but also have important indirect effects through attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. This study provides a new perspective for the theoretical development of green consumer behavior and offers valuable practical insights for businesses and policymakers in promoting green consumption and sustainable products.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Recommendations and Functional Food Purchases: Understanding Consumer Decision-Making
hot.abstract: Amid rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), personalized recommendation systems have become a key factor shaping consumer decision-making in functional food purchases. However, the influence of AI recommendation characteristics on purchase intention, particularly the underlying mediating mechanisms, remains underexplored. This study aims to investigate how AI recommendation features (personalization and transparency), along with functional food attributes (perceived health benefits and perceived naturalness), influence purchase intention through the mediating roles of perceived packaging and perceived value. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, data were collected via a structured questionnaire survey, and structural equation modeling was employed for hypothesis testing and model validation. The results indicate that AI recommendation personalization significantly enhances purchase intention both directly and indirectly, while transparency influences purchase intention only through perceived value, emphasizing its role in fostering trust rather than directly driving purchasing behavior. Additionally, perceived health benefits positively influence purchase intention both directly and through mediation, whereas perceived naturalness affects purchase intention only indirectly via perceived value. These findings contribute to consumer behavior research by elucidating psychological mechanisms underlying AI-driven purchase decisions while also providing insights for functional food marketers on how to effectively integrate AI recommendation systems to enhance consumer engagement.

hot.title: A scoping review and expert consensus on digital determinants of health
hot.venue: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
hot.abstract: Objective: To map how social, commercial, political and digital determinants of health have changed or emerged during the recent digital transformation of society and to identify priority areas for policy action. Methods: We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase and Web of Science on 24 September 2023, to identify eligible reviews published in 2018 and later. To ensure we included the most recent literature, we supplemented our review with non-systematic searches in PubMed® and Google Scholar, along with records identified by subject matter experts. Using thematic analysis, we clustered the extracted data into five societal domains affected by digitalization. The clustering also informed a novel framework, which the authors and contributors reviewed for comprehensiveness and accuracy. Using a two-round consensus process, we rated the identified determinants into high, moderate and low urgency for policy actions. Findings: We identified 13 804 records, of which 204 met the inclusion criteria. A total of 127 health determinants were found to have emerged or changed during the digital transformation of society (37 digital, 33 social, 33 commercial and economic and 24 political determinants). Of these, 30 determinants (23.6%) were considered particularly urgent for policy action. Conclusion: This review offers a comprehensive overview of health determinants across digital, social, commercial and economic, and political domains, highlighting how policy decisions, individual behaviours and broader factors influence health by digitalization. The findings deepen our understanding of how health outcomes manifest within a digital ecosystem and inform strategies for addressing the complex and evolving networks of health determinants.
