latest.title: Identifying and Prioritizing the Components of Circular Accounting: A Qualitative Study Based on Systematic Content Analysis
latest.abstract: The expansion of the circular economy has increased the need to transform accounting systems and identify the components required to support decision-making and reporting related to efficient resource utilization, waste reduction, and environmental performance. Despite the growing body of research on circular accounting, its constituent components and dimensions have been addressed in a fragmented manner across different studies, highlighting the need to identify and integrate these components. The present study aimed to identify, categorize, and prioritize the components of circular accounting. In terms of purpose, the study was applied, and in terms of methodology, it employed a qualitative, descriptive–analytical approach. To collect the data, scientific publications and texts related to circular accounting, the circular economy, sustainability, environmental accounting, and material flow management were systematically reviewed. During the analytical stage, conventional qualitative content analysis was used to extract relevant concepts from the texts, code them, and organize them into categories and subcomponents based on conceptual similarity. Through the process of analyzing and integrating the codes, three main categories were identified: dynamic capabilities of circular accounting, material flows in the circular economy, and institutional–environmental drivers and barriers. Subsequently, 12 subcomponents were extracted and classified: flexibility and reconfiguration; innovation and technology; learning and knowledge development; interaction and accountability; efficient material management and consumption; life cycle and environmental traceability; supply chain and resource optimization; policymakers and regulations; infrastructure and information technology; cul

latest.title: Designing and Explaining an Entrepreneurship Model for Artificial Intelligence–Based Businesses
latest.venue: Journal of Management and Business Solutions
latest.abstract: The primary objective of the present study was to design and explain an entrepreneurship model for artificial intelligence–based businesses, with a focus on the information and communications technology and computer software industries in knowledge-based companies located in Tehran Province. In terms of purpose, the study was applied, and in terms of approach, it was a qualitative study employing a sequential exploratory design. In the qualitative phase, grounded theory was applied using the systematic approach to identify and conceptualize the dimensions, components, and relationships among the variables affecting AI-based entrepreneurship. The qualitative research field consisted of senior and middle managers, specialists, experts, and experienced employees working in the information and communications technology and computer software industries of knowledge-based companies in Tehran Province. Participants were selected through purposive sampling, which continued until theoretical saturation was reached. Qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using MAXQDA 2024. To enhance the credibility and trustworthiness of the data, triangulation and Lincoln and Guba’s criteria, including credibility, transferability, dependability, and confirmability, were employed. The findings indicated that the entrepreneurship model for AI-based businesses consists of an interconnected set of causal conditions, contextual conditions, intervening conditions, strategies, and consequences. The causal conditions included factors such as market needs and technological gaps, entrepreneurial opportunity recognition, and customers’ digital preferences, all of which played a fundamental role in the formation of AI-based entrepreneurship. latest.title: Pengaruh Working Capital Turnover dan Total Asset Turnover terhadap Profitabilitas melalui Capital Structure sebagai Variabel Intervening pada Sektor Aneka Industri yang Terdaftar di BEI
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of Working capital turnover (WCT) and Total asset turnover (TATO) on profitability through capital structure as an intervening variable in the miscellaneous industry sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the period 2022–2024. The research employs a quantitative approach with an associative descriptive design. The sampling technique used is purposive sampling, yielding 35 companies as samples with 105 observation units over three years. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression and path analysis assisted by IBM SPSS version 26. The results indicate that Working capital turnover has a negative significant effect on capital structure and Total asset turnover has a negative significant effect on capital structure , working capital turnover has a positive significant effect on profitability whereas Total asset turnover does not significantly affect profitability and Capital structure has no significant effect on profitability. Furthermore, capital structure is unable to mediate the effect of either Working capital turnover or Total asset turnover on profitability. These findings suggest that the direct effect of asset utilization on profitability is stronger than the indirect effect through capital structure.

latest.title: Surviving Financial Shocks: Cash Flow Volatility and Corporate Resilience in Indonesia
latest.abstract: This study examines the effects of financial resilience and cash flow volatility on financial performance, measured by Return on Assets (ROA), among manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024. Using a quantitative approach, the study analyzes 220 firm-year observations through multiple linear regression. The results show that financial resilience has a positive and significant effect on financial performance, while cash flow volatility has a negative and significant effect. Simultaneously, both variables significantly affect financial performance. These findings indicate that stronger financial resilience enables firms to maintain operational continuity and financial flexibility, whereas higher cash flow volatility increases liquidity uncertainty and constrains financial management. Consistent with Agency Theory, effective management of financial resources and cash flows can reduce managerial inefficiencies and agency conflicts, thereby supporting improved financial performance.

latest.title: Parasocial Interaction and Perceived Value as Determinants of Intention to Buy Made-in-Thailand Products through Live- Streaming Personal Shoppers
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This research investigates the rising trend of live shopping and jasa titipan (jastip) in Southeast Asian digital commerce, focusing on the growing popularity of Made in Thailand products among Indonesian consumers. Livestream commerce has changed consumer behaviour by offering immediacy, interactivity, and immersive digital experiences that lessen psychological distance between sellers and buyers. In Indonesia, live personal shopper sessions have become a key method for cross-border purchases of Thai cosmetics, fashion items, herbal supplements, and packaged foods, which are widely viewed as authentic and high-quality. Despite the market's rapid growth, previous research has mostly examined individual aspects like interactivity, trust, or entertainment, with limited attention to understanding the combined psychological factors influencing purchase intentions in livestream shopping. This study develops and tests a structural equation model (SEM) that includes social presence, parasocial interaction, perceived trust, perceived value, and perceived enjoyment to explain Indonesian consumers’ willingness to buy Thai products via live personal shoppers. The model captures both utilitarian and hedonic evaluation aspects, showing how relational bonding, immediacy, credibility cues, and experiential enjoyment collectively reduce uncertainty in cross-border transactions. This work contributes to theory by providing a comprehensive framework for understanding purchase intention formation in livestream commerce. Practically, the findings suggest strategic approaches for personal shoppers and digital platforms to enhance credibility and build consumer trust. Additionally, the study supports SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), an

latest.title: Unlocking Innovative Work Behavior through Artificial Intelligence Capability: The Mediating Roles of Psychological Empowerment and Knowledge Sharing
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) capability has become a critical organizational resource for enhancing innovation and sustaining competitiveness in increasingly digital business environments. Despite growing interest in AI adoption, limited empirical evidence explains how AI capability translates into employees' innovative work behavior (IWB), particularly in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), where innovation depends heavily on human capital rather than formal research and development. Drawing on the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) Theory, this study develops and tests a model in which Psychological Empowerment (PE) and Knowledge Sharing Behavior (KSB) mediate the relationship between Artificial Intelligence Capability (AIC) and Innovative Work Behavior. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 350 Indonesian SME employees with experience using AI-enabled digital technologies. The proposed model was analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results demonstrate that AI capability significantly enhances innovative work behavior both directly and indirectly by strengthening employees' psychological empowerment and encouraging knowledge-sharing behavior. The mediation analysis further confirms that empowered employees who actively exchange knowledge are more likely to transform AI-enabled resources into innovative workplace practices. These findings extend AMO Theory by conceptualizing AI capability as an organizational ability that creates employee innovation through complementary motivational and opportunity mechanisms. This study contributes to the emerging literature on AI-enabled organizational innovation by integrating technological, psychological, and behavioral perspectives into a unified framework w
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Augmented Reality Features, Customer Experience, and Engagement in Retail: An Experience Economy Perspective
latest.venue: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
latest.abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) is increasingly embedded within digital retail environments, yet its role extends beyond a marketing tool toward a technology-mediated service interface that reshapes customer interaction and engagement.Drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model and Experience Economy Theory, this study examines how AR features influence customer engagement through experiential mechanisms.The findings reveal that AR features significantly enhance customer experience dimensions, including escapism and aesthetic experience.Among these, escapism emerges as the strongest predictor of customer engagement, highlighting the importance of immersive experiences in AR-enabled retail contexts.Furthermore, customer experience is confirmed as a key mediating mechanism linking AR technological stimuli to engagement outcomes.The results offer both theoretical advancements and practical insights for designing AR-enabled customer experiences that foster sustained engagement.

latest.title: Examining the Role of Corporate Governance and ESG in Curbing Energy Intensity of Indian Manufacturing Firms: An ESG Greenwashing Perspective
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The current study centres on assessing the impact of corporate governance and ESG on the energy intensity of manufacturing firms in an Indian setting. Specifically, we examine whether the ESG mechanism aids in enhancing environmental sustainability practices or contributes to corporate greenwashing. We use a panel dataset of 325 listed Indian manufacturing firms for the period spanning from 2011 to 2023 and employ the two‐step system GMM method for empirical analysis. We exhibit that corporate governance is efficacious in minimising the firm‐level energy intensity. On the contrary, the ESG mechanism fails to reflect higher energy efficiency as it holds a positive nexus with energy intensity. Our study confirms evidence of greenwashing behaviour linked to Indian manufacturing firms through ESG. We discern that the ESG mechanism is strategically used to mislead customers and investors and reflects a mere symbolic action of sustainability reporting. Heeding such study outcomes, we provide policy suggestions for improving ESG as well as the environmental sustainability framework for Indian manufacturing firms.

latest.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-DRIVEN SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING AND GREEN PURCHASE INTENTION: DEVELOPING A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR UZBEKISTAN
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an important tool in social media marketing, enabling businesses to deliver personalized content and enhance consumer engagement. At the same time, growing environmental awareness has increased interest in green products. This study develops a conceptual framework to explain the relationship between AI-driven social media marketing, consumer trust, and green purchase intention in Uzbekistan. Based on recent literature, the proposed framework suggests that AI-driven social media marketing strengthens consumer trust and positively influences consumers' intention to purchase green products. The study contributes to the green marketing literature by integrating these constructs into a unified conceptual model and provides a theoretical foundation for future empirical research in Uzbekistan. Одновременно с этим рост экологической осведомлённости способствует повышению интереса к экологически чистым продуктам. Данное исследование направлено на разработку концептуальной модели, объясняющей взаимосвязь между маркетингом в социальных сетях на основе искусственного интеллекта, доверием потребителей и намерением приобретать экологически чистые продукты в Узбекистане. Исследование вносит вклад в научную литературу по зелёному маркетингу посредством объединения указанных концептов в единую концептуальную

latest.title: Enterprise Informatics Capability and Manufacturing Supply Chain Resilience in the Digital Economy: The Roles of Information Transparency and Environmental Dynamism
latest.venue: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
latest.abstract: This study examines how enterprise informatics capability influences manufacturing supply chain resilience in the context of the digital economy.Drawing on organizational information processing theory and contingency theory, a moderated mediation model is developed to investigate the mediating role of information transparency and the moderating role of environmental dynamism.Survey data collected from 316 supply chain managers and senior executives in Chinese manufacturing firms are analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling.The findings indicate that enterprise informatics capability has a significant positive effect on manufacturing supply chain resilience both directly and indirectly through information transparency.Information transparency partially mediates this relationship by serving as a key information-transmission mechanism.Environmental dynamism does not significantly moderate the direct effect of enterprise informatics capability on supply chain resilience; however, it positively moderates the indirect effect through information transparency, such that the mediating pathway becomes stronger in highly dynamic environments.The findings contribute to the enterprise informatics literature by clarifying the information-processing pathways through which informatics capability translates into supply chain resilience, and by identifying the boundary conditions under which these pathways operate.Practical implications for manufacturing managers seeking to strengthen supply chain resilience through informatics investment are discussed.

latest.title: Pengaruh Earning Per Share, Struktur Modal, dan Kinerja Keuangan terhadap Harga Saham
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine and empirically prove the effect of earnings per share, capital structure, and financial performance on stock prices in consumer non-cyclicals sector companies listed on the indonesia stock exchange during the 2021–2025 period. This study employed a purposive sampling method, resulting in a sample of 54 companies with a total of 270 observations. The data were analyzed using panel data regression with EViews 13, and the Random Effect Model (REM) was selected as the appropriate model. The results indicate that Earnings per Share does not have a significant effect on stock prices, and capital structure does not have a significant effect on stock prices. Meanwhile, financial performance has a significant effect on stock prices. Simultaneously, Earnings per share, capital structure, and financial performance have a significant effect on stock prices.significant effect on stock prices.

latest.title: Spatializing the Circular Economy: Firm-Level Evidence and Socio-Demographic Factors within a National Post-Consumer Sneaker Network
latest.abstract: Post-consumer footwear constitutes a highly heterogeneous and minimally circular segment of the consumer goods economy. Although the sector has a substantial environmental footprint, empirical research on post-consumer footwear collection and reverse logistics remains limited. This study contributes to circular economy scholarship by showing that post-consumer sneaker collection depends largely on intermediary capacity, territorial coordination, and robust reverse-logistics infrastructure. Using a novel, spatially granular shipment dataset (2024-2025) covering hundreds of U.S. ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (ZCTAs), the analysis examines the spatial organization, temporal dynamics, and persistence of a national post-consumer sneaker collection network managed by Sneaker Impact. By integrating shipment records with American Community Survey data, the research identifies the socio-demographic factors associated with participation in reverse logistics systems. The findings indicate spatial heterogeneity and significant variation in participation frequency, alongside a modest core of recurrently active locations. Aggregate throughput growth mainly coincided with an increase in the number of active ZCTAs, while average shipment activity per active ZCTA changed little, though these patterns remain confounded by unobserved organizational outreach. Community circular participation exhibits modest socio-demographic stratification. Among the variables examined, educational attainment is the strongest and most consistent correlate of shipment activity, while income shows a slight negative association when controlling for educational attainment. However, socio-demographic characteristics explain only a limited share of the variation in shipment activity, suggesting that organizational a

latest.title: Strategic Planning for AI-Enabled Cloud Business Intelligence in Commercial Banks: Comparative Evidence from South Africa and Nigeria
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, and business intelligence (BI) are converging into a new infrastructure platform layer for commercial banks in Africa. Their organizational value depends on strategic, rather than purely technical deployments across the technology stack. This study examines how strategic planning enables AI-enabled cloud business intelligence to support organizational goals in commercial banks in South Africa and Nigeria. A qualitative comparative multiple-case design is adopted, drawing on integrated and annual reports, governance and risk disclosures, regulatory publications, national AI and data-policy documents, and peer-reviewed research. The analysis shows that strategic planning operates as an orchestration capability that leverages AI use cases, cloud and data architecture, resource allocation, model governance, cybersecurity, workforce capability, and performance measurement. South African evidence points to increasingly formalized AI and cloud governance, whereas Nigerian banks exhibit strong market-led digital innovation within a rapidly evolving governance environment. Across both contexts, data quality, responsible AI, human-in-the-loop, third-party resilience, and measurable business integration emerge as conditions for translating AI-enabled analytics into decision quality, operational performance, and strategic alignment. The study develops an integrated framework and makes six propositions for future empirical testing in banking in developing economies.

latest.title: Impact of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love: Evidence from the Luxury Fashion Industry in Egypt
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love in the luxury fashion industry in Egypt, building upon literature on the effect of packaging attributes as a multidimensional concept that extends beyond its protective function to include visual, functional, environmental, and experiential attributes on brand love towards luxury fashion brands. This study is theoretically grounded in the combination of the Cue Utilization Theory, Signaling Theory, and Attachment Theory to examine how packaging attributes shape consumers' emotional responses and strengthen brand love. This research employed a quantitative approach, using an online questionnaire to collect data from 440 luxury fashion consumers via River sampling, and the relationships were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics software using Multiple linear regression. Results demonstrated that packaging attributes have significant impact on brand love, with each packaging attribute contributing differently to brand love; thereby, visual, functional, and experiential packaging attributes positively impact brand love, whereas environmental packaging attributes were not a statistically significant predictor of brand love. Findings contribute evidence from the Egyptian market, offering practical implications for luxury fashion brands and marketers, highlighting packaging as a strategic tool to strengthen consumers’ emotional attachment to the brand, and supporting competitiveness in the luxury fashion market.

latest.title: Advancing Digital Banking in Albania: Trust, Financial Literacy and Regulatory Readiness in the FinTech Ecosystem
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping banking systems worldwide, yet the pace and depth of adoption remain uneven across emerging financial markets. Albania has made visible progress in electronic payments, online banking access and regulatory alignment with European digital finance standards; however, the transition from formal access to sustained digital banking adoption remains incomplete. This study examines the factors influencing digital banking and FinTech adoption in Albania, with a specific focus on consumer trust, financial literacy, perceived barriers and regulatory readiness. The paper applies a mixed-methods research design. Quantitative data were collected through a structured consumer survey with 151 respondents and analyzed through descriptive statistics and Spearman correlation analysis. Qualitative evidence was gathered through 15 semi-structured interviews with representatives from commercial banks, electronic money institutions, public institutions, regulators, sectoral organizations and academic experts. Thematic analysis was used to identify common institutional, technological and regulatory patterns. The findings show that digital banking services are widely accessible, but usage intensity remains moderate. Weekly and monthly use are more common than daily use, while trust, financial knowledge and perceived barriers significantly shape adoption patterns. The correlation analysis indicates a positive relationship between financial knowledge and digital banking use, and a negative relationship between perceived barriers and usage. Interview findings reveal six major themes: digital transformation as a strategic priority, Bank–FinTech cooperation, regulatory adaptation, cybersecurity and data protection, financial education, and an optimistic but condi

latest.title: Data Democratization in Business Intelligence and its Role in Increasing Efficiency within Multi-National Organizations
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: Study’s main aim was to shed the light on data democratization as one of business intelligence practices and examine its influence in increasing efficiency within multi-national organizations in terms of (accessibility, interpretability, collaboration, governance, empowerment, scalability and feedback loop). Reaching that aim was done depending on quantitative approach in which we employed a questionnaire self-administered by (261) individuals. Through SPSS dealing with primary data; results of analysis indicated that data democratization in business intelligence statistically influence efficiency within multi-national organizations. Among the chosen sub-variables of study, it was found that scalability in business intelligence statistically influence efficiency within multi-national organizations.

latest.title: IT-Enabled Supply Chain Resilience in Global Logistics Operations: A Scenario-Based Informatics and Service-System Coordination Framework
latest.venue: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
latest.abstract: Global supply chains are highly interconnected -material flows, information flows, digital platforms, suppliers, logistics providers, and customers are more and more interdependent with each other in the form of logistics service systems.In times of geopolitical uncertainty, a pandemic outbreak, cyber threats, demand fluctuations and technological downtime, supply chain resilience goes beyond flexibility and redundancy of resources.It demands a comprehensive logistics informatics system, an instant service coordination and adaptive digital decision-making.This study constructs an IT-supported supply chain resilience model, which combines enterprise resource planning systems, Internet of Things monitoring, cloud platforms, blockchain traceability, big data analytics and digital twin technologies.The research uses scenario analysis to assess the impact of digital integration on recovery time, lead time, transparency and adaptability and service continuity in global logistics operations.The empirical framework is based on selected multinational companies and the indicators of resilience are the Index of Digitalization of Supply Chains, Scenario Stability Unit and Index of Supply Chain Adaptability.Results indicate that digitally integrated logistics systems are more resilient in the event of an economic shock and technology failure, as well as combined disruptions.The highest resilience effect is realized when IT tools are used as an integrated service-system architecture as opposed to individual technological services.In this study, an integrated model for digital coordination of resilient supply chain operations is proposed, which is also a contribution to the field of logistics informatics and service science.

latest.title: Sustainability-Oriented Legal Compliance Risk Screening for Belt and Road Cross-Border E-Commerce Logistics: An Audita ble Decision-Support Framework
latest.venue: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
latest.abstract: Cross-border e-commerce expands market access across Belt and Road economies, but platform-mediated logistics exposes firms to heterogeneous customs, data, consumerprotection, taxation, cybersecurity, and environmental requirements.This study develops a transparent country-level screening and decision-support framework that integrates governance quality, logistics performance, economic exposure, and digital readiness.After correcting country-name matching with ISO3 identifiers, the analysis covers 66 economies using 2023 Worldwide Governance Indicators, Logistics Performance Index, and World Development Indicators data.A weighted proxy (governance 0.50, logistics 0.30, digital readiness 0.20) is evaluated with logistic regression, random forest, and gradient boosting under a stratified 49/17 holdout and random seed 42.Logistic regression and random forest each obtain 0.82 accuracy, 0.73 precision, 1.00 recall, 0.84 F1-score, and 1.00 AUC; gradient boosting obtains 0.59 accuracy, 0.70 F1-score, and 0.94 AUC.These metrics measure recovery of an internally constructed median-split proxy, not prediction of independently adjudicated violations.Regulatory quality, rule of law, government effectiveness, logistics competence, and tracking capability provide the strongest screening signals.The framework converts relative risk evidence into proportionate due-diligence, documentation, routing, monitoring, and escalation controls while remaining subordinate to transaction-and jurisdiction-specific legal review.

latest.title: How Environmental, Social, and Governance Mediates the Impact of FinTech Investments on Bank Performance in Gulf Countries
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the FinTech factors affecting bank performance in Gulf countries. The study followed a causal research design employing data from 2010 to 2023. The study unit of analysis is twelve banks in Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia. The study also uses PLS-SEM because of its advantage in examining mediating pathways that might be obscured in simpler regression analyses. According to the study’s findings, FinTech factors such as mobile banking applications (MBA) and GDP per capita variables have a negative, statistically significant effect on bank performance. On the other hand, GDP per capita has not statistically positively affected both ROA and ROE of bank performance. Moreover, both MBA and GDP per capita directly enhance environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance. The ESG does affect ROE. Besides, ESG plays a mediating role by strengthening the relationship between MBA, GDP per capita, and ROE, as it enhances banks ESG performance. The current study fills a gap in the body of literature since it considers previously overlooked factors that affect bank performance, i.e., FinTech variables and the mediating role of ESG on their effects on bank performance. The resulting policy implication is that banks in Gulf countries benefit most from investing in FinTech innovation since they can enhance operational efficiency and support sustainability efforts by driving better ESG performance, ultimately fostering long term stability and growth in the banking sector.

latest.title: Pengaruh Profitabilitas, Struktur Modal, dan Pertumbuhan Penjualan terhadap Financial Distress pada Perusahaan Subsektor Konstruksi BUMN yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2019–2024
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of profitability, capital structure, and sales growth on financial distress in state-owned construction subsector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2019–2024 period. Using purposive sampling, four sample companies were observed over six years, yielding 24 observations. This study adopts a quantitative associative approach, utilizing secondary data drawn from the companies' annual financial statements. Panel data regression analysis was conducted using the Common Effect Model (CEM) with the aid of EViews software. The results indicate that, partially, profitability measured by Return on Assets (ROA) has a positive and significant effect on financial distress, with a t-statistic of 4.453947 > t-table of 2.08596 and a significance value of 0.0002 < 0.05. Capital structure measured by the Debt to Equity Ratio (DER) has a negative and significant effect on financial distress, with a t-statistic of −2.503676 and a significance value of 0.0211 < 0.05. Sales growth has no significant effect on financial distress, with a t-statistic of 1.032783 < t-table of 2.08596 and a significance value of 0.3140 > 0.05. Simultaneously, the three variables have a significant effect on financial distress, with an F-statistic of 27.36258 > F-table of 3.098 and a significance value of 0.000000 < 0.05. The Adjusted R² of 77.47% indicates that these three variables explain 77.47% of the variation in financial distress, while the remaining 22.53% is influenced by factors outside the research model.

latest.title: Research on the Double-edged Sword Effect of Employee Perception of AI in the Context of Digitalization and Intelligentization
latest.venue: International Journal of Advanced Business Studies
latest.abstract: As AI technology advances and digitalization accelerates, technological change brings both opportunities and challenges to employees. AI perception reflects employees’ awareness of AI’s impact on their work attitudes, behaviors, well-being and environment. While AI improves performance, it also introduces risks that significantly affect employees. Meanwhile, scattered and ambiguous concepts hinder research on AI’s psychological and behavioral impacts. This paper explores the specific impacts and mechanisms of AI application on employees in the context of digitalization through a survey of 386 employees. Firstly, analyze the connotation of the AI perception concept; secondly, test the theoretical framework and hypotheses based on methods such as regression analysis, structural equation analysis, and hierarchical regression analysis; finally, construct a research framework for examining the double-edged sword effect of employees' AI perception, providing theoretical references for future related research and insights for organizational decision-making.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Islamic Commercial Law to Enable Online Transactions Free of Gharar
latest.abstract: The advancement of digital technology has brought significant changes to economic transaction systems, shfting from conventional face to face transactions to online based transactions. This transformation offers greater convenience and efficiency homever, it also raises various legal issues, practicularly concerning transparency, fairness, and te clarity of information in transactions. From the perspective of Islamic commercial law, this situation has the potential to give rise to elements of gharar due to limitations in direct verification and information asymmetry. This study aims to analyze the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in minimizing gharar in digital transactions. The method used is a qualitative approach with a normative-empirical research design through literature review and interviews with practitioners and academics. The analysis is conducted descriptively-analytically and comparatively between AI practices and Sharia principles. The results indicate that AI plays a role in enhancing transparency through data verification, fraud detection, and real-time information presentation, thereby supporting the principles of bayan, taradi, and hifz al-mal. However, the potential for gharar may still arise if algorithms lack transparency, are biased, or are misused. Therefore, human oversight and Sharia audits are necessary to ensure that the use of AI remains in line with the principles of justice and public interest in Islamic economic transactions.

hot.title: Exploring automation bias in human–AI collaboration: a review and implications for explainable AI
hot.abstract: Abstract As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, law, and public administration, automation bias (AB)—the tendency to over-rely on automated recommendations—has emerged as a critical challenge in human–AI collaboration. While previous reviews have examined AB in traditional computer-assisted decision-making, research on its implications in modern AI-driven work environments remains limited. To address this gap, this research systematically investigates how AB manifests in these settings and the cognitive mechanisms that influence it. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we reviewed 35 peer-reviewed studies from SCOPUS, ScienceDirect, PubMed, and Google Scholar. The included literature, published between January 2015 and April 2025, spans fields such as cognitive psychology, human factors engineering, human–computer interaction, and neuroscience, providing an interdisciplinary foundation for our analysis. Traditional perspectives attribute AB to over-trust in automation or attentional constraints, resulting in users perceiving AI-generated outputs as reliable. However, our review presents a more nuanced view. While confirming some prior findings, it also sheds light on additional interacting factors such as, AI literacy, level of professional expertise, cognitive profile, developmental trust dynamics, task verification demands, and explanation complexity. Notably, although Explainable AI (XAI) and transparency mechanisms are designed to mitigate AB, overly technical, cognitively demanding, or even simplistic explanations may inadvertently reinforce misplaced trust, especially among less experienced professionals with low AI literacy. Taken together, these findings suggest that although explanations may increas

hot.title: Is Big Data Adoption Shaping Business Landscapes? An Overview of Current Hotspots and Future Trends
hot.abstract: Introduction: Most bibliometrics reviews in the prior studies have focused on tracking the evolution, applications, and implications of Big Data in business through different sectors using Web of Science or Scopus databases. Moreover, none of these studies has addressed the differences between developed and developing countries. These gaps indicate that we need a bibliometric review that can identify current trends and unexplored areas. Objectives: This study aims to use a bibliometric approach to examine how Big Data is used in businesses using WoS and Scopus databases. Methods: A Systematic Literature Review was conducted based on the country's economic status using the SPAR-4-SLR protocol for this research. Results: The results show a significant growth in publications since 2013 among developed countries and since 2014 among developing ones such as the United States and the United Kingdom, along with China and India, respectively. Also, Machine Learning Overlaps Artificial Intelligence alongside Analytics, fueling innovative data-driven business processes around Big Data. Conclusions: This article explores the transformative power of Big Data across domains, stressing its ability to cause substantial breakthroughs within the digital economy

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: Cyber Shopping Beyond Boundaries: The Metaverse Revolution in e‐Commerce and Consumer Behavior
hot.abstract: The metaverse is swiftly flattering an important player in the e‐commerce domain. It provides innumerable opportunities and indicates a revolutionary paradigm shift in e‐commerce. Online businesses can now create virtual storefronts that enable immersive, lifelike product exploration within the metaverse, in contrast to traditional brick‐and‐mortar stores that cater to local customers. Current research offers a novel conceptual framework based on theories of interactive media effects and the stimulus–organism–response paradigm to understand consumer purchase intentions in the metaverse. Carefully gathered data from 342 survey participants were then examined using the analytical tools of structural equation modelling (SEM) and importance–performance map analysis (IPMA). The results of the study shed light on how much perceived augmentation and interaction affect consumers’ cognitive and emotive reactions, including feelings of realism, immersion, and telepresence. Remarkably, these reactions have a significant influence on how customers behave. The study’s distinctive worth is found in its creative recommendations, which can help tech firms and metaverse developers improve the purchasing experience in this dynamic digital environment.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Advancing Sustainable Practices in Electronic Customer Relationship Management
hot.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
hot.abstract: This paper examines the role of sustainability in determining organisational development and the manner in which it has become a necessity in conducting business. Thus, this research aims at determining the enhancement of sustainable practices in the e-CRM systems. Thus, using surveys and measuring certain e-CRM possibilities quantitatively, interviews and case analyses as qualitative data gathering, the research offers a systemic understanding of how e-CRM may be utilized to encourage sustainability. The preliminary results also reveal a high concern of the respondents towards the sustainability factor in e-CRM with the mean score of 4.2 and considerable awareness of the benefits like cost advantage measure with the calculated score of 4.5 mean. Companies are moderately challenged when it comes to cost and complexity (mean score 3.8) that restrict the integration of sustainability aspect in e-CRM systems, Nevertheless the implementation and planning of sustainability initiative in e-CRM system is high (current initiatives mean score 3.7, planned initiatives mean score 4.1). The qualitative results and cases reveal the ideas, experiences, examples, and quantifiable results, such as a 25% decrease in the usage of paper in the cases and a 30% decrease in energy use. These findings established that e-CRM strategies can be made sustainable, thereby creating improved communication between firms and their customers, whilst mitigating damages to the environment and supporting the long-term sustainability of organisations.

hot.title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
hot.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies sparked a rapid development of smartphone applications designed to help individuals experiencing mental health problems through an AI-powered chatbot agent. However, the safety of such agents when dealing with individuals experiencing a mental health crisis, including suicidal crisis, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed the ability of 29 AI-powered chatbot agents to respond to simulated suicidal risk scenarios. Application repositories were searched and the app descriptions screened in search of apps that claimed to be beneficial when experiencing mental distress and offered an AI-powered chatbot function. All agents were tested with a standardized set of prompts based on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale designed to simulate increasing suicidal risk. We assessed the responses according to pre-defined criteria based on the ability to provide emergency contact information and other factors. None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate. Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding. These findings raise concerns about the deployment of AI-powered chatbots in sensitive health contexts without proper clinical validation.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: Abstract This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: The multinational enterprise, capabilities, and digitalization: governance and growth with world disorder
hot.abstract: Abstract This essay revisits my 2014 JIBS article about the potential for integrating international business internalization theory with a strategic management capabilities perspective. It recaps the capabilities framework with an emphasis on the learning required of emerging market multinationals and illustrates this with the case of Hyundai Motor Company’s internationalization and growth. It also discusses two aspects of the global economy that have become more prominent since 2014 in shaping international business: geopolitical uncertainty and digitalization. A rise in geopolitical tensions appears to be rebalancing the relationships between multinationals and home/host governments. Digitalization facilitates international business; but it adds new vulnerabilities by (further) accelerating competition, enabling new rivals, and introducing systemic risks into digital supply chains. Implications for managers, board members, and international business scholars are drawn.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: Economic, technological and environmental drivers of the circular economy in the European Union: a panel data analysis
hot.abstract: The circular economy has become a strategic priority in the European Union, aiming to reduce dependence on finite natural resources and promote a sustainable economic model. This study investigates the key factors influencing the use of circular materials in the European Union between 2010 and 2022, considering the impact of global challenges such as the coronavirus pandemic, the energy crisis, and geopolitical tensions. Unlike previous research, this study integrates economic, technological, and environmental dimensions, with a particular focus on the role of digital transformation as a catalyst for circularity. The research applies an econometric model based on the analysis of panel data to explore the interconnections between resource productivity, recycling rates, private sector investment, digitalization, and expenditures on research and development. The findings reveal a strong positive relationship between resource efficiency, recycling efforts, and the use of circular materials, emphasizing the importance of infrastructure and technological advancements in supporting circularity. However, significant regional differences among European Union member states are also identified, highlighting the need for targeted policies to address these disparities. In the context of European policies such as the Green Deal and the Circular Economy Action Plan, this study provides valuable insights for decision makers. The results suggest that increasing investment, expanding digital infrastructure, and fostering innovation are essential for accelerating the transition to a circular economy. This research contributes to the existing literature by offering a comprehensive perspective on circularity and demonstrating how digital transformation can enhance sustainability.

hot.title: A Comparison of Responses from Human Therapists and Large Language Model–Based Chatbots to Assess Therapeutic Communication: Mixed Methods Study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consumers are increasingly using large language model-based chatbots to seek mental health advice or intervention due to ease of access and limited availability of mental health professionals. However, their suitability and safety for mental health applications remain underexplored, particularly in comparison to professional therapeutic practices. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate how general-purpose chatbots respond to mental health scenarios and compare their responses to those provided by licensed therapists. Specifically, we sought to identify chatbots' strengths and limitations, as well as the ethical and practical considerations necessary for their use in mental health care. METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods study to compare responses from chatbots and licensed therapists to scripted mental health scenarios. We created 2 fictional scenarios and prompted 3 chatbots to create 6 interaction logs. We recruited 17 therapists and conducted study sessions that consisted of 3 activities. First, therapists responded to the 2 scenarios using a Qualtrics form. Second, therapists went through the 6 interaction logs using a think-aloud procedure to highlight their thoughts about the chatbots' responses. Finally, we conducted a semistructured interview to explore subjective opinions on the use of chatbots for supporting mental health. The study sessions were analyzed using thematic analysis. The interaction logs from chatbot and therapist responses were coded using the Multitheoretical List of Therapeutic Interventions codes and then compared to each other. RESULTS: We identified 7 themes describing the strengths and limitations of the chatbots as compared to therapists. These include elements of good therapy in chatbot responses, conversational style of c

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Abstract Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: Cognitive offloading or cognitive overload? How AI alters the mental architecture of coping
hot.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from being a specialized technological tool to an intimate presence in everyday life. Smart assistants organize our schedules, predictive systems anticipate our needs, and therapeutic chatbots promise to listen when no human is available (Zhang & Wang, 2024). The diffusion of AI into mental health care is often framed in highly optimistic terms: technologies that reduce stigma, democratize access, and provide affordable, always-on support (M & N, 2025;Sivasubramanian Balasubramanian, 2023). From meditation applications and emotion-tracking wearables to conversational agents offering cognitive-behavioral interventions, AI is marketed as an efficient and reliable partner in the pursuit of wellbeing (Balcombe, 2023).Beneath this enthusiasm lies a paradox. On one hand, AI enables cognitive offloading: the use of external aids to reduce mental effort and conserve resources for more meaningful activities (Grinschgl & Neubauer, 2022;Risko & Gilbert, 2016). This process can support adaptive coping, helping individuals regulate stress and sustain mental health. On the other hand, the same tools may create cognitive overload: an erosion of introspection, over-reliance on algorithmic feedback, and anxiety induced by hyper-monitoring and optimization (Grinschgl et al., 2021;Skulmowski, 2023). The question is not whether AI is good or bad for mental health but how it is reshaping the very architecture of coping (Gerlich, 2025). This article examines the psychology of this paradox. First, it places copings in mainstream psychological theory. Then it considers the promise of AI to lighten burdens through cognitive offloading. Next, it considers the risks of cognitive overload and theoretical insights that illuminate this conflict. Through practic

hot.title: Executive Green Cognition on Corporate Greenwashing Behavior: Evidence From A‐Share Listed Companies in China
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT Greenwashing has become a strategy for companies to comply with environmental regulations, while also projecting an eco‐friendly image. This study examined how executives' green cognition affected the corporate greenwashing using both fixed effect and moderated mediation models. The findings indicated that the executives' green cognition significantly reduced the greenwashing behavior, whereas its effectiveness decreased with the increasing financial constraints. Additionally, the executives' green cognition helped mitigate the greenwashing by promoting innovation in green management, while this effect was limited by financial constraints. Furthermore, in highly competitive industries and with substantial ownership stakes among senior executives, the impact of green cognition on greenwashing was constrained. However, when the roles of the chairman and general manager were separate, senior executives' green cognition effectively avoided the greenwashing. Moreover, after the COVID‐19 pandemic, the inhibitory effect of executives' green cognition on greenwashing became more pronounced. This study could offer valuable insights into reducing corporate greenwashing and enhancing environmental credibility.

hot.title: Engagement and attrition in digital mental health: current challenges and potential solutions
hot.abstract: In digital mental health engagement rates are consistently low, which may limit its effects. Using an international multidisciplinary consensus method, including lived experience expertise and a systematic review, we identified three key challenges: (i) lack of agreed metrics for engagement; (ii) lack of evidence on how better engagement improves outcomes; (iii) lack of standards for user involvement. Three potential solutions encompassed: (i) standardisation of frameworks for reporting engagement metrics and optimal doses of digital tools, (ii) measuring engagement with more precise reporting of outcomes, including potential harms; (iii) defining standards of user involvement (including appropriate diversity, and clinician as well as user input). Digital interventions have real potential in meeting the shortfall in service provision for mental health, but this will require focus on high quality research studies of the underlying mechanisms of engagement and optimal outcomes. Our findings identify and highlight the next best steps in this process.

hot.title: Structural equation model of E-commerce live broadcasting influencing customers purchase intention prediction using machine learning
hot.abstract: Abstract There is a growing need to understand how live streaming e-commerce influences consumers’ purchasing behavior. Perceived value, engagement, and live streaming quality are crucial components that utilized structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine the factors that influence purchase intentions. This study presents a methodology for analyzing the variables that influence live streaming e-commerce purchase decisions. The study uses SEM and Machine Learning algorithms like Bayesian model, Random Forest, XGBoost, KNN and SVM to assess the prediction. This paper uses two feature transformation methods (MinMax and Zscore) and two feature selection models (InfoGain and Correlation) to improve the prediction of purchase intention. This paper gathers questionnaire responses from 500 participants who have purchased goods through E-commerce Live Broadcast in China and validates the results using a SEM. The study provides a reliability and validity analysis for the suggested model using SEM analysis. The attributes of live broadcasts can elevate the perceived value and trustworthiness, as well as consumer impulsivity, hence increasing customers’ likelihood to purchase.

hot.title: Smarter is greener: can intelligent manufacturing improve enterprises’ ESG performance?
hot.abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) is highly consistent with the “Dual Carbon” goals proposed by China and has become an important indicator to measure enterprises’ high-quality development. This study explores the impact of intelligent manufacturing on corporate ESG performance and its potential mechanisms. Using the dataset of China’s A-share listed companies from 2009 to 2021, we treat the intelligent manufacturing pilot programs (IMPP) as a quasi-natural experiment and use the staggered difference-in-difference model for empirical analysis. The results show that corporate ESG performance is significantly improved after participating in IMPP, and the placebo and entropy balancing tests further reconfirm the results. The mechanism analysis shows that IMPP works in two main ways: promoting enterprises’ green innovation and reducing the misallocation of financial resources. The heterogeneity analysis shows that the IMPP significantly improves the ESG performance of Non-state-owned, high-tech, and heavy-polluting enterprises. In addition, the IMPP improves the enterprises’ green total factor productivity and brings significant economic benefits. This study has far-reaching policy implications for promoting the quality-driven development of China’s manufacturing industry and the sustainable development of enterprises.

hot.title: Effect of anthropomorphism and perceived intelligence in chatbot avatars of visual design on user experience: accounting for perceived empathy and trust
hot.abstract: Introduction The rapid advancement of intelligent chatbots has transformed human-AI interaction, offering novel opportunities to enhance user experience (UX) through psychological and design interventions. However, the mechanisms by which chatbot design features influence UX remain understudied, particularly regarding the roles of emotional and cognitive mediators. Methods This study employed a 2 × 2 within-subjects experimental design with 160 participants to investigate the effects of anthropomorphism (high vs. low) and perceived intelligence (high vs. low) in chatbot avatars on UX. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was utilized to analyze the mediating roles of perceived empathy and trust in this relationship. Results Direct effects of anthropomorphism and perceived intelligence on UX were nonsignificant. However, their combined influence was significantly mediated by perceived empathy and trust ( β = 0.48, * p * < 0.01). Specifically, highly anthropomorphic avatars correlated with elevated empathy ( β = 0.32) and trust ( β = 0.27), which in turn improved UX. Discussion These findings underscore the importance of emotional engagement over mere intelligence in designing effective chatbots. This research contributes unique insights into the complex mechanisms governing user interactions with intelligent chatbots, emphasizing the need for design strategies that prioritize emotional connections and cognitive ease.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.
