hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Hotel certifications are not only crucial for environmental sustainability, but also serve as

hot.title: Digital literacy, digital accessibility, human capital, and entrepreneurial resilience: a case for dynamic business ecosystems
hot.abstract: This study examines the role of digital literacy, digital accessibility, and human capital in fostering entrepreneurial resilience among entrepreneurs in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These countries serve as exemplary models in digital transformation, particularly in navigating crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Grounded in the resource-based view and the theory of dynamic capabilities, this research investigates how these factors contribute to entrepreneurial resilience. This study employs structural equation modeling to analyze survey data from 317 individuals with entrepreneurial experience. According to the findings, digital literacy, accessibility, and human capital significantly enhance innovation, strengthening entrepreneurial resilience. Agility is identified as a key moderator, amplifying the positive impact of these competencies on resilience. Although the success of entrepreneurial ecosystems has often been attributed to entrepreneurial actors, resource providers, connectors, or entrepreneurial intentions, this study underscores the importance of fostering digital competencies and agility to build resilient entrepreneurial ecosystems. It offers policymakers and business leaders insights into the mechanisms that enhance resilience in dynamic and crisis-affected environments where the digital landscape is rapidly evolving.

hot.title: Digital Leadership and Sustainable Development: Enhancing Firm Sustainability Through Green Innovation and Top Management Innovativeness
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the crucial role of digital leadership in advancing sustainable development by fostering green innovation and enhancing firm sustainability. Building on Organizational Learning Theory (OLT) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory (DCT), this research fills a key gap by examining how digital leadership integrates digitalization with sustainable development, particularly within the Chinese information technology sector. The study investigates the impact of digital leadership on green innovation and sustainable performance, moderated by top management innovativeness. To enhance analytical robustness and minimize bias, a three‐phase time‐lagged data collection approach was employed to mitigate common method bias and ensure robust analysis, with responses from 413 employees representing diverse roles. The results indicate that digital leadership positively influences the green innovation process, which partially mediates the relationship between digital leadership and firm sustainability. Furthermore, the findings reveal that top management innovativeness amplifies the positive effects of digital leadership on green innovation, reinforcing the importance of leadership‐driven sustainability strategies. These insights contribute to the expanding discourse on corporate digital sustainability, demonstrating that digital transformation not only enhances operational efficiency but also serves as a catalyst for long‐term sustainable development. The study offers valuable implications for policymakers, business leaders, and researchers committed to leveraging digital leadership for corporate sustainability and the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

hot.title: Customer data access and fintech entry: Early evidence from open banking
hot.abstract: Open banking (OB) empowers bank customers to share their financial transaction data with fintechs and other banks. New cross-country data shows 49 countries adopted OB policies, privacy preferences predict policy adoption, and adoption spurs fintech entry. UK microdata shows that OB enables: (i) consumers to access both financial advice and credit; (ii) SMEs to establish new lending relationships. In a calibrated model, OB universally improves welfare through entry and product improvements when used for advice. When used for credit, OB promotes entry and competition by reducing adverse selection, but higher prices for costlier or privacy-conscious consumers partially offset these benefits.

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: The impact of digital HRM system and digital transformation on HR efficiency with organizational agility as a moderator
hot.abstract: The study focuses on understanding the moderation effect of organizational agility in the impact of digital HRM system and digital transformation on HR efficiency in organizations intending to excel in the digital era. This study examines the association between digital HRM systems, digital transformation, and HR efficiency, considering the moderating role of organizational agility. Based on the study model, the authors proposed five hypotheses to be tested in this study. They adapted the study instrument based on quantitative descriptive approach and distributed 500 questioners to collect 385 responses. The study’s findings reveal that both digital HRM systems and digital transformation impact HR efficiency. The significant findings were that digital HRM systems (β = 0.456, p < 0.001) and digital transformation (β = 0.194, p = 0.006) have a positive and significant impact on HR efficiency. In addition, organizational agility serves as a moderator in the relationship between digital HRM systems and HR efficiency (β = 0.154, p = 0.025) but has no effect on the relationship with digital transformation (β = − 0.075, p = 0.248). This study contributes to the literature by demonstrating the role of digital HRM systems and digital transformation as key organizational resources that enhance HR efficiency. It also highlights how organizational agility and digital capabilities serve as dynamic resources, contributing to an organization’s adaptability and sustained competitive advantage. The future research directions and limitations are presented at the end.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: How do we assess the trustworthiness of AI? Introducing the trustworthiness assessment model (TrAM)
hot.abstract: Designing trustworthy AI-based systems and enabling external parties to accurately assess the trustworthiness of these systems are crucial objectives. Only if trustors assess system trustworthiness accurately, they can base their trust on adequate expectations about the system and reasonably rely on or reject its outputs. However, the process by which trustors assess a system’s actual trustworthiness to arrive at their perceived trustworthiness remains underexplored. In this paper, we conceptually distinguish between actual and perceived trustworthiness, trust propensity, trust, and trusting behavior. Drawing on psychological models of how humans assess other people’s characteristics, we present the two-level Trustworthiness Assessment Model (TrAM). At the micro level, we propose that trustors assess system trustworthiness based on cues associated with the system. The accuracy of this assessment depends on cue relevance and availability on the system’s side, and on cue detection and utilization on the human’s side. At the macro level, we propose that individual micro-level trustworthiness assessments propagate across different trustors – one stakeholder’s trustworthiness assessment of a system affects other stakeholder’s trustworthiness assessments of the same system. The TrAM advances existing models of trust and sheds light on factors influencing the (accuracy of) trustworthiness assessments. It contributes to theoretical clarity in trust research, has implications for the measurement of trust-related variables, and practical implications for system design, stakeholder training, and regulation related to trustworthiness assessments.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Recommendations and Functional Food Purchases: Understanding Consumer Decision-Making
hot.abstract: Amid rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), personalized recommendation systems have become a key factor shaping consumer decision-making in functional food purchases. However, the influence of AI recommendation characteristics on purchase intention, particularly the underlying mediating mechanisms, remains underexplored. This study aims to investigate how AI recommendation features (personalization and transparency), along with functional food attributes (perceived health benefits and perceived naturalness), influence purchase intention through the mediating roles of perceived packaging and perceived value. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework, data were collected via a structured questionnaire survey, and structural equation modeling was employed for hypothesis testing and model validation. The results indicate that AI recommendation personalization significantly enhances purchase intention both directly and indirectly, while transparency influences purchase intention only through perceived value, emphasizing its role in fostering trust rather than directly driving purchasing behavior. Additionally, perceived health benefits positively influence purchase intention both directly and through mediation, whereas perceived naturalness affects purchase intention only indirectly via perceived value. These findings contribute to consumer behavior research by elucidating psychological mechanisms underlying AI-driven purchase decisions while also providing insights for functional food marketers on how to effectively integrate AI recommendation systems to enhance consumer engagement.

hot.title: Barriers and Enablers of AI Adoption in Human Resource Management: A Critical Analysis of Organizational and Technological Factors
hot.abstract: This paper examines the key factors recognized as transformative in the field of human resource management (HRM) and explores their influence on the global adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). While AI holds significant promise for enhancing HRM efficiency, employee engagement, and Decision Making, its implementation presents a range of organizational, technical, and ethical challenges that organizations worldwide must navigate. Change aversion, data security worries, and integration expenses are major roadblocks, but strong digital leadership, company culture, and advancements in NLP and machine learning are key enablers. This paper presents a complex analysis that questions the common perception of AI as only disruptive by delving into the relationship between power dynamics, corporate culture, and technology infrastructures. In this paper, we bring together research from several fields to help scholars and practitioners understand the nuances of AI adoption in HRM, with an emphasis on the importance of inclusive methods and ethical frameworks.

hot.title: The Vector Grounding Problem
hot.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) produce seemingly meaningful outputs, yet they are trained on text alone without direct interaction with the world. This leads to a modern variant of the classical symbol grounding problem in AI: can LLMs' internal states and outputs be about extra-linguistic reality, independently of the meaning human interpreters project onto them? We argue that they can. We first distinguish referential grounding—the connection between a representation and its worldly referent—from other forms of grounding and argue it is the only kind essential to solving the problem. We contend that referential grounding is achieved when a system's internal states satisfy two conditions derived from teleosemantic theories of representation: (1) they stand in appropriate causal-informational relations to the world, and (2) they have a history of selection that has endowed them with the function of carrying this information. We argue that LLMs can meet both conditions, even without multimodality or embodiment.

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: The current clinical approach to feeding and eating disorders aimed to increase personalization of management
hot.abstract: Feeding and eating disorders (FEDs) are a heterogeneous grouping of disorders at the mind-body interface, with typical onset from childhood into emerging adulthood. They occur along a spectrum of disordered eating and compensatory weight management behaviors, and from low to high body weight. Psychiatric comorbidities are the norm. In contrast to other major psychiatric disorders, first-line treatments for FEDs are mainly psychological and/or nutrition-focused, with medications playing a minor adjunctive role. Patients, carers and clinicians all have identified personalization of treatment as a priority. Yet, for all FEDs, the evidence base supporting this personalization is limited. Importantly, disordered eating and related behaviors can have serious physical consequences and may put the patient's life at risk. In these cases, immediate safety and risk management considerations may at least for a period need to be prioritized over other efforts at personalization of care. This paper systematically reviews several key domains that may be relevant to the characterization of the individual patient with a FED aimed at personalization of management. These domains include symptom profile, clinical subtypes, severity, clinical staging, physical complications and consequences, antecedent and concomitant psychiatric conditions, social functioning and quality of life, neurocognition, social cognition and emotion, dysfunctional cognitive schemata, personality traits, family history, early environmental exposures, recent environmental exposures, stigma, and protective factors. Where possible, validated assessment measures for use in clinical practice are identified. The limitations of the current evidence are pointed out, and possible directions for future research are highlighte

latest.title: Predicting different dimensions of fatigue from speech data: a longitudinal study in shift workers
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Shift work, or working outside of normal circadian cycles, is associated with both experience of fatigue and poorer long-term physical and mental health. However, current methods for assessing fatigue present several barriers to building understanding of how these risks develop over time within individuals. Objective Here, we explore the potential of momentary speech activity-based fatigue measurement in a large, multi-lingual cohort of shift workers, using an intensive longitudinal study design (twice-daily measurement over two weeks in N =1,197 individuals from six different countries). Methods Paralinguistic speech features were used to predict different aspects of acute and chronic fatigue at each study time-point, with performance assessed in unseen (held-out) data. Results are reported both across the dataset as a whole, and for user-specific prediction models. Findings In the cross-sectional analysis, good (close to or exceeding current state-of-the-art) performance was achieved for both current sleep deprivation and self-reported sleepiness levels. The within-user analysis revealed robust increases in performance, yielding the ability to detect more subjective aspects of fatigue such as pervasive physical and mental exhaustion. Conclusions These findings offer preliminary support for the utility of using brief momentary speech samples as a low-burden, acceptable, and reliable measure of different aspects of fatigue in high-risk populations such as shift workers. Clinical Implications Developing brief, accessible measures of different dimensions of fatigue is an important step towards building understanding of how risks for poorer health outcomes develop over time within individuals exposed to significant circadian disruption. latest.title: Vague Stimulating Ideas, Images and Metaphors in Scientific Thinking: Researchers’ Work with Horizons of Unclear Knowledge
COMMERCIALIZATION OF YOUTH INNOVATION PROJECTS: FROM IDEAS TO SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This paper examines the scientific and practical aspects of commercializing youth innovation projects and transforming innovative ideas into sustainable businesses. The study focuses on the importance of entrepreneurial skills, market research, financial management, technological development, and institutional support in the commercialization process. Particular attention is given to the challenges faced by young entrepreneurs and the mechanisms that facilitate the successful introduction of innovative products and services into competitive markets. The research employs theoretical analysis and synthesis of scientific literature to identify the main factors influencing innovation commercialization. The findings suggest that effective business development requires a comprehensive approach integrating creativity, strategic planning, economic feasibility, and sustainable management practices.

latest.title: Organisational capabilities, corporate sustainability and firm competitiveness of coffee enterprises in Vietnam's Central Highlands: co-creation in an international trade context
latest.venue: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines how marketing capability, digital capability, and supply chain capability influence corporate sustainability and firm competitiveness among coffee enterprises in Vietnam's Central Highlands. It also investigates the moderating role of co-creation in the relationship between corporate sustainability and firm competitiveness. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, Stakeholder Theory, and Service-Dominant Logic, the study analyses data from 236 coffee enterprises using SmartPLS 4 and PLS-SEM. Corporate sustainability is modelled as a higher-order construct including economic, social, and environmental dimensions. Findings All hypotheses are supported. Marketing capability, digital capability, and supply chain capability positively affect corporate sustainability, with digital capability showing the strongest effect. Corporate sustainability strongly enhances firm competitiveness and mediates the effects of organisational capabilities on competitiveness. Co-creation also positively moderates the sustainability–competitiveness link. Research limitations/implications The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, self-reported data, and regional focus, which may constrain generalisability. However, it shows that competitiveness depends not only on internal capabilities but also on sustainability-oriented practices and stakeholder collaboration. Originality/value This study integrates key organisational capabilities into a unified framework explaining how corporate sustainability enhances firm competitiveness in an export-oriented agricultural context. It also highlights the mediating role of sustainability and the moderating role of co-creation in strengthening sustainable competitiveness i

latest.title: PRAKTIK BELAJAR MEMBACA PADA MAPEL BAHASA INDONESIA DI KELAS 1 SDN KEMBANGARUM 01 SEMARANG
latest.venue: LANGUAGE Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Bahasa dan Sastra
latest.abstract: Reading proficiency serves as the fundamental cornerstone of basic literacy in primary education, yet early-grade mastery often encounters substantial obstacles. This study aimed to analyze the specific forms of early reading difficulties and identify contributing factors among first-grade students at SDN Kembangarum 01 Semarang. A qualitative descriptive design was employed, focusing on five students selected through purposive sampling. Data were gathered through early reading assessment tests, classroom observations, in-depth interviews with the teacher and parents, and documentation. The most prominent findings revealed that all five subjects experienced pronounced difficulties in discriminating visually similar letters (b-d, p-q), articulating diphthongs, and decoding complex consonant clusters (ng, ny), resulting in faltering reading fluency. These difficulties were influenced by internal factors, including communicative anxiety, physical fatigue, and fluctuating attention spans, as well as external elements such as limited visual media and varying domestic learning support. ABSTRAK Kemampuan membaca merupakan fondasi utama literasi dasar di sekolah dasar, namun penguasaannya pada kelas awal masih menghadapi tantangan nyata. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis bentuk kesulitan membaca permulaan dan mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor yang berkontribusi terhadap kendala tersebut pada peserta didik kelas 1 SDN Kembangarum 01 Semarang. Pendekatan yang digunakan adalah kualitatif deskriptif terhadap lima peserta didik yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui tes kemampuan membaca permulaan, observasi kelas, wawancara mendalam dengan guru dan orang tua, serta dokumentasi. latest.title: Pre-free-throw ritualized behaviors among Chinese basketball players: a qualitative study
latest.abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to comprehensively explore the formation reasons and constituent elements of pre-free-throw ritualized behaviors (RBs) among Chinese basketball players under competitive pressure, and to investigate participants’ perceptions of how RBs influence their psychological states and sports performance. The study was conducted within China’s official Athlete Technical Level Grading System , where athletes are classified into hierarchical levels reflecting their competitive achievements. Methods We conducted one-on-one semi-structured interviews with 20 Chinese basketball players at or above the National Level 2. Using a qualitative research approach based on codebook thematic analysis (TA), we explored the usage background, usage goals, usage habits, usage experiences and effectiveness evaluation of their RBs. Results Participants reported that Chinese basketball players primarily adopt pre-free-throw RBs to alleviate negative emotions and enhance attentional focus, which they perceived as beneficial to their performance. The execution steps of pre-free-throw RBs predominantly consist of 3 to 4 actions, which typically include dribbling, deep breathing, spinning the ball, wiping shoe soles and focusing on the basket. Moreover, as competition intensity increases, both the duration and frequency of RB use tend to increase. Participants reported that performing pre-free-throw RBs produced a series of positive psychological effects, and they perceived a noticeable improvement in their free-throw accuracy. Conversely, if athletes were required to refrain from performing pre-free-throw RBs, they anticipated negative effects, including a perceived decline in free-throw accuracy. Conclusions The study suggests that pre-free-throw RBs may play a role

latest.title: Effects of air pollution on corporate charitable donations: evidence from China
latest.abstract: Air pollution, which is viewed as one of the global environmental challenges, not only brings huge health costs, but also worsens firm performance. An increasing number of studies have recognized that air pollution has important implications for firm behaviors. However, little research focuses on how air pollution influences corporate charitable donation, which is a key behavior for firms to improve reputation and market valuation. In this paper, we combine the listed data from China Stock Market and Accounting Research Database and city-level air pollution data in China to investigate the impact of air pollution on corporate charitable donation. Using the instrumental variable method and regression discontinuity design, we find that an increase in air pollution would lead to a reduction in corporate charitable donations. Our results are robust to various specifications that consider potential air pollution data manipulation, alternative measures, and exclusion of first-tier cities. We further conduct the heterogeneity analyses and find that state-owned enterprises and firms in highly polluting industries are more sensitive to the change of air pollution.

latest.title: Swap and Save: How a Button Shapes Lasting Online Grocery Shopping Behavior
latest.abstract: A well-documented phenomenon in the literature is that consumers exhibit persistence in their choices. Using data from the mineral water category on a price comparison platform that delivers real-time prompts of cheaper alternatives through "swap and save" buttons, this study examines whether and how these prompts influence persistent product choices in online grocery shopping. The findings reveal that shoppers who switched to an alternative product after receiving a prompt were 23.7 percentage points more likely to select that alternative product in subsequent visits, with this effect lasting for up to 10 shopping trips. Our analysis suggests that this sustained impact is driven not by long-term cost savings but by product discovery enabled through these real-time prompts.

latest.title: Cash Hedging under Partial Vertical Ownership: A Mean-Variance Analysis
latest.abstract: Existing research has separately explored cash hedging and partial vertical ownership (PVO), yet their joint impact on supply chain operations—especially under overlapping external risks and internal ownership structures—remains underexplored. This study investigates how PVO influences a risk-averse supplier’s cash hedging strategies and profitability. We develop a two-tier supply chain model with an upstream supplier and two downstream manufacturers (one holding PVO), using a mean-variance framework and binary hedging strategy (full/no hedging). We reveal a paradox: while vertical ownership seemingly should intensify hedging through risk-sharing, PVO in fact reduces supplier’s hedging likelihood by mitigating standalone risk aversion, thereby raising the threshold. Uniform pricing under PVO raises hedging thresholds more than differentiated pricing, enhancing risk absorption. Higher PVO boosts the partially owned manufacturer’s profits at the supplier’s expense, particularly with low production costs. Increased product substitution diminishes profits for all firms and weakens hedging advantages due to market volatility. Sequential manufacturer decisions lower the supplier’s hedging threshold relative to simultaneous decisions. An increase in the partial hedging ratio leads to an inverse U-shaped pattern in the supplier’s hedging threshold. This study shows that firms must consider PVO when making hedging and pricing plans. Managers should balance risk and market share, and pay attention to how ownership and product similarity affect risk decisions.

latest.title: OPEN: A Benchmark Dataset and Baseline for Older Adult Patient Engagement Recognition in Virtual Rehabilitation Learning Environments
latest.venue: ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare
latest.abstract: Engagement in virtual learning is critical to participant satisfaction, performance, and adherence, particularly in domains such as online education and virtual rehabilitation, where interactive communication is essential for success. However, accurately measuring engagement in virtual group settings remains a significant challenge. There is growing interest in leveraging artificial intelligence for large-scale, real-world, and automated engagement recognition. Although engagement has been widely studied among younger populations in academic contexts, research methods and datasets focused on older adults in virtual and telehealth learning environments remain limited. Existing approaches often overlook the contextual relevance of learning materials and the longitudinal dynamics of engagement across sessions. This paper presents OPEN (Older adult Patient ENgagement), a novel dataset created to support the development of artificial intelligence models for engagement recognition. The dataset was collected from eleven older adults participating in virtual group learning sessions over six weeks as part of their cardiac rehabilitation programs, yielding over 35 hours of data, which represents the largest dataset of its kind. While raw video is withheld to protect privacy, the publicly released data include facial, hand, and body joint landmarks, as well as behavioral and affective features extracted from video. Observational annotations comprise second-level binary engagement states, emotional and behavioral labels, and context-type details, such as whether the instructor addressed the group or an individual. Multiple versions of the dataset were generated using sample lengths of 5, 10, and 30 seconds, as well as variable-length segments. To demonstrate its utility, various ma

latest.title: Test-track and on-road studies: Methodological insights on the assessment of carsickness and its modulating factors
latest.venue: Transportation Research Part F Traffic Psychology and Behaviour
latest.abstract: The research on motion sickness and effective countermeasures has gained additional attention due to the ongoing development of highly automated driving vehicles. In order to understand the phenomenon of motion sickness better and support effective testing, this work sheds lights on motion sickness considering essential modulating factors: The relation between the development of carsickness and testing environment is explored in relation to psychological factors. Simultaneously, carsickness is often stimulated by non-driving related tasks (NDRTs) and publications have shown different effects on motion sickness by various NDRTs. Therefore, it is also investigated whether the optical flow during NDRTs influences carsickness. Lastly, it is investigated whether there is an effect on performance caused by carsickness across different testing environments. 47 participants participated in a within-subject study in a vehicle either driving on a public road or on a test track. While administering comparable accelerations and two randomly assigned NDRTs, carsickness, psychological factors and performance were measured within these environments. The results indicate that it was possible to set-up rides in both environments which led to comparable motion sickness stimuli based on the vehicle accelerations. The optical flow did not significantly affect carsickness on a population-level but illustrated ~15% on individual level. At the same time, few differences could be found among psychological factors, but they do not indicate that the transfer of results between testing environments would not be valid. Lastly, cognitive performance was affected by the two testing environments with regard to the reaction time. This work elucidates on the one hand that multiple factors influence mot

latest.title: When Is Something Alive? Integrating Bottom-Up and Top-Down Perspectives on Aliveness
latest.venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Consciousness
latest.abstract: What it means for an individual entity to be alive remains conceptually unresolved, particularly for artificial systems that display increasingly life-like behavior. This paper distinguishes life as an evolutionary, population-level process from aliveness as an individual property, and develops a candidate condition for assessing when an entity, biological or artificial, should be considered alive. A bottom-up heuristic identifies structural and functional characteristics commonly associated with biological organisms, but applying this heuristic to an embodied artificial agent shows that such characteristics are not by themselves sufficiently discriminative. A complementary top-down perspective introduces self-referential regulation, understood as the capacity of an entity to internally represent and regulate its own continued existence through embodied causal processes. Integrating both perspectives yields a unified candidate condition for aliveness, proposed primarily for complex entities while leaving open how aliveness should be characterized in simpler ones.

latest.title: Friend advice influences mate choice through brain-to-brain synchrony and computational decision processes
latest.abstract: Abstract Individuals often rely on friends’ advice when facing ambiguous cues in mate-choice decisions, yet how such advice optimizes outcomes remains unclear. Using fNIRS hyperscanning, we simultaneously recorded neural and behavioral activity from 66 adult friend dyads (33 female dyads) during interactive advice phases. Computational modeling quantified the decision optimization parameter ( β ). It showed that only the bidirectional Social Information Processing (SIP) model—best fit behavioral data, indicating that optimization arises from reciprocal adaptation rather than one-way influence. Behaviorally, positive advice from in the relationship advisors increased mate-choice intention, whereas negative advice from single advisors more effectively promoted optimization. Both conditions elicited enhanced interpersonal neural synchrony (INS) in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), linked to risk evaluation, and in the left superior and middle temporal gyri (l-STG, l-MTG), associated with semantic processing and value transformation. Machine learning analyses showed that trial-level INS predicted momentary optimization, while task-level INS robustly forecasted overall decision improvement. Together, these findings demonstrate that decision optimization emerges from dynamic brain-to-brain alignment in control and semantic networks—reflecting emotional sharing during positive advice and risk re-evaluation during negative advice. This study extending SIP theory to interactive decision-making and revealing how friend advice enhances decision quality and social well-being.

latest.title: Uncovering the unseen: a multi-scalar scoping review of short-term rentals and urban transformation
latest.abstract: Abstract This critical scoping review examines how short-term rentals (STRs) have transformed urban tourism research and proposes an integrated sustainability framework bridging economic, social, spatial, and governance dimensions. Building on PRISMA-ScR guidelines, it systematically maps 161 studies published between 2009 and 2025, identifying key patterns in the economic, environmental, spatial, and regulatory analysis of STRs. The findings reveal that while STRs foster tourism growth and local development, they also exacerbate housing unaffordability, gentrification, and overtourism. The literature remains dominated by data-driven methods, spatial analysis, econometric modelling, and machine learning yet exhibits strong geographic biases and limited integration across disciplines. Results highlight the growing professionalisation of hosts, the role of digital technologies in reshaping governance, and the urgent need for adaptive, sustainability-oriented regulation. By consolidating fragmented debates, this review offers a multidimensional synthesis that informs smart city planning, digital governance, and the pursuit of the Sustainable Development Goals in contemporary tourism destinations.

latest.title: How social exclusion shapes intertemporal choice: Self-control resources as the central bridge
latest.abstract: Intertemporal decision-making is crucial for social functioning, and social exclusion has been linked to a stronger preference for short-term gains. However, it remains unclear which psychological processes most proximally link exclusion to myopic intertemporal choice. We reanalyzed data from two complementary studies using psychological network analysis to examine the structural role of self-control resources (SCR) relative to trait self-control, impulsivity, and affect. In Experiment 1 ( N = 144), participants reported chronic social exclusion, SCR, trait self-control, impulsivity (BIS subscales), positive and negative affect, and completed a monetary intertemporal choice task. In Experiment 2 ( N = 96), acute exclusion was manipulated using the Cyberball paradigm. Across both experiments, the estimated networks retained a positive association between social exclusion and temporal discounting, whereas higher SCR was associated with more patient intertemporal choices. SCR had the largest absolute two-step bridge expected influence in both networks. Together, these findings highlight the association of momentary self-control resources with intertemporal choice in the context of social exclusion.

latest.title: EEG emotion recognition based on masked generative adversarial networks and neural architecture search
latest.abstract: Abstract EEG signals face challenges such as a scarcity of training data, significant individual variability, and difficulties in designing neural network architectures, which severely limit the performance and generalization capabilities of emotion recognition models. This paper proposes an EEG-based emotion recognition method that integrates masked generative adversarial data augmentation with personalized neural architecture search. We designed a data augmentation strategy using a frequency-domain feature-based stochastic electrode mask generative adversarial network, which effectively expands the training dataset and enhances the model’s generalization ability. Subsequently, we constructed a neural architecture search space tailored for EEG signals and employed a differentiable architecture search method to automatically discover the optimal network topology. Finally, a personalized architecture search strategy is employed to independently identify the classification network best suited to each subject’s unique EEG signal characteristics. Experimental validation on the public EEG emotion dataset DEAP achieved a classification accuracy of 98.64% on the Arousal dimension and 98.59% on the Valence dimension, significantly outperforming traditional machine learning methods and deep learning models with fixed architectures.

latest.title: Beyond cognitive ability, investigating the symmetrical and asymmetrical pathways of emotional and spiritual intelligence on academic achievement in higher education
latest.abstract: Abstract Higher education is typically explained in terms of cognitive ability (IQ) when linked to academic achievement. However, despite evidence of non-cognitive intelligence, specifically emotional and spiritual intelligence, its association with academic achievement remains underexplored. In Ghana, where spiritual orientation is strong, research on the relationship between emotional and spiritual intelligence and academic achievement among higher education students remains limited. This study used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) and Fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (FsQCA) to assess symmetrical and asymmetrical pathways. The study used a quantitative cross-sectional correlation design, drawing on data from 339 students across six colleges at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). PLS-SEM shows that emotional intelligence is significantly related to academic achievement (β = 0.344, p < .001) and spiritual intelligence (β = 0.661, p < .001). Spiritual intelligence is associated with academic achievement (β = 0.371, p < .001). The model explains 43. 4% of the variance in academic achievement. The FsQCA results showed that a single configuration was consistently associated with high academic achievement. The combined presence of both high emotional intelligence and spiritual intelligence had a consistency of 0.825 and a coverage of 0.766. Configurations in which one intelligence was high showed high consistency but low PRI consistency, so they were associated with both high and low achievement. The same findings appear in the robustness analysis. Therefore, emotional intelligence and spiritual intelligence appear to relate to achievement conjecturally, as co-occurring resources rather than independent or compe

latest.title: From rights to reach: a distributive policy framework bridging health literacy education, standardised medical sign language, and healthcare access for people with hearing loss in Thailand
latest.venue: International Journal for Equity in Health
latest.abstract: Abstract Background People with hearing loss in Thailand face persistent gaps between rights legislated under the Persons with Disabilities Empowerment Act B.E. 2550 and rights as experienced in everyday clinical encounters. Existing research rarely connects multi-region lived-experience evidence with concrete policy instruments. This study developed a distributive policy framework, anchored by a standardised medical sign language vocabulary and the MU-silentcare mobile application, to advance equitable health literacy and healthcare access. Methods A sequential explanatory mixed-methods, three-phase design was conducted across all seven regions of Thailand. Phase 1 used semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions with 138 purposively sampled stakeholders, including people with lived experience. Phase 2 administered a validated needs-assessment questionnaire (Cronbach’s α = 0.92; Item-Objective Congruence Index = 0.8) to 421 people with hearing loss recruited by cluster sampling; data were analysed using the modified Priority Needs Index (PNI modified ). Phase 3 combined a 14-day MU-silentcare mobile-application workshop, pre–post paired-samples t -tests on 453 participants, and policy-validation focus group discussions with 88 stakeholders. Results Phase 1 identified twelve issues across three domains: health literacy barriers, healthcare access and service-quality gaps, and systemic policy deficiencies. Phase 2 ranked healthcare access (PNI = − 0.50) and digital innovation (PNI = − 0.45) as top-priority needs; urgent-care response times received the highest importance rating ( M = 4.67/5). Phase 3 produced statistically significant improvements across all five health-literacy dimensions (overall t (452) = − 30.42, p < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 2.49); the largest e

latest.title: Bite-block effects on native s/ʃ and English r/l in child speakers of a language with/without this contrast
latest.abstract: Learning to produce non-native speech contrasts requires developing new phonological categories as well as new articulatory-perceptual mappings for these new categories. However, within the same speakers, it remains unclear how these new categories compare to contrasts that are already fully established in the native language. To examine potential differences between native and non-native sounds, we recorded Japanese children’s (8–12 years) productions of a non-native contrast (English /ɹ/−/l/, indexed by F3–F2) and a native contrast (/s/−/ʃ/, indexed by Center of Gravity). Recordings were done both under normal speaking conditions and under articulatory perturbation induced by a temporary bite-block while listening to a model. Children acoustically differentiated both contrasts under normal speaking conditions, but the two contrasts showed different developmental profiles: differentiation of the native contrast did not vary with age, whereas differentiation of the non-native contrast was significant only in older children. As expected, the bite-block manipulation reduced acoustic distinctness for both contrasts; however, susceptibility to this disruption was age-invariant for the native contrast but increased with age for the non-native contrast.

latest.title: Keywords
latest.abstract: It is such an honour to contribute to this special issue celebrating our amazing friend Carrie Menkel-Meadow. She has so many wonderful qualities, has written so many influential things, and has initiated and contributed to such important debates over many years in the field of dispute resolution that it is impossible to do her and her work justice in this essay. I therefore decided to organize my contribution around keywords that come to my mind when I think about Carrie and I will connect these to her work in separate entries as the body of my essay. I also weave into the text how she has influenced my work and continues to do so. The keywords are professional, feminist, mentor, generosity, and contemporary. This approach allows me to focus on how I understand her work to embody so many of her personal qualities. My methodological anchor here is Raymond Williams’s classic Keywords: A Vocabulary of Culture and Society (1976), in which he argues that language in not neutral and that many commonly used terms carry contested and often conflicting meanings depending on who uses them and in what context. Williams highlights the close relationship between language and social life. This is a helpful way to think about Carrie and her work on dispute resolution. Keywords: Carrie Menkel-Meadow; ADR; professional; mentor; feminist; engaged contemporary; generosity.

latest.title: Team members’ levels of expertise and team performance: The mediating role of collective learning and the moderating role of team psychological safety.
latest.venue: Group Dynamics Theory Research and Practice
latest.abstract: Objective: In knowledge-intensive teams, members’ expertise is a critical resource for performance. We therefore examine how members’ levels of expertise (expertness) influence team performance via collective learning. More specifically, we predict that high overall expertness generates more diverse and higher-quality ideas from which all members can learn. Such learning, in turn, enhances team performance by enabling members to integrate one another’s knowledge and jointly reflect on potential solutions. At the same time, variation in expertness can impair collective learning and, thereby, team performance by creating competence-based status hierarchies that discourage members from building on each other’s insights. In this last situation, we argue that team psychological safety can partly mitigate these detrimental effects by encouraging members to contribute to collective learning despite differences in perceived expertise. Method: We test our predictions in a sample of 76 interdependent student teams working on a complex four-week business simulation. Results: Our results partly support our predictions. Higher overall team expertness is positively associated with team performance, and collective learning partially mediates this relationship. Variation in expertness is negatively associated with performance through reduced collective learning, but only when psychological safety is low, while no such negative relationship exists in high psychologically safe teams. Conclusion: Our study suggests that teams might benefit from high average levels of expertise, while in low psychological safety teams the variation in members’ expertness can be detrimental for learning and ultimately performance.

latest.title: Experiencing the Queer Collective Through Time: Exploring Perceptions of Cultural and Historical Continuity Among LGBTQ + Emerging Adults
latest.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Using a pre-registered explanatory sequential mixed method design, we examined collective continuity, which until now has been studied in populations where its transmission is assumed to occur naturally via familial and cultural engagement. We examined collective continuity among LGBTQ+ emerging adults for whom access to the culture and history of the collective is not always available. METHOD STUDY 1: In Study 1, we examined associations across three measures of collective continuity and their associations with LGBTQ+ identity and well-being in college and community samples of emerging adults (N = 246). RESULTS STUDY 1: We found little association between the measures of collective continuity, modest associations between collective continuity and LGBTQ+ identity, and no relations between collective continuity and well-being. METHOD STUDY 2: Given the lack of empirical overlap in measures of collective continuity, in Study 2 we employed a qualitative interview approach (N = 8) to provide greater descriptive data on the phenomenon. RESULTS STUDY 2: These analyses revealed a lack of collective continuity and highlighted unique factors that facilitate or forestall the development of collective continuity among LGBTQ+ people, distinguishing this process from other groups (e.g., ethnic and national) in important ways. CONCLUSION: Together, these findings provide the opportunity for theoretical refinement and expansion of collective continuity.

latest.title: ปจจยทมอทธพลตอการยอมรบผลตภณฑสเตกไกคอลอนลกผสมซอสพรกไทยดำของผบรโภคในจงหวดพทลง
latest.venue: Warasan Wichai Lae Songserm Wichakan Kaset
authors: เสาวณีย์ เล็กบางพง
latest.abstract: This research aimed to study: 1) consumers’ personal characteristics; 2) consumer acceptance; 3) the level of importance of marketing mix factors; and 4) the factors influencing consumer acceptance of hybrid chicken steak with black pepper sauce in Phatthalung province. Data were collected from 400 respondents using questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations) and stepwise multiple regression analysis. The results were as follow: 1) The findings revealed that most consumers were female, aged 21–40 years, held a bachelor’s degree, were single, and worked in government agencies or state enterprises. 2) Consumers accepted it due to its appetizing aroma, pleasant taste, and deliciousness. Most preferred a price range of 50–100 Baht and a package weight of 101–200 grams, and showed an intention to continue purchasing the product in the future. 3) The overall marketing mix factors were rated at the highest level (\bar{x}=4.56), with product factors receiving the highest importance, followed by distribution channels, sales promotion, and price. 4) Age had a statistically significant negative effect on product acceptance at the 0.05 level, while product and distribution channel factors were the key determinants influencing consumer acceptance. These findings highlight consumers’ emphasis on product quality and accessibility. They may serve as guidelines for developing processed livestock products, adding value to agricultural products, and improving marketing strategies for community products in Phatthalung province.

latest.title: ปจจยทสงผลตอการจดการผลผลตยางพาราตามหลกสภาพทกษปา (FSC) ของสหกรณกองทนสวนยาง บานคลองชาง จำกด อำเภอควนเนยง จงหวดสงขลา
