hot.title: Third-party evaluators perceive AI as more compassionate than expert humans
hot.abstract: Empathy connects us but strains under demanding settings. This study explored how third parties evaluated AI-generated empathetic responses versus human responses in terms of compassion, responsiveness, and overall preference across four preregistered experiments. Participants (N = 556) read empathy prompts describing valenced personal experiences and compared the AI responses to select non-expert or expert humans. Results revealed that AI responses were preferred and rated as more compassionate compared to select human responders (Study 1). This pattern of results remained when author identity was made transparent (Study 2), when AI was compared to expert crisis responders (Study 3), and when author identity was disclosed to all participants (Study 4). Third parties perceived AI as being more responsive-conveying understanding, validation, and care-which partially explained AI's higher compassion ratings in Study 4. These findings suggest that AI has robust utility in contexts requiring empathetic interaction, with the potential to address the increasing need for empathy in supportive communication contexts.

hot.title: Real Earnings Management and ESG Performance in China: The Mediating Role of Corporate Innovations
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT This study addresses whether the positive consequences of corporate innovation can mitigate the negative repercussions of earning management practices on corporate sustainability. Specifically, it investigates the impact of real earning management (REM) practices on corporate environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance. Likewise, it explores the mediating role of corporate innovation inputs and outputs in this relationship. The study uses a sample of the A‐share listed firms in the Chinese stock market from 2011 to 2021. We measure REM activities as a comprehensive index of corporate abnormal cash flows, abnormal production costs and abnormal discretionary expenses. The Chinese firms' ESG performance is based on Huazheng's ESG rating. Corporate innovation is categorised into innovation input (i.e., R&D expenditure) and innovation output (i.e., patent applications). The study finds that REM practices inversely affect corporate ESG performance and its various pillars. Likewise, firms that engage in higher REM practices are less likely to allocate resources to innovation (i.e., lower R&D expenditure) and have a low innovation output (i.e., fewer patent applications). Nevertheless, firms with higher innovation input and/or higher innovation output exhibit higher ESG performance. Finally, the corporate innovation input and output mediate the relationship between REM practices and ESG performance, suggesting that the positive influence of innovation on ESG performance helps to mitigate the negative consequences of earnings management practices. These results underscore the significance of ethical financial practices and innovation‐driven strategies in enhancing corporate ESG performance.

hot.title: Digital Tokens and Platform Building
hot.abstract: Abstract We present a model rationalizing the economic value of digital tokens for launching peer-to-peer platforms. By using the blockchain to transparently distribute tokens before the platform launches, a token sale overcomes later coordination failures between the platform’s users. This result follows from forward induction reasoning, under which the costly and observable action of token acquisition credibly communicates the intent to participate on the platform. Our framework demonstrates the applications of digital tokens to entrepreneurship, and offers guidance for both practitioners and regulators.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Advancing Sustainable Practices in Electronic Customer Relationship Management
hot.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
hot.abstract: This paper examines the role of sustainability in determining organisational development and the manner in which it has become a necessity in conducting business. Thus, this research aims at determining the enhancement of sustainable practices in the e-CRM systems. Thus, using surveys and measuring certain e-CRM possibilities quantitatively, interviews and case analyses as qualitative data gathering, the research offers a systemic understanding of how e-CRM may be utilized to encourage sustainability. The preliminary results also reveal a high concern of the respondents towards the sustainability factor in e-CRM with the mean score of 4.2 and considerable awareness of the benefits like cost advantage measure with the calculated score of 4.5 mean. Companies are moderately challenged when it comes to cost and complexity (mean score 3.8) that restrict the integration of sustainability aspect in e-CRM systems, Nevertheless the implementation and planning of sustainability initiative in e-CRM system is high (current initiatives mean score 3.7, planned initiatives mean score 4.1). The qualitative results and cases reveal the ideas, experiences, examples, and quantifiable results, such as a 25% decrease in the usage of paper in the cases and a 30% decrease in energy use. These findings established that e-CRM strategies can be made sustainable, thereby creating improved communication between firms and their customers, whilst mitigating damages to the environment and supporting the long-term sustainability of organisations.

hot.title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
hot.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies sparked a rapid development of smartphone applications designed to help individuals experiencing mental health problems through an AI-powered chatbot agent. However, the safety of such agents when dealing with individuals experiencing a mental health crisis, including suicidal crisis, has not been evaluated. In this study, we assessed the ability of 29 AI-powered chatbot agents to respond to simulated suicidal risk scenarios. Application repositories were searched and the app descriptions screened in search of apps that claimed to be beneficial when experiencing mental distress and offered an AI-powered chatbot function. All agents were tested with a standardized set of prompts based on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale designed to simulate increasing suicidal risk. We assessed the responses according to pre-defined criteria based on the ability to provide emergency contact information and other factors. None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate. Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding. These findings raise concerns about the deployment of AI-powered chatbots in sensitive health contexts without proper clinical validation.

hot.title: AI capability and green innovation impact on sustainable performance: Moderating role of big data and knowledge management
Global, regional and national burden of depressive disorders and attributable risk factors, from 1990 to 2021: results from the 2021 Global Burden of Disease study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Depressive disorders pose a significant global public health challenge, yet evidence on their burden remains insufficient. AIMS: To report the global, regional and national burden of depressive disorders and their attributable risk factors from 1990 to 2021. METHODS: Data from the Global Burden of Disease 2021 were analyzed for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. We explored the age-standardised incidence, prevalence and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of depressive disorders by age, gender and sociodemographic index. RESULTS: In 2021, there were 357.44 million incident cases, 332.41 million prevalent cases and 56.33 million DALYs. Age-standardised rates for incidence, prevalence and DALYs were 4333.62, 4006.82 and 681.14 per 100 000 persons, with annual declines of 0.06%, 0.03% and 0.04%. Uganda, Greenland and Lesotho had the highest prevalence, while Spain, Mexico and Uruguay showed the largest increases. Greenland and Brunei Darussalam had the highest and lowest age-standardised DALYs rates, respectively. DALYs peaked in the 55-59 age group for men and 60-64 for women, with higher rates in women. Regionally, a U-shaped association was found between the sociodemographic index and DALYs rates. Population growth was the main driver for the increase in DALYs cases. Childhood maltreatment was the leading risk factor, with intimate partner violence affecting more females and childhood sexual abuse more males. CONCLUSIONS: Despite decreasing trends in incidence, prevalence and DALYs rates, absolute case numbers and age-standardised rates continue to increase for depressive disorders. Tackling childhood abuse and improving depressive disorder management are crucial to reducing future burdens.

hot.title: Can Generative AI Chatbots Emulate Human Connection? A Relationship Science Perspective
hot.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence capable of sustaining complex conversations has created a burgeoning market for companion chatbots promising social and emotional connection. The appeal of these products raises questions about whether chatbots can fulfill the functions of close relationships. Proponents argue that relationships with chatbots can be as meaningful as relationships between humans, whereas critics argue they are a dangerous distraction from genuine connections. This analysis applies theoretical tools from more than 50 years of research on close relationships to evaluate the extent to which human-chatbot interactions meet the definition of and fulfill the functions of close relationships. Interactions between humans and chatbots do possess some characteristic features of close relationships: Humans and chatbots can influence each other and engage in frequent and diverse conversations over time. Chatbots can be responsive in ways humans perceive as supportive, generating feelings of connection and opportunities for growth. Yet because chatbots make only superficial requests of their users, relationships with them cannot provide the benefits of negotiating with and sacrificing for a partner and may reinforce undesirable behaviors. Research that attends to the characteristics of users, chatbots, and their interactions will be crucial for identifying for whom these relationships will be beneficial or harmful.

hot.title: Generative artificial intelligence and internationalization green innovation: Roles of supply chain innovations and AI regulation for SMEs
Umbrella review of meta-analyses on the risk factors, protective factors, consequences and interventions of cyberbullying victimization
hot.abstract: The increasing prevalence of cyberbullying victimization has become a commonplace issue globally. Although research has explored various predictors and consequences of cyberbullying victimization, most focus on a narrow range of variables or contexts, highlighting the need to comprehensively review and synthesize the wealth of empirical findings. We conducted a systematic review of meta-analyses on cyberbullying victimization, incorporating 56 meta-analyses and 296 effect sizes (sample size range 421-1,136,080, sample size median 53,183; searched via EBSCOhost ERIC, EBSCOhost PsycInfo, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, 13 cyberbullying-related journals, Google Scholar and ProQuest Dissertations and Theses) to address the following critical questions: (1) What are the crucial sociodemographic and psychological profiles of cyberbullying victims? (2) What critical contextual and environmental factors are associated with cyberbullying victimization? (3) What are the key psychological and behavioural consequences of cyberbullying victimization? (4) How effective are existing interventions in mitigating impacts of cyberbullying? Included meta-analyses had to focus on cyberbullying victimization and report at least one predictor or consequence. A quality assessment was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Instrument for Systematic Reviews and Research Syntheses. Findings suggest that females, school-aged populations, traditional bullying victims and frequent internet users were more likely to be cyberbullied. Unregulated school environments and unsupportive parental relationships were also associated with increased cyberbullying victimization. Cyberbullying victimization was consistently associated with negative psychological outcomes, lower school perf

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.

latest.title: Selecting the right path: a framework for lead-time reduction in consumer goods supply chains
latest.venue: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management
latest.abstract: Purpose Consumer goods firms often face severe shortages caused by forecast inaccuracy, where a few variants become unexpected bestsellers and trigger costly stockouts. This article positions the choice of lead-time reduction initiatives as a crucial decision for enhancing responsiveness and mitigating shortages and frames this decision as a performance-management prioritization problem under uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach This work developed a pragmatic direction-selection framework grounded in a design science approach and applied in a case to guide managers in evaluating and prioritizing lead-time reduction initiatives. The framework integrates insights from the literature with feasibility-oriented evaluation criteria, applying the principles of multi-criteria decision analysis to assess initiatives in terms of expected return on investment (impact relative to effort) and implementation horizon. Findings The study offers a theory-based, empirically validated framework for identifying and planning lead time reduction initiatives in a context of hard-to-predict demand, making explicit a performance-management logic for prioritizing responsiveness initiatives. The case shows that initiatives with attractive expected impact–effort profiles are not necessarily robust priorities once implementation risk and sensitivity to assumptions are considered. Research limitations/implications The study advances performance-management research by reframing lead-time reduction as a decision problem under uncertainty and extending the focus from performance evaluation to intervention selection, translating dispersed responsiveness insights into a replicable prioritization logic, validated in a real case and supported by sensitivity checks. Practical implications The study pro

latest.title: Cultural Perceptions and Country Brands in the Global Art Market
latest.venue: Journal of arts, humanities and social science.
latest.abstract: This study bridges a gap in the literature concerning brand image, country of origin, and consumer perceptions of luxury products, specifically exploring the relatively unknown roles of geographic distance and sales transaction location. Utilizing the luxury art market, data encompassing 1726 transactions over thirty years was collected. The study examined the relationship between sale price and cultural indulgence, as well as the relationship between sale price and the distance between the sale location and the artist's home nation. The methodology employed three separate multiple linear regressions: a base model incorporating artist nationality, gender, and art history textbook representation; the base model plus cultural indulgence; and the base model plus geographical distance. Results indicated that auction houses located in more culturally indulgent areas command a premium, as do those located farther from the artist's home nation. The data is limited to two-dimensional artworks post-1750, included in prominent art history texts, and only includes auction sale price information. It is suggested that future researchers explore different art transactions or other industries like collectible luxury sports cars. The findings offer practical implications for practitioners in choosing sales office locations for premium goods and for brokers seeking higher prices by considering the cultural context of buyers and sellers. As globalization spreads, this study sheds light on cultural preferences using the luxury art market as a representative example, suggesting potential shifts in artwork preferences as cultural values evolve. This study contributes to the growing body of work in this field through our unique data set and results.

latest.title: Swap and Save: How a Button Shapes Lasting Online Grocery Shopping Behavior
latest.abstract: A well-documented phenomenon in the literature is that consumers exhibit persistence in their choices. Using data from the mineral water category on a price comparison platform that delivers real-time prompts of cheaper alternatives through "swap and save" buttons, this study examines whether and how these prompts influence persistent product choices in online grocery shopping. The findings reveal that shoppers who switched to an alternative product after receiving a prompt were 23.7 percentage points more likely to select that alternative product in subsequent visits, with this effect lasting for up to 10 shopping trips. Our analysis suggests that this sustained impact is driven not by long-term cost savings but by product discovery enabled through these real-time prompts.

latest.title: Friend advice influences mate choice through brain-to-brain synchrony and computational decision processes
latest.abstract: Abstract Individuals often rely on friends’ advice when facing ambiguous cues in mate-choice decisions, yet how such advice optimizes outcomes remains unclear. Using fNIRS hyperscanning, we simultaneously recorded neural and behavioral activity from 66 adult friend dyads (33 female dyads) during interactive advice phases. Computational modeling quantified the decision optimization parameter ( β ). It showed that only the bidirectional Social Information Processing (SIP) model—best fit behavioral data, indicating that optimization arises from reciprocal adaptation rather than one-way influence. Behaviorally, positive advice from in the relationship advisors increased mate-choice intention, whereas negative advice from single advisors more effectively promoted optimization. Both conditions elicited enhanced interpersonal neural synchrony (INS) in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), linked to risk evaluation, and in the left superior and middle temporal gyri (l-STG, l-MTG), associated with semantic processing and value transformation. Machine learning analyses showed that trial-level INS predicted momentary optimization, while task-level INS robustly forecasted overall decision improvement. Together, these findings demonstrate that decision optimization emerges from dynamic brain-to-brain alignment in control and semantic networks—reflecting emotional sharing during positive advice and risk re-evaluation during negative advice. This study extending SIP theory to interactive decision-making and revealing how friend advice enhances decision quality and social well-being.

latest.title: Uncovering the unseen: a multi-scalar scoping review of short-term rentals and urban transformation
latest.abstract: Abstract This critical scoping review examines how short-term rentals (STRs) have transformed urban tourism research and proposes an integrated sustainability framework bridging economic, social, spatial, and governance dimensions. Building on PRISMA-ScR guidelines, it systematically maps 161 studies published between 2009 and 2025, identifying key patterns in the economic, environmental, spatial, and regulatory analysis of STRs. The findings reveal that while STRs foster tourism growth and local development, they also exacerbate housing unaffordability, gentrification, and overtourism. The literature remains dominated by data-driven methods, spatial analysis, econometric modelling, and machine learning yet exhibits strong geographic biases and limited integration across disciplines. Results highlight the growing professionalisation of hosts, the role of digital technologies in reshaping governance, and the urgent need for adaptive, sustainability-oriented regulation. By consolidating fragmented debates, this review offers a multidimensional synthesis that informs smart city planning, digital governance, and the pursuit of the Sustainable Development Goals in contemporary tourism destinations.

latest.title: NAVIGATING DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION: THE INTERPLAY OF AMBIDEXTROUS LEADERSHIP, AGILITY, AND ORGANIZATIONAL RESILIENCE IN EMERGING MARKETS
latest.abstract: In an increasingly volatile, uncertain, complex, and ambiguous (VUCA) global environment, organizations face dual pressures to optimize existing operational capabilities while aggressively deploying digital innovations. This study investigates the structural mechanisms through which ambidextrous leadership drives sustainable organizational resilience via the mediating role of dynamic enterprise agility within emerging-market business enterprises. Anchored in the Dynamic Capabilities Framework and the Resource-Based View (RBV), we posit a structural model examining exploratory and exploitative leadership behaviors, process agility, market responsiveness, and multifaceted resilience (operational, financial, and strategic). Employing a cross-sectional, quantitative survey design, empirical data were gathered from N=412 senior executives, general managers, and chief technology officers across technology-enabled, manufacturing, and financial services firms in India. Structural Equation Modeling via Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM) was utilized to test the hypothesized paths and mediation effects. The results demonstrate that ambidextrous leadership exerts a statistically significant positive effect on organizational resilience (=0.342,p<0.001) and enterprise agility (=0.584,p<0.001). Furthermore, enterprise agility significantly mediates the relationship between ambidextrous leadership and organizational resilience (=0.286,p<0.001), accounting for a substantial indirect effect. The findings provide practical and theoretical frameworks for enterprise leaders navigating digital transformations under UGC-CARE and global research benchmark criteria, highlighting that structural ambidexterity without dynamic process adaptation yields suboptimal long-term stability.

latest.title: Experiencing the Queer Collective Through Time: Exploring Perceptions of Cultural and Historical Continuity Among LGBTQ + Emerging Adults
latest.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Using a pre-registered explanatory sequential mixed method design, we examined collective continuity, which until now has been studied in populations where its transmission is assumed to occur naturally via familial and cultural engagement. We examined collective continuity among LGBTQ+ emerging adults for whom access to the culture and history of the collective is not always available. METHOD STUDY 1: In Study 1, we examined associations across three measures of collective continuity and their associations with LGBTQ+ identity and well-being in college and community samples of emerging adults (N = 246). RESULTS STUDY 1: We found little association between the measures of collective continuity, modest associations between collective continuity and LGBTQ+ identity, and no relations between collective continuity and well-being. METHOD STUDY 2: Given the lack of empirical overlap in measures of collective continuity, in Study 2 we employed a qualitative interview approach (N = 8) to provide greater descriptive data on the phenomenon. RESULTS STUDY 2: These analyses revealed a lack of collective continuity and highlighted unique factors that facilitate or forestall the development of collective continuity among LGBTQ+ people, distinguishing this process from other groups (e.g., ethnic and national) in important ways. CONCLUSION: Together, these findings provide the opportunity for theoretical refinement and expansion of collective continuity.

latest.title: ปจจยทมอทธพลตอการยอมรบผลตภณฑสเตกไกคอลอนลกผสมซอสพรกไทยดำของผบรโภคในจงหวดพทลง
latest.venue: Warasan Wichai Lae Songserm Wichakan Kaset
authors: เสาวณีย์ เล็กบางพง
latest.abstract: This research aimed to study: 1) consumers’ personal characteristics; 2) consumer acceptance; 3) the level of importance of marketing mix factors; and 4) the factors influencing consumer acceptance of hybrid chicken steak with black pepper sauce in Phatthalung province. Data were collected from 400 respondents using questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations) and stepwise multiple regression analysis. The results were as follow: 1) The findings revealed that most consumers were female, aged 21–40 years, held a bachelor’s degree, were single, and worked in government agencies or state enterprises. 2) Consumers accepted it due to its appetizing aroma, pleasant taste, and deliciousness. Most preferred a price range of 50–100 Baht and a package weight of 101–200 grams, and showed an intention to continue purchasing the product in the future. 3) The overall marketing mix factors were rated at the highest level (\bar{x}=4.56), with product factors receiving the highest importance, followed by distribution channels, sales promotion, and price. 4) Age had a statistically significant negative effect on product acceptance at the 0.05 level, while product and distribution channel factors were the key determinants influencing consumer acceptance. These findings highlight consumers’ emphasis on product quality and accessibility. They may serve as guidelines for developing processed livestock products, adding value to agricultural products, and improving marketing strategies for community products in Phatthalung province.

latest.title: Модель синхронизированного продукта
latest.abstract: Представлена интегративная модель синхронизированного продукта для приборостроительных предприятий, позволяющая обосновать технические параметры инноваций в зависимости от потребительских ожиданий. Модель объединяет атрибутивный анализ Кано, функцию желательности Харрингтона и Scrum-планирование. Предложен коэффициент реверсивной адаптивности. Результаты позволяют снизить долю неуспешных запусков и сократить время вывода продукта на рынок

latest.title: The mediating effects of perceived quality and brand image between country-of-origin and purchase intention for refurbished iPhones
latest.abstract: This study investigates how Country-of-Origin influences Students’ Purchase Intention toward Refurbished iPhones, with Brand Image and Perceived Quality as mediating variables. A quantitative explanatory design was applied, involving 136 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS). The empirical results revealed that Country-of-Origin positively and significantly affected Brand Image, Perceived Quality, and purchase intention, both directly and indirectly. Brand Image and Perceived Quality were also confirmed to mediate the relationship between Country-of-Origin and purchase intention. These findings underscore the role of Country-of-Origin as a quality signal shaping consumer perceptions and purchase intentions regarding refurbished high-technology products, and contribute to a deeper understanding of consumer behavior while offering insights for marketing strategies in emerging markets.

latest.title: Analisis Strategi Penetapan Harga dalam Kegiatan Bisnis Online Group Order (GO) K-Pop dengan Nilai Kepercayaan di Media Sosial
latest.venue: Jurnal Semesta Ilmu Manajemen dan Ekonomi
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis strategi penetapan harga yang ditetapkan pada bisnis online group order (go) dan respon anggota komunitas di media sosial pada group order komunitas penggemar K-pop, khususnya group order by EL yang fokusnya pada grup Ateez. Peneliti menggunakan jenis penelitian kualitatif dengan pendekatan netnografi. Pengumpulan data dilakukan dengan observasi secara digital pada informasi kegiatan, interaksi, dan komunikasi, serta respon pada media sosial yaitu Line, X, dan e-commerce Shopee. Hasil penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa group order by EL tidak hanya fokus dalam strategi penetapan harga berdasarkan biaya namun juga penilaian anggota berupa nilai kepercayaan. Kegiatan transaksi yang terjadi dalam group order by EL terbukti dilakukan dilengkapi dengan bukti pendukung melibatkan respon anggota dengan kalimat positif dan emoticon yang menunjukkan kepuasan pada ulasan dan komentar dalam media sosial. Nilai kepercayaan di media sosial dibentuk dengan interaksi dan komunikasi terkait harga dan barang berupa percakapan hingga kesesuaian dalam penerimaan barang oleh anggota berupa ulasan dan testimoni yang diberikan.

latest.title: Analysis of ESG Performance, Profitability, Leverage, and Sustainable Growth on Firm Value Category
latest.abstract: Background: Firm value is an important indicator for assessing a company’s performance and prospects. Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors, profitability, leverage, and sustainable growth are expected to be related to firm value. However, the relationships among these factors need to be tested empirically using an appropriate statistical approach.Aim: This study aims to analyze the effects of ESG Performance, Return on Assets (ROA), Leverage Ratio, and Sustainable Growth on firm value category.Method: The study uses a quantitative approach with secondary data comprising 88 observations. The analysis applies binary logistic regression with the Enter method. The tests include the Omnibus Test, the Hosmer–Lemeshow Test, the Nagelkerke coefficient of determination, the classification table, and tests of the regression coefficients at the 5% significance level.Results: The results show that the regression model as a whole is not yet significant, with a Chi-square value of 5.071 and a significance of 0.280. A Nagelkerke R-squared of 0.075 indicates that the model’s explanatory power is relatively limited. The Hosmer–Lemeshow test yields a significance of 0.477, while the overall classification accuracy reaches 59.1%. Partially, ESG Performance, ROA, Leverage Ratio, and Sustainable Growth have significance values of 0.084, 0.364, 0.757, and 0.982, respectively. Accordingly, none of the independent variables is significant at the 5% level.Conclusion: The model provides insufficient statistical evidence of the effects of the four variables on firm value category.Implementation: Future research should consider adding relevant variables, reviewing how firm value is measured, and refining the model specification to improve explanatory power and predictive accuracy.

latest.title: Human and Organizational Drivers in Marketing-Logistics Collaboration and Supply Chain Performance: Evidence from Moroccan Mass Retailing
latest.abstract: Effective collaboration between manufacturers and retailers depends not only on operational integration but also on the human and organizational conditions that facilitate cross-functional coordination, communication, and joint decision-making. This study examines the relationship between marketing-logistics collaboration and supply chain performance in Moroccan mass retailing, with particular attention to information sharing quality and retail format. Drawing on survey data from 142 organizational observations, the study employs structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine the relationships among marketing-logistics collaboration, information sharing quality, and supply chain performance. CPFR and VMI are examined as specific collaborative practices through supplementary regression analyses rather than as separate constructs in the principal structural model. The findings indicate that marketing-logistics collaboration is positively associated with supply chain performance (β = 0.312, p < 0.001). Information sharing quality significantly mediates this relationship, with a significant indirect effect (β = 0.301, 95% CI [0.182, 0.443]). A multi-group comparison further indicates that the collaboration-performance relationship is stronger among hypermarkets than among supermarkets. These findings support a socio-organizational interpretation of marketing-logistics collaboration, in which human and organizational conditions provide an important theoretical foundation for coordinating people, information, responsibilities, and processes. The study contributes to research on interfunctional collaboration by providing empirical evidence from an emerging-market retail context and offers managerial implications for strengthening organizational coordination and information-shar

latest.title: Pengaruh promosi, harga, dan kualitas produk terhadap keputusan pembelian produk Scarlett Whitening di Jakarta
latest.abstract: The rapid development of the skincare industry in Indonesia has driven companies to understand the factors influencing consumer purchasing decisions. This study aims to analyze the effects of promotion, price, and product quality on the purchasing decisions of Scarlett Whitening products in Jakarta. A quantitative approach with a survey method was employed in this research. Data were gathered by distributing questionnaires to 140 respondents who are consumers of Scarlett Whitening in the Jakarta area. The sampling technique used was purposive sampling. The independent variables in this study include promotion, price, and product quality, while the dependent variable is the purchasing decision. The results of the study indicate that promotion, price, and product quality partially have a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions. In conclusion, promotion, price, and product quality are essential factors in influencing consumer purchasing decisions for Scarlett Whitening products in Jakarta. The findings of this study are expected to contribute to the development of marketing science.

latest.title: Service recovery as a relational and risk-based capability: Evidence from a freight forwarding firm
latest.abstract: This study examines how service recovery and operational risk management interact to develop competitive advantage and sustain customer loyalty in the business-to-business (B2B) freight forwarding industry. Employing a qualitative case study approach at PT Antillia Raya Logistics, Indonesia, the research draws on in-depth interviews with seven informants representing internal employees, customers, and vendors. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify patterns in service recovery practices, operational risk management, and business relationship development. The findings reveal that service recovery extends beyond corrective actions and operates through anticipatory communication, immediate problem resolution, and post-incident evaluation. Transparent communication, timely responses, customer education, and collaborative coordination with vendors play essential roles in maintaining trust during operational disruptions. Operational risk management is characterized by adaptive decision-making and experience-based practices, although formal risk documentation remains limited. The integration of service recovery and risk management facilitates organizational learning, strengthens operational responsiveness, and supports the prevention of recurring service failures. These integrated capabilities contribute to competitive advantage through service flexibility, reliability, and relationship quality rather than price-based differentiation alone. Customers and vendors perceive the firm's ability to manage uncertainty and resolve operational challenges as an important foundation for continued business relationships. This study contributes to service management literature by positioning service recovery as a relational and risk-integrated organizational capability
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: A Critical Analysis of the Legal and Ethical Challenges of Digital Lending Applications in Tanzania: A Doctrinal Analysis with Comparative Reference to Nigeria
latest.venue: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
latest.abstract: App-based digital lending has changed how Tanzanians borrow: a loan can be applied for, scored and disbursed on a handset within minutes, with an algorithm in place of the loan officer and the borrower’s phone data in place of collateral. This article asks whether Tanzanian law has kept pace with that change. Using doctrinal legal research, it examines the Microfinance Act, Cap 407, its 2019 Non-Deposit Taking Regulations, the Bank of Tanzania’s 2024 Guidance Note on Digital Lenders, the Financial Consumer Protection Regulations as amended in 2025, the 2025 Complaints Guidelines and the Personal Data Protection Act, Cap 44. The analysis draws on information asymmetry theory, the vulnerability theory of the consumer, informational self-determination and contextual integrity, and algorithmic accountability. It finds that the reforms of 2019 to 2025 have filled most literal silences in the law, but that the framework retains one legal gap, the absence of any standard for authenticating a guarantor’s consent on a mobile interface; four normative gaps, concerning informed guarantor consent, a flat penalty ceiling, the timing and comparability of cost disclosure, and weak explanation and reconsideration rights for automated decisions; two implementation gaps, in unaudited debt recovery and in-app redress; and one coordination gap among the Bank of Tanzania, the Personal Data Protection Commission and the newly designated self-regulatory associations. Nigeria’s move from interim guidelines to binding regulations, upheld by its Federal High Court in 2026, shows that converting guidance into enforceable rules is achievable. The article recommends a binding guarantor-verification standard, scaled penalties, pre-application cost disclosure, specified algorithmic disclosure, joint

latest.title: Moving the needle: overcoming systemic inertia to foster collective sustainability agency in organizations
latest.abstract: of dire ecological threats? We examine four systemic barriers behind collective inertia and argue that collective sustainability agency is necessary to overcome systemic inertia. Collective sustainability agency is the organizational capacity through which members transform individual sustainability concerns and responsibilities into coordinated collective influence over the practices, priorities, and structures that shape organizational sustainability outcomes. Unlike collective efficacy or organizational climate, which centers on shared beliefs about a group's capability, collective sustainability agency emphasizes the mobilization and exercise of that capability. Building on Wong et al.'s (2025) call to recognize employees as collective agents of systemic sustainability change, this perspective focuses on how organizations transform dispersed individual attitudes into shared responsibility, coordinated action, and collective influence capable of challenging organizational inertia.Environmental sustainability is defined as practices that minimize ecological harm, conserve natural resources, and support long-term ecological balance (Ones & Dilchert, 2012). While employees may personally endorse these principles, they often engage in environmentally harmful practices at work. This discrepancy occurs because organizational structures, incentives, leadership, and daily job demands shape human behavior far more powerfully than personal attitudes alone. Addressing the "attitude-behavior gap" requires more than changing individual minds-it demands the deliberate design of organizational systems that actively motivate, support, and mobilize sustainable choices (Kühner et al., 2025).Most organizations operate with economic success as their central priority. This creates a "gro

latest.title: The Impact of Customer Experience, Social Media Engagement and Customer Relationship Management on Repurchase Intention Mediated by Brand Love in The Fastfood Sector
latest.venue: International Journal of Management and Economics Invention
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT : This study aims to analyze the influence of customer experience, social media engagement, and customer relationship management on repurchase intention, with brand love serving as a mediating variable, within the fast-food industry in Indonesia. The study employs a quantitative approach using a survey method and a cross-sectional research design. Data were collected by distributing online questionnaires to fast-food consumers who have made a purchase and interacted with the respective brand’s social media. The final dataset consists of responses from 226 individuals. Data analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with the assistance of SmartPLS software. The results indicate that customer experience, social media engagement, and customer relationship management have a positive impact on both brand love and repurchase intention. Furthermore, brand love is also shown to have a positive effect on repurchase intention; consequently, all research hypotheses are supported.

latest.title: Strengthening post-earthquake logistical resilience: a fuzzy-optimization framework for emergency route planning in Türkiye
latest.abstract: Introduction Post-earthquake humanitarian routing is challenging because transportation conditions may be incomplete, uncertain, and direction-dependent. This study develops a reproducible fuzzy-optimization framework for emergency route planning in earthquake-affected regions of Türkiye. Methods Hexagonal fuzzy numbers (HFNs) are audited and processed using deterministic data-cleaning rules and a bounded ranking operator to obtain generalized cost units (GCUs). The resulting directed cost matrix is formulated as an asymmetric traveling salesman problem (ATSP). Held–Karp dynamic programming provides an exact benchmark, against which five metaheuristic algorithms—ant colony optimization (ACO), genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), cuckoo search algorithm (CSA), and bee colony optimization (BCO)—are evaluated. Independent computational runs, statistical tests, and heterogeneous disruption scenarios are used to assess solution quality and robustness. Results The framework provides a reproducible procedure for transforming fuzzy transportation data into a directed routing model. The exact solution serves as a reference for evaluating the metaheuristic algorithms, while run-level statistical comparisons and sensitivity experiments examine algorithm performance and the effects of transportation-cost increases, road closures, and node-level disruptions. Discussion The study demonstrates the value of explicit fuzzy-data auditing, bounded cost transformation, exact benchmarking, and reproducible computational experiments in emergency route planning. The proposed framework offers methodological support for post-earthquake logistics and can be extended to more comprehensive humanitarian routing models incorporating vehicle capacities, multiple vehicles, time-d

latest.title: How does perceptual distortion occur? Unraveling the interference mechanism of environmental color in the perception of original colors of cultural artifacts
latest.abstract: Color design within museum interiors constitutes a critical factor in shaping visitors’ perception of the authenticity of the original colors of cultural artifacts. Drawing upon multi-source qualitative data, including in-depth interviews and professional texts, this study employs grounded theory to exploratorily construct a theoretical model of the interference mechanism through which environmental colors affect the perception of artifact original colors. The findings reveal that optical-physical, cognitive-psychological, semantic-cultural, and emotional-value jointly constitute four core dimensions underlying such interference effects. At the physical level, environmental colors generate initial chromatic signals, which subsequently produce perceptual deviations through cognitive processing, trigger semantic reconstruction, and ultimately influence value judgments via emotional experiences. These dimensions may operate independently or synergistically, with cognitive processing and semantic association functioning as the central mediating pathways. The study provides an empirically grounded cognitive-psychological explanatory framework for understanding the dynamic relationship between environmental colors and the perception of artifact original colors, thereby offering theoretical support for museums to more effectively address the challenge of chromatic distortion in artifact display.

latest.title: FROM FINANCIAL LITERACY TO AI LITERACY: PREPARING COMMERCE STUDENTS FOR ALGORITHM-DRIVEN FINANCIAL DECISION-MAKING
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly visible in everyday financial activities. Students and consumers now encounter automated financial recommendations, digital investment platforms, personalised financial information and AI-based tools when making or evaluating financial choices. This changing environment raises an important question for Commerce education: is conventional financial literacy sufficient when financial information is increasingly mediated by algorithms? The present study examines financial literacy, AI literacy and awareness of ethical issues associated with AI-supported financial applications among Commerce students, and investigates their relationship with algorithmic financial decision quality. The study follows a descriptive and analytical research design and considers 250 student observations. Data were examined using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression. Four major constructs were considered in the analysis: financial literacy, AI literacy, ethical awareness and algorithmic financial decision quality. The findings show that financial literacy recorded the highest mean score (M = 3.56), while AI literacy recorded a comparatively lower mean score (M = 3.33). AI literacy demonstrated the strongest correlation with algorithmic financial decision quality (r = .705, p ≤ .01), followed by financial literacy (r = .623, p ≤ .01) and ethical awareness (r = .605, p ≤ .01). The regression model explained 67.2% of the variation in algorithmic financial decision quality. AI literacy emerged as the strongest predictor (β = .443), followed by financial literacy (β = .376) and ethical awareness (β = .199), with all three predictors statistically significant at p ≤ .001. The findings suggest that financial knowledge

latest.title: Generation Z Consumers’ Balance Between Online Shopping and Basic Needs in the Era of Digital Discounts
latest.venue: Journal of Management Entrepreneurship and Tourism
latest.abstract: The expansion of e-commerce and digital promotions has increased purchasing opportunities for Generation Z while raising concerns about balancing online shopping with essential needs. This study synthesized six empirical studies conducted in Indonesia to examine promotional purchasing influences, financial management factors, and implications for essential expenditure. A narrative literature review employed thematic synthesis of reported quantitative and qualitative findings without collecting primary data. Flash sales showed consistent positive associations with impulsive buying and purchase intention, while customer reviews were associated with purchase intention. Findings concerning fear of missing out and live shopping were less consistent across the reviewed studies. Qualitative evidence suggested that buy-now-pay-later facilities reduced the perceived immediate burden of payment and could obscure future obligations. Digital financial literacy was negatively associated with consumptive online shopping, while financial literacy and attitudes were positively associated with personal financial management. Financial socialization was linked to management indirectly through literacy rather than through a significant direct association. A conceptual framework and six propositions were developed to connect promotional stimuli, payment mechanisms, behavioral regulation, and essential-needs prioritization. Because none of the included studies directly measured essential-needs budget protection, the proposed relationships require future empirical testing using actual expenditure allocation, savings, and deferred-payment indicators.

latest.title: EFFECT OF ACCOUNTING TECHNOLOGY EXPENDITURE ON SHAREHOLDER’S RETURN (ROE) IN SELECTED CONSUMER GOODS MANUFACTURING FIRMS IN NIGERIA (2006-2025)
latest.venue: International Journal of Entrepreneurship and Forensic Management Research
latest.abstract: This study examined the impact of board monitoring mechanisms on return on asset in selected consumer goods manufacturing firms in Nigeria between 2006 and 2025. Using an ex-post facto research design, secondary data were analyzed from ten (10) firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group over a 20-year period, Panel Regression Analysis was used to examine the extent to which accounting technology expenditure influence return on equity. Fixed Regression showed that OPEX is negative (β -2.57E-05, p = 0.0000) and significant to Return on Equity (ROE). The study concluded that the model specified for the study adequately captured all variables and is of good fit. Accounting technology expenditure is significant to return on equity in selected consumer goods manufacturing firms in Nigeria. It recommends that firms should focus more on human capital investment, as it consistently improves shareholders’ returns. At the same time, management should carefully evaluate R&D and software investments to ensure that they are aligned with long-term profitability objectives rather than short-term financial pressure.

latest.title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
latest.abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

latest.title: Unveiling ESG ratings: corporate perspectives and institutionalisation dynamics
latest.venue: Sustainability Accounting Management and Policy Journal
latest.abstract: Purpose Environmental, social and governance (ESG) ratings have become a central mechanism for assessing, benchmarking and signalling corporate sustainability performance to financial investors. Yet, their widespread use persists despite ongoing criticism of their capacity to accurately reflect firms’ social and environmental contributions. This paper aims to examine this paradox from the perspective of rated companies, exploring why firms continue to engage with ESG ratings despite criticism of their effectiveness, even as investors remain their primary users. Drawing on institutional theory, the authors adopt this underexplored perspective and investigate how ESG ratings become institutionalised within organisations. Design/methodology/approach Based on abductive thematic analysis of 45 semi-structured interviews with sustainability executives from listed European firms, the authors develop a framework distinguishing between substantive and symbolic forms of ESG rating institutionalisation. Findings ESG rating adoption is shaped by institutional pressures and unfolds along a continuum. At one end, firms substantively integrate sustainability considerations into core operations; at the other, ESG ratings are used symbolically to secure external recognition and legitimacy. This study also highlights the risk of deinstitutionalisation if the limitations of ESG ratings remain unaddressed. Practical implications This study offers managers, investors and policymakers insights into navigating ESG pressures and strengthening the credibility of ESG frameworks while providing a diagnostic lens to distinguish symbolic compliance from substantive integration. latest.title: A Critical Review of Machine Learning Approaches for Credit Risk and Loan Default Prediction
latest.abstract: Approval or rejection of loans continues to be difficult decisions, and these decisions are becoming more difficult as financial markets continue to become globalised and interconnected. This review will look at research papers that examine how machine learning can assist with establishing more effective predictions of loan defaults in various lending environments, including U.S. traditional commercial banks (using both conventional and nonconventional forms of borrowing), P2P lending platforms (like Kiva and Lending Club), and mobile money networks in Sub-Saharan Africa. A common theme emerges across different studies referenced, which is that machine learning algorithms such as Gradient Boosting and XGBoost outperform traditional regression techniques (e.g., logistic regression) with a significant safety margin (generally 10%–15%), with 10% being the lowest margin of error for any study, and 30% being the highest margin of error across studies measuring AUC (area under the curve). The more significant findings are found when comparing average AUC measurement results to the AUC results of a dataset of behavioural signals (including factors related to how many times borrowers are late on payments, velocity of spends made by borrowers, and downloadable applications added to their mobile devices), all of these factors combined have produced much better predictive power than traditional financial ratios have produced on their own. latest.title: Selection of push/pull boundary in closed-loop supply chains and performance evaluation under dynamic factors
latest.venue: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences
latest.abstract: Context—In today’s competitive business environment, increasing sustainability concerns and environmental awareness have encouraged companies to adopt closed-loop supply chain (CLSC) structures. CLSCs involve not only the forward flow of products from suppliers to consumers but also the reverse flow, including the collection, recovery, recycling, and disposal of returned products. However, the reintegration of returned products into the supply chain increases network complexity, especially under dynamic market conditions. Therefore, effective management of forward and reverse supply chain processes is essential. In this context, the appropriate use of push and pull strategies and the correct positioning of the push–pull boundary constitute an important decision problem that directly affects supply chain performance.Objective—The aim of this study is to investigate the effect of different push–pull boundary positions on the performance of a CLSC. Specifically, the study aims to determine which service provider should be selected as the push–pull boundary to improve key performance indicators, including total profit, inventory holding cost, penalty cost, sales profit, and delivery lead time.Method—In this study, a simulation-based approach was employed to model the CLSC structure. Eight different simulation models were developed, each representing a different push–pull boundary position at various service providers within the supply chain network. To systematically analyze the factors affecting model performance, the Taguchi experimental design method was used. latest.title: Linking green entrepreneurship to green innovation: the mediating role of green entrepreneurial self-efficacy
latest.venue: African Journal of Economic and Management Studies
latest.abstract: Purpose In line with the United Nations 2030 Agenda, environmental sustainability has become a prominent concept in academic discourse. Due to its vast natural resources, Africa is well-positioned to become a global leader in green business. However, with a growing small and medium-sized enterprise (SME)population in Africa, empirical evidence on SME sustainability efforts remains limited. For this reason, this research examined the mediation effect of green entrepreneurial self-efficacy on the relationship between green entrepreneurship and green innovation in Zimbabwean manufacturing SMEs. Design/methodology/approach The data were analysed using SmartPLS 4 from a randomly selected sample of 370 managers. Findings The results showed that while green entrepreneurship strongly influenced green innovation, green entrepreneurial self-efficacy partially mediated the relationship between the two variables. Originality/value The study contributes context-specific evidence from an African economy, addressing the limited representation of developing markets in green innovation research. In environments characterised by institutional constraints and resource scarcity, identifying self-efficacy as an enabling mechanism provides novel insight into how firms can stimulate green innovation despite structural limitations. The findings, therefore, enrich both theory and practice by integrating strategic and psychological perspectives within the African economic context.

latest.title: Do auditors respond to clients’ consumer complaints? Evidence from audit fees
latest.abstract: This study investigates whether auditors incorporate consumer complaints into audit risk assessments and pricing decisions. Drawing on data from the Black Cat Complaint Platform, a leading online consumer complaint platform in China, evidence shows that firms with more complaints pay significantly higher audit fees. The effect is more pronounced among non-Big 4 auditors and auditors with lower industry expertise. Audit fees are also higher when complaints involve larger monetary amounts or remain unresolved, and both product-related and experience-related complaints are positively associated with audit fees. In addition, the evidence suggests that auditors expend more effort in response to consumer complaints.

latest.title: Pengaruh Perencanaan Pajak, Leverage, dan Ukuran Perusahaan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan
latest.abstract: The inconsistent fluctuations in corporate value within the consumer non-cyclical sector—which inherently operates in fulfilling society's primary daily needs—serve as the foundational anomaly driving this study. This research aims to evaluate the impact of tax planning, leverage ratio, and firm size on corporate market value. Employing a quantitative approach with an associative design, this study utilizes secondary data derived from the financial statements of issuers listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) spanning the 2020–2024 period. By applying a purposive sampling technique, a sample of 43 companies was obtained, yielding a total pooling data of 215 observations, which were subsequently analyzed using panel data regression via EViews 13 software. The simultaneous test results demonstrate that the combination of tax planning, leverage, and firm size significantly influences firm value. Separately, however, the partial analysis reveals that only the leverage variable plays a significant role in determining corporate value, whereas tax planning and firm size exhibit no functional or significant relationship in the consumer non-cyclical sector during the observation period.

latest.title: Metacognitive Awareness as a Predictor of Reasoning Among SS I Economics Students in Enugu Education Zone, Enugu State, Nigeria
latest.abstract: This study examined metacognitive awareness as a predictor of economic reasoning among SS I Economics students in Enugu Education Zone, Enugu State, Nigeria. The study was guided by three research questions and two null hypotheses tested at the 0.05 level of significance. A predictive correlational research design was adopted. A multistage sampling procedure was used to select 357 SS I Economics students from a population of 5,195 students. The two instruments, the Metacognitive Awareness Questionnaire (MAQ) and the Economic Reasoning Test (ERT), were developed by the researcher. Three experts, comprising one expert in Economics Education and two experts in Measurement and Evaluation, validated the instruments based on relevance, clarity, appropriateness, adequacy of content coverage, and alignment with the objectives of the study. Internal consistency reliability was determined using the psych package in R statistical software, yielding reliability coefficients of 0.79 for the MAQ and 0.73 for the ERT. Data were analysed using mean, standard deviation, Pearson Product-Moment Correlation Coefficient, and multiple linear regression. The findings showed that students obtained a mean metacognitive awareness score of 2.44 (SD = 0.87) and a mean economic reasoning score of 16.83 (SD = 6.76). Metacognitive awareness had a positive and statistically significant relationship with economic reasoning, r(355) = .385, p < .001. Furthermore, planning, monitoring, and evaluation jointly predicted economic reasoning significantly, F(3, 353) = 20.62, p < .001, accounting for 14.9% of the variance in economic reasoning. However, none of the three dimensions made a statistically significant unique contribution when considered simultaneously. The study recommends that Economics teachers s

latest.title: E-Commerce in Agribusiness: Transforming Agricultural Input and Food Markets in Emerging Economies
latest.venue: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports
latest.abstract: E-commerce is altering the organisation of agricultural input distribution, farm-output marketing and urban food procurement across emerging economies. Yet the proposition that digital platforms necessarily reduce intermediation, raise farm incomes and improve food-system efficiency is not established by the evidence as a whole. This critical narrative review examines transaction-based digital marketplaces, electronic agricultural auctions, input e-stores, digitally mediated procurement and consumer-facing food platforms, with attention to China, India and sub-Saharan Africa. Peer-reviewed empirical studies, reviews and selected methodological sources were purposively assessed for identification strategy, outcome validity, external relevance and conflicting results. The literature indicates that electronic commerce can broaden market reach, enable comparison of input offers, reorganise procurement and support sales continuity during disruptions. The magnitude and distribution of these benefits depend on logistics, verification of goods, intermediary services, buyer competition, digital capabilities and platform rules. A randomised expansion study in rural China found limited producer-income effects, whereas several observational and quasi-experimental studies report gains for selected participants; recent evidence also indicates diminishing returns, unequal benefits and adverse spillovers on offline farmers. Indian electronic agricultural markets demonstrate that price transparency does not guarantee effective cross-market competition, while African evidence documents both opportunities for input dealers and persistent fulfilment and trust constraints. latest.title: Pengaruh Citra Merek, Pemasaran Media Sosial, dan Kepercayaan Merek terhadap Niat Pembelian
latest.venue: Journal of Management and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of brand image, social media marketing, and brand trust on the purchase intention of consumers of Camille Beauty products in Semarang City. This study employed a quantitative approach. The population consisted of all consumers of Camille Beauty products in Semarang City; however, the exact number of the population was unknown. The sample size was determined based on Roscoe's theory, resulting in 126 respondents. The sampling technique used was purposive sampling, with the criteria that respondents were residents of Semarang City and had used Camille Beauty products for at least one month. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using SPSS version 22. The data analysis techniques included respondent descriptive analysis, variable descriptive analysis, validity testing, reliability testing, the F-test, the coefficient of determination (R²) test, and the t-test. The results indicate that brand image, social media marketing, and brand trust have a positive and significant effect on the purchase intention of consumers of Camille Beauty products in Semarang City.

Fixed Regression also showed that Board Gender Diversity (BOGD) is positive and significant to Return on Asset (β = 0.047967, p = 0.0000). Board IT Competence exerted strong positive and significant effect on ROA (β = 0.126435, p = 0.0000). CEO Duality has positive and significant effect on ROA (β = 0.026689, p = 0.0000). The study concluded that the model specified for the study adequately captured all variables and is of good fit. Accounting technology expenditure is significant to return on equity in selected consumer goods manufacturing firms in Nigeria. It recommends that firms should focus more on human capital investment, as it consistently improves shareholders’ returns. At the same time, management should carefully evaluate R&D and software investments to ensure that they are aligned with long-term profitability objectives rather than short-term financial pressure.

latest.title: Mindful eating and sustainable dining behaviors: a psychological resources perspective
latest.venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the psychological mechanisms linking mindful eating (ME) with sustainable dining behaviors in restaurant contexts. Drawing on Hunecke’s psychological resources perspective for sustainable lifestyles, the study explains how self- and other-focused psychological resources are associated with green restaurant selection and dining-out leftover prevention across pre- and post-consumption stages. Design/methodology/approach A dual-pathway sequential mediation model was developed and tested using data from 611 Taiwanese consumers who had dined out within the previous three months. Structural equation modeling was used to examine the hypothesized paths and mediating relationships. Findings The findings support two sequential pathways linking ME to sustainable dining outcomes. The self-focused pathway operates through self-compassion and subjective vitality, whereas the other-focused pathway operates through altruistic values and food gratitude. Together, these complementary psychological resources connect ME with green restaurant selection and dining-out leftover prevention across pre- and post-consumption stages. Research limitations/implications The findings advance sustainable hospitality research by highlighting psychological resources as mechanisms through which ME is associated with sustainable dining behaviors. From a practical perspective, mindful dining experiences may encourage self-focused resources, while appreciative communication may strengthen altruistic concern and food gratitude. Originality/value This study extends Hunecke’s psychological resources perspective to hospitality by specifying complementary self- and other-focused pathways. It advances research on the intention–behavior gap and broadens ME as a dining-specific ant

latest.title: Profitability, Leverage, and ESG Disclosure as Determinants of Firm Value: Evidence from Indonesia's ESGL Index
latest.abstract: This study investigates the effects of profitability, leverage, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure on firm value among companies included in Indonesia's ESG Leaders (ESGL) Index, focusing on the energy and raw materials sectors during the 2020-2024 period. These sectors play a strategic role in the Indonesian economy while facing increasing pressure to adopt sustainable business practices. Using purposive sampling, this study obtained 110 firm-year observations. Panel data regression analysis was employed using e-views 12 to examine the relationship between the research variables. The findings reveal that profitability and leverage have a positive and significant effect on firm value, whereas ESG disclosure does not significantly influence firm value. These results indicate that investors continue to place greater emphasis on financial performance than sustainability disclosure when evaluating firms in these sectors. The novelty of this study lies in its focus on companies included in the ESGL index, which represent firms expected to demonstrate stronger sustainability practices than conventional listed companies. The findings provide practical implications for corporate managers, investors, and regulators by emphasizing the importance of balancing financial performance with credible sustainability disclosure to enhance long-term firm value. latest.title: From awe to emotional brand attachment: a cognitive appraisal perspective on VR brand experiences
latest.abstract: Purpose Prior research on awe in relation to virtual reality (VR) has treated awe as a response to technological stimuli, leaving the consumer appraisals through which awe arises underexplored. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory, this paper aims to address this gap by investigating whether aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals of a VR brand experience predict awe and whether awe mediates the relationships between these appraisals and emotional brand attachment. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via a survey of 334 Generation Z participants who experienced an in-person brand encounter via a VR headset and were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in LISREL. Findings Aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals positively predict awe, which, in turn, predicts emotional brand attachment. Awe also mediates the relationships between each of the three appraisal and emotional brand attachment. Originality/value At the intersection of the cognitive psychology of VR and emotional branding, this paper reframes the origins of awe in VR brand experiences, shifting from a stimulus-centred to an appraisal-centred account. It also identifies aesthetic, sensory and content appraisals as the experiential predictors of awe and extends emotional branding to self-transcendent emotions by showing how awe translates experiential appraisals into emotional brand attachment.

latest.title: An Analysis of the Factors Influencing Consumer Behavior in the Purchase of Food Products
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Management and Accounting
latest.abstract: Food purchasing behavior reflects interactions among consumer characteristics, psychological evaluations, marketing stimuli, and purchasing circumstances. This study aimed to identify, classify, and synthesize factors influencing consumer behavior in purchasing food products. A descriptive qualitative literature review was conducted using secondary data from journal articles, academic books, and previous research reports. The original review covered literature published between 1991 and 2023, with findings analyzed through thematic synthesis and comparative interpretation. Six determinant categories were identified: cultural, social, personal, psychological, marketing-mix, and situational factors. Comparative evidence revealed differences in the dominant factors across food categories and purchasing environments. Price was dominant in instant noodle purchasing, with a reported influence of 12.15%, while psychological factors were most influential in steamed layer cake purchasing. Product attributes were most decisive in a selected food outlet, whereas purchasing time was the strongest factor in a fast-food restaurant setting. These differences indicated that purchasing behavior depended on product characteristics, consumer evaluations, and transaction circumstances rather than a universally dominant determinant. The study contributes an integrated conceptual framework for interpreting heterogeneous purchasing influences and supports context-sensitive marketing strategies. Differences in research designs and measurements limit direct statistical comparisons and causal generalization.

latest.title: ESG Performance and Its Disclosures: Evidence on Corporate Profitability from ASEAN-5 Manufacturing Firms
latest.venue: MARGINAL JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING GENERAL FINANCE AND INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC ISSUES
latest.abstract: Growing pressure on firms to demonstrate sustainability has made ESG a central corporate concern, yet evidence on its financial consequences remains mixed, particularly in emerging ASEAN markets. Listed manufacturers across the ASEAN-5 countries are the subject here, with attention to whether ESG performance links to their financial results. The relationship examined in the study is how ROA is affected by ESG performance and its three subcomponents including Environmental, Social, and Governance Disclosure Scores. Using a quantitative approach to explanatory research design, the study uses panel data collected from 744 firm-year observations of manufacturing firms in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Philippines, and Thailand in the period 2023-2025. Regarding the overall ESG Score, the study finds no support for the hypothesis, as its effect on ROA is negative and statistically significant. Each of the three disclosure scores, namely Environmental, Social, and Governance, behaves differently, producing a positive and statistically significant effect on ROA. What this suggests is that high ESG performance may not necessarily yield high financial performance, while every individual ESG dimension can still affect ROA positively.

hot.title: Exploring automation bias in human–AI collaboration: a review and implications for explainable AI
hot.abstract: Abstract As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, law, and public administration, automation bias (AB)—the tendency to over-rely on automated recommendations—has emerged as a critical challenge in human–AI collaboration. While previous reviews have examined AB in traditional computer-assisted decision-making, research on its implications in modern AI-driven work environments remains limited. To address this gap, this research systematically investigates how AB manifests in these settings and the cognitive mechanisms that influence it. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we reviewed 35 peer-reviewed studies from SCOPUS, ScienceDirect, PubMed, and Google Scholar. The included literature, published between January 2015 and April 2025, spans fields such as cognitive psychology, human factors engineering, human–computer interaction, and neuroscience, providing an interdisciplinary foundation for our analysis. Traditional perspectives attribute AB to over-trust in automation or attentional constraints, resulting in users perceiving AI-generated outputs as reliable. However, our review presents a more nuanced view. While confirming some prior findings, it also sheds light on additional interacting factors such as, AI literacy, level of professional expertise, cognitive profile, developmental trust dynamics, task verification demands, and explanation complexity. Notably, although Explainable AI (XAI) and transparency mechanisms are designed to mitigate AB, overly technical, cognitively demanding, or even simplistic explanations may inadvertently reinforce misplaced trust, especially among less experienced professionals with low AI literacy.
