latest.title: Operational strategies for managing purchase decisions in festival shopping: Analyzing the role of fear of missing out (FOMO) in the digital transformation era
latest.venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
latest.abstract: Purpose: For most consumers who experience fear of missing out, regret related to falling behind trends outweighs regret related to financial costs. In fact, the intensity of the attraction created through fear of missing out is positively correlated with impulse buying, which potentially reduces self-control during shopping activities. Hence, fear of missing out is considered a psychological disorder that affects the mental health of the individual. Therefore, this study aims to explain the reactive-behavioral outcomes (e.g., impulsive buying decisions) by emphasizing the perceptual drivers of the 'Fear Of Missing Out' (FOMO) phenomenon within the context of festival shopping opportunities in the digital transformation era.Methodology: This study is a basic-applied research based on its purpose and a mixed research based on its research strategy. The qualitative strategy used in the first stage of the research is grounded theory and the quantitative strategies used in this survey-correlational research. The qualitative participants included marketing and sales consultants as well as professors of business, marketing, and e-commerce, 10 of whom were selected as participants through non-probability judgmental sampling. The statistical population of the quantitative part of the study is people who visited various festivals and made various purchases.The sampling method in the quantitative section was random, and the sample size was determined to be 221 participants based on relationship of Cohen. To prevent sample attrition, about 240 questionnaires were distributed in this study and 229 questionnaires were returned to the researcher.Findings: The results showed that perceptual drivers (positive customer perception of the brand, deceptive advertising, customer experience,

latest.title: Brand Love, Customer Brand Engagement, and Brand Pride as Predictors of Brand Defense among Indonesian iPhone 17 Series Users
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines how brand love, customer brand engagement, brand pride, and regulatory focus are associated with brand defense among Indonesian iPhone 17 Series users. Cross-sectional data from 350 respondents recruited through purposive sampling were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. Brand love was positively associated with customer brand engagement, which was positively associated with brand defense. The direct association between brand love and brand defense was nonsignificant, whereas the indirect association through customer brand engagement was significant, supporting a pattern of indirect-only mediation. Brand pride also showed a positive direct association with brand defense. Promotion focus and prevention focus did not significantly moderate either the brand love-engagement association or the corresponding indirect association, indicating that regulatory focus did not function as a boundary condition in this context. Together, the proposed predictors explained 50.9% of the variance in brand defense. The findings extend the consumer-brand relationship perspective by identifying customer brand engagement as a relational pathway linking brand love with brand defense and brand pride as a complementary identity-related predictor. These findings provide insight into why consumers defend identity-relevant premium brands and highlight engagement and brand pride as important considerations for brand management.

latest.title: Impact of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love: Evidence from the Luxury Fashion Industry in Egypt
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of Packaging Attributes on Brand Love in the luxury fashion industry in Egypt, building upon literature on the effect of packaging attributes as a multidimensional concept that extends beyond its protective function to include visual, functional, environmental, and experiential attributes on brand love towards luxury fashion brands. This study is theoretically grounded in the combination of the Cue Utilization Theory, Signaling Theory, and Attachment Theory to examine how packaging attributes shape consumers' emotional responses and strengthen brand love. This research employed a quantitative approach, using an online questionnaire to collect data from 440 luxury fashion consumers via River sampling, and the relationships were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics software using Multiple linear regression. Results demonstrated that packaging attributes have significant impact on brand love, with each packaging attribute contributing differently to brand love; thereby, visual, functional, and experiential packaging attributes positively impact brand love, whereas environmental packaging attributes were not a statistically significant predictor of brand love. Findings contribute evidence from the Egyptian market, offering practical implications for luxury fashion brands and marketers, highlighting packaging as a strategic tool to strengthen consumers’ emotional attachment to the brand, and supporting competitiveness in the luxury fashion market.

latest.title: The Indonesian hedonic trap: Exploring consumer attitudes and legal risks in counterfeit luxury purchases
latest.abstract: The relationship between hedonism, the impression of legal danger, and customer attitudes about luxury fashion counterfeit products is explored in this study. Data was collected from 385 respondents in East Java, Indonesia, using multistage sampling and using structural equation modelling (SEM) analysis, with a focus on those who had previously purchased counterfeit products. The results show that consumer perceives and intention to buy for counterfeit luxury products are positively influenced by hedonism. However, this effect is considerably moderated by legal risk perception, which lowers intention to buy among individuals who are legally risk orientated. This study provides an overview of the consumption of counterfeit products by integrating legal (risk perception) and psychological (hedonism) perspectives. Further psychological and socioeconomic elements influencing the purchase of counterfeit products should be investigated in future studies. These results can be used by policymakers and brand owners to create effective consumer education initiatives and legal enforcement strategies to minimise the use of counterfeit products.

latest.title: Why Parent Brand Trust Is Not Enough? Entitativity, Perceived Quality, and Perceived Risk in Life Insurance Trust Transfer
latest.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
latest.abstract: This research investigates the mechanisms by which trust transfers from prominent parent brands to their affiliated life insurance sub-brands in Indonesia. While consumers may trust established conglomerates, this trust may not automatically translate into credibility for their life insurance extensions. The study examines how entitativity, operationalized as perceived similarity and brand tie, together with perceived quality and perceived risk, facilitate sub-brand trust and behavioral intention. Using a quantitative survey approach, data from 483 valid respondents were evaluated via Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The analysis identified a significant but weak direct effect of parent brand trust on sub-brand trust. This shows that a reputable parent brand may help establish initial trust, but cannot substitute for the consumer’s own evaluation of the life insurance sub-brand. Clearer parent–sub-brand unity, higher perceived quality, and lower perceived risk promote trust in the sub-brand, which is a significant driver of behavioral intention. This data was limited to only Indonesian respondents. This study contributes to trust transfer literature by conceptualizing entitativity as a higher-order construct in hierarchical brand relationships, offering practical guidance for life insurance companies to leverage parent brand equity through service excellence and clearer brand integration.

latest.title: Innovative Operation Ideas of Guangxi Agricultural Assistance Platform from a Demand-Side Orientation: A Case Study of "Mang Xiaozhong"
latest.abstract: In recent years, with the deep penetration of the digital economy into rural areas and the rapid development of agricultural e-commerce in Guangxi, the demand-side oriented agricultural assistance model has emerged as an innovative form of agricultural product circulation. In response to problems in the upward distribution of characteristic agricultural products in Guangxi—including disconnection between production and marketing, high loss in circulation links, difficulties in brand transformation, and seasonal capital shortage at the production end—the "Mang Xiaozhong" platform constructs four interconnected operation strategies: customized pre-sale, two-way exchange among production areas, rule-based trust design, and consumer-side pre-purchase crowdfunding. These strategies adapt to the industrial reality of decentralized smallholder production and staggered listing of multiple categories in Guangxi. The research shows that the demand-side oriented, asset-light third-party service model can address the practical bottlenecks of county-level agricultural assistance e-commerce in Guangxi, and has reference value for the construction of similar platforms.

latest.title: Pengaruh Analisis Brand Identity dan Brand Image terhadap Brand Awareness Produk iPhone di Kalangan Generasi Z (Studi pada Mahasiswa FEB Universitas Pancasila)
latest.abstract: This research aims to determine the influence of Brand Identity and Brand Image on Brand Awareness of iPhone products among Generation Z. The respondents in this study were iPhone users from the Faculty of Economics and Business at Universitas Pancasila. The sampling method used was non-probability sampling with a purposive sampling technique, and the total sample tested consisted of 100 respondents. The data collection instrument used was a questionnaire distributed through Google Forms. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression analysis, classical assumption tests, hypothesis testing, and processed using SPSS 22. The results of the study indicate that Brand Identity has a positive effect on Brand Awareness, Brand Image has a positive effect on Brand Awareness, and Brand Identity and Brand Image simultaneously have a positive effect on Brand Awareness.

latest.title: THE MEDIATING FUNCTION OF PERCEIVED CREDIBILITY IN THE IMPACT OF SUSTAINABILITY REPORT QUALITY ON INVESTOR TRUST
latest.venue: Financial and credit activity problems of theory and practice
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationship between investor trust and perceived sustainability reporting quality, paying special attention to the mediating function of perceived credibility. The study creates an integrated framework based on signaling theory and information asymmetry theory to explain how investors understand sustainability disclosures and convert their evaluations into trust in reporting firms. In particular, the study looks at the direct connections between investor trust, perceived sustainability reporting quality, and perceived credibility. It also evaluates whether credibility may explain the relationship between investor confidence and reporting quality. Individual investors and representatives of institutional investors in Vietnam provided survey data. With investor type included as a control variable and bootstrapping used to assess the mediating link, covariance-based structural equation modeling was used to analyze the suggested correlations. The results show that investor trust and perceived credibility are positively correlated with higher perceived sustainability reporting quality. Additionally, investor trust and perceived credibility are positively correlated, and the relationship between reporting quality and trust is partially mediated by perceived credibility. These results imply that sustainability disclosures boost investor confidence by increasing the credibility that investors assign to company information in addition to its perceived quality. The scientific uniqueness of the study is the identification of perceived credibility as a unique explanatory mechanism that links investor trust in an emerging capital market with sustainability reporting quality. The study expands on current debates on sustainability disclosure and investor decis

latest.title: Customer Focus Program (CFP) in a Regulation-Constrained Category: A Field-Based Qualitative Study of Distribution and Merchandising Execution in India's Organized Cigarette Trade
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose: In categories where mass advertising and open promotion are legally prohibited, the sales and distribution system becomes the main route through which a firm can express customer orientation. This paper examines how a Customer Focus Program (CFC) operates at the point of sale in the cigarette sales and distribution network of a large Indian fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) organisation. Design/methodology/approach: The study is a descriptive, qualitative, field-observation-based case study conducted over a two-month period (15 May to 15 July 2026) in the Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) territory of Maharashtra. Observations were recorded during accompanied market visits across convenience, grocery, wholesale, sub-wholesale, stockist, moped and van direct-selling channels, using a four-field recording format (objective, activity observed, practical observation, relevance to customer focus). Observations were mapped to an Availability–Visibility–Freshness (AVF) framework and to an eight-step CFC field-execution flow. Findings: Four findings emerge. (1) Availability is produced by layered, complementary coverage formats rather than by any single actor. (2) Effective execution must be segment-aware and margin-aware, because retailers' stocking and promotion choices respond jointly to product segment and trade pricing structure. (3) Merchandising and planogram discipline is the primary visibility lever when above-the-line promotion is unavailable. (4) The salesman–retailer relationship is the mechanism that sustains the program. Originality/value: The paper offers a field-grounded account of customer orientation as enacted at the last mile in a heavily regulated category, an area where the marketing-channels and customer-orientation literatures rarely meet. It proposes

latest.title: Cross-Sectoral Patterns of Circular Consumption Behaviours: Evidence from R-Strategies
latest.abstract: Transitioning to a circular economy requires not only systemic and technological change but also consumer engagement in circular practices. While circular economy research has extensively examined R-strategy frameworks, existing studies have largely focused on organisational and supply-side perspectives, with limited attention to how these strategies are reflected in consumer behaviour across product domains and how such behaviours can be addressed through policy. This study investigates reported circular consumption behaviour across three key product sectors: household appliances, consumer electronics and apparel. Drawing on data from a survey of 1,000 adult consumers in Poland, the analysis focuses on seven consumer-relevant R-strategies derived from the wider 9R framework: Refuse, Rethink, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Repurpose and Recycle. The study examines sector-specific reported prevalence, cross-sectoral reach and associations between analogous behaviours across sectors. The results show that prolonged product use, mapped to Rethink in this study, is the most commonly reported practice and has the broadest cross-sectoral reach. Refuse and Repurpose show lower prevalence and narrower cross-sectoral reach. At the same time, analogous circular practices are positively associated across product sectors, indicating that circular consumption is sector-sensitive but partly interconnected. Exploratory CART analyses further indicate that these pairwise associations are accompanied by hierarchical and subgroup-specific cross-sectoral patterns. These findings provide new insights for consumer policy. They suggest value in considering both sector-sensitive instruments and broader practice-based approaches. Product longevity represents a relatively widespread cross-sectoral pract

latest.title: Consumer Complaints, Loyalty Risk, and Cancellation Intention in Digital Subscription Platforms: A Text Mining Analysis
latest.abstract: This study examines consumer complaints regarding digital video subscription platforms using data collected from Şikayetvar, Türkiye’s largest online consumer complaint platform. The study aims to identify the dominant themes underlying consumer complaints, compare thematic distributions across platforms, and explore loyalty-related textual indicators and explicit cancellation-related expressions embedded in complaint texts. A total of 2,005 complaints related to Netflix, Exxen, and Gain were analyzed. After a series of preprocessing steps, complaint texts were vectorized using TF-IDF and analyzed using Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF). Seven major complaint themes were identified, including billing and refund issues, subscription management problems, technical access difficulties, content-related concerns, promotional issues, sports broadcasting and live-stream access problems, and payment security complaints. Chi-square analysis revealed significant differences in thematic complaint distributions across platforms. In addition, loyalty risk indicators differed significantly among platforms according to Kruskal–Wallis test results. Logistic regression analysis showed that platform type and complaint themes were significantly associated with explicit cancellation-related expressions identified in the complaint texts. The findings suggest that online complaint data can provide valuable insights into customer dissatisfaction patterns and may serve as a useful monitoring tool for identifying potential loyalty-related risks in digital subscription services. The study contributes to the growing literature on text mining and digital consumer behavior by providing evidence from Turkish-language complaint data and offering a reproducible framework for complaint-based cust
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Exploring Consumers' Journey From Physical Ownership to Digital Assets
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT This special issue examines consumers' evolving relationship with digital assets as consumption shifts from physical ownership towards immersive, access‐based digital environments. Synthesising 12 contributions across four themes (i.e., metaverse/NFT experiences, wellbeing and identity consequences, digital consumption across service contexts and marketing strategies for digital assets), our editorial maps how digital scarcity, authenticity, community engagement and psychological ownership shape consumer value, behaviour and wellbeing in digital consumption. Findings reveal digital assets' dual capacity to enhance identity expression and engagement while generating dark‐side outcomes such as hoarding, piracy and compulsive spending. The editorial also proposes a research agenda spanning six areas, namely value creation for digital assets, the role of ownership and identity, monetization of digital assets, cultural factors in digital consumption , digital consumption in different markets and marketing strategies for digital consumption, that could guide future inquiry into digital asset consumption.

latest.title: Towards a Conceptual Integration of Masstige in Consumer Behaviour through a Kaleidoscopic View
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Abstract: The purpose of this research paper is to conduct a comprehensive scoping review with the objective to examine the advancement of masstige marketing as an essential notion in consumer-brand engagement researches. The study covers a multitude of facets of masstige marketing literature, comprising frameworks, methodologies, antecedents, outcomes, mediators, moderators through the examination of 88 studies. In an effort to incorporate masstige marketing notion within the consumer-brand engagement research, this paper highlights the necessity of constructing robust frameworks and tackling the quantitative difficulties. This scoping review provides insights to practitioners and academics who desire to further explore the domain of masstige. Keywords: Brand Management, Masstige, Luxury, Consumer-Brand Relationship, Prestige Brands

latest.title: The Effects of Brand Equity and Sales Promotion on Customer Loyalty with Purchase Decisions as a Mediating Variable
latest.abstract: This study examines brand equity, sales promotion, purchase decisions, and customer loyalty among Purbasari body scrub consumers on TikTok Shop in Yogyakarta City. Questionnaire data from 100 purposively selected respondents were analyzed using multiple regression and Sobel tests in SPSS 26. The reported regressions indicate positive associations of brand equity and sales promotion with loyalty and purchase decisions. A separate test reports a purchase decision–loyalty association. Mediation interpretations remain provisional because the Sobel inputs are inconsistent with the regression coefficients. These cross-sectional findings require consistent model outputs before mediation conclusions can be confirmed.

latest.title: Unpacking the university environment
latest.venue: Journal of Interdisciplinary Studies in Education
latest.abstract: Universities increasingly compete on environmental quality, yet the mechanism converting it into brand equity remains under-specified. This study separates the university environment into learning and emotional dimensions and tests whether their associations with brand equity are mediated by student engagement and moderated by institutional reputation. Integrating the stimulus–organism–response framework, student involvement theory, and signaling theory, we analyzed data from 256 students at Vietnam National University, Hanoi, using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The learning environment was associated with both engagement and equity, whereas the emotional environment was associated with equity only through engagement. Brand reputation dampened rather than amplified the engagement–equity link. These findings suggest that engagement-oriented investments may yield the highest returns for institutions with nascent reputational capital.

latest.title: Pleasure or annoyance? The opposing effects of food-service rituals
latest.venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management
latest.abstract: Purpose Food-service rituals are increasingly prevalent in hospitality practice, yet their effects in real-world settings remain underexplored. Drawing on Interaction Ritual Chain theory, this research aims to investigate when and why food-service rituals enhance versus undermine encounter satisfaction. Design/methodology/approach Three video-based experiments were conducted in a restaurant setting. Findings Study 1 shows a positive main effect of food-service rituals on encounter satisfaction. Study 2 demonstrates that food-service rituals enhance satisfaction by evoking pleasure among customers with hedonic consumption goals but elicit annoyance among customers with utilitarian goals. Study 3 further reveals that food-service rituals exert a positive effect under communal customer-brand relationship norms, but backfire under exchange relationship norms. Practical implications This study offers valuable guidance for restaurant operators. Businesses should consider customers’ consumption goals and customer-brand relationship norms when implementing food-service rituals. Originality/value This study enriches the hospitality management literature by developing a more balanced understanding of food-service rituals and highlighting the conditions and emotional mechanisms that shape customer reactions.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: From “mine” to “me”: how perceived NFT attributes shape brand resonance in Chinese Generation Z sports fandom
latest.venue: International Journal of Sports Marketing and Sponsorship
latest.abstract: Purpose Situated within sports fandom and China’s regulated digital asset environment, this study examines how perceived uniqueness, scarcity, controllability, and non-fungible tokens (NFT) symbolism shape brand resonance through psychological ownership and customer-brand identification among Generation Z fans. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on psychological ownership theory and social identity theory, the study tests a serial mediation model using survey data from 489 Chinese Generation Z sports fans and partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings Perceived uniqueness, controllability, and NFT symbolism strengthen psychological ownership, which increases customer-brand identification and, in turn, brand resonance. This pattern supports a layered process from perceived NFT attributes to ownership, identification, and sustained fan-brand relationships. Perceived scarcity has no significant direct or indirect effects. Research limitations/implications Psychological ownership explains how NFTs become personally meaningful, while customer-brand identification links ownership to loyalty, attachment, community, and engagement. Sports brands operating in regulated digital markets should provide meaningful opportunities for fans to express their affiliation, exercise control, and participate in brand communities, rather than relying primarily on scarcity. Originality/value This study integrates ownership and identity perspectives to explain how sport brand NFTs foster digital belonging and brand resonance in sports fandom. It also provides evidence from China, where NFT circulation and speculative activities operate under regulatory constraints.

latest.title: The Effect of Service Quality and Image of The Medan Class I Special Immigration Office on Consumer Satisfaction with Electronic Passports
latest.venue: Journal of Management Economic and Accounting
latest.abstract: This research aims to determine the influence of price and product quality on purchasing interest in Rengginang Zaennissa Snack Medan. This research used quantitative methods involving 72 respondents. Data collection was carried out using questionnaire distribution. The data obtained were analyzed using statistical formulas, namely using the normality test, multicollinearity test, heteroscedasticity test and multiple linear regression analysis with the SPSS Version 23.0 program. The results of this research show that the results of this study indicate that the t-test results obtained a calculated t value of 94.012 greater than ttable 1.99 with a significance level of 0.000. Thus, H2 is accepted and Ho is rejected, which means that price has a positive and partially significant influence on consumer purchasing interest. The calculated t value of 42.462 is greater than ttable 1.99 with a significance level of 0.000. Thus, H2 is accepted and Ho is rejected, which means that product quality has a positive and partially significant influence on consumer purchasing interest. The calculated F value is 10127.477 with a significance level of 0.00o. Because the calculated F value of 10127.477 is greater than Ftable 3.13, it can be concluded that simultaneously the product quality and price variables have a significant influence on the dependent variable, namely purchasing interest.

latest.title: Social Media's Effect on Luxury Brand Attachment and Purchase Intentions in India
latest.abstract: Abstract Strong cultural traditions and shifting global tastes are combining to create the fast expanding Indian luxury market. For the lately expanding Indian luxury consumer market, this research investigates the connection between Purchase Intention (PI), use of social media (SMU), and Luxury Brand Attachment (LBA). The Uses and Gratifications Theory (UGT) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) serve as the foundation for this study's development and analysis of a comprehensive model that includes Motivation (MOT) as a factor and communication (WOM) as a crucial consequence and mediator. 350 seasoned luxury brand customers in key Indian cities were interviewed using a standardized online questionnaire. In addition to convergent and discriminant validity tests, the reliability of the measuring scales was thoroughly evaluated using Cronbach's Alpha.

latest.title: Neuromarketing as a strategic tool for influencing consumption: : an integrative literature review
latest.venue: Amazônica - Revista de Psicopedagogia, Psicologia escolar e Educação
latest.abstract: Introdução: O neuromarketing consolidou-se como campo interdisciplinar que investiga processos emocionais e inconscientes subjacentes ao comportamento de consumo. Objetivo: Esta revisão integrativa analisa como a literatura recente (2020–2025) descreve o neuromarketing como ferramenta estratégica de influência no consumo, bem como os desafios éticos e sociais associados. Método: Realizou-se busca nas bases SciELO e Google Scholar, com os descritores "neuromarketing", "neurociência", "comportamento do consumidor" e "influência", limitada a artigos publicados em português e inglês a partir de 2020. Foram excluídas dissertações, teses, TCCs e livros. Após triagem por título, resumo e leitura integral, nove artigos compuseram o corpus final. Resultados: A análise evidenciou quatro eixos temáticos: (i) fundamentos neuropsicológicos do consumo; (ii) mediação hormonal nas decisões de compra; (iii) fatores culturais, sociais, pessoais e psicológicos que modulam o comportamento do consumidor; e (iv) implicações éticas, com destaque para manipulação inconsciente, discriminação algorítmica e consumo compulsivo. Considerações finais: O neuromarketing amplia a compreensão do consumo, mas sua aplicação exige regulamentação, formação ética de profissionais e alfabetização midiática dos consumidores. No Brasil, a diversidade cultural representa oportunidade para o desenvolvimento de práticas mais inclusivas e socialmente responsáveis

latest.title: Brand Authenticity, Digital Interaction, and Sensory Experience as Predictors of Local Coffee Repurchase Intention
latest.venue: Jurnal Relevansi Ekonomi Manajemen dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of brand authenticity, digital interaction, and sensory experience on repurchase intention of local coffee among Millennials and Generation Z, with novelty in integrating these three variables into a single empirical model representing cognitive, social, and affective dimensions. This research employs a quantitative approach with an explanatory design involving 100 respondents selected through purposive sampling and analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results indicate that brand authenticity has a positive and significant effect on repurchase intention (β = 0.488; p < 0.05), while sensory experience is the most dominant factor (β = 0.883; p < 0.001). In contrast, digital interaction does not have a significant effect (β = -0.030; p > 0.05). Simultaneously, all variables significantly influence repurchase intention, explaining 61.8% of its variance. These findings highlight that consumer loyalty in local coffee is primarily driven by sensory experience and perceived authenticity rather than digital interaction, suggesting that practitioners should prioritize enhancing product experience and authenticity as key strategies to increase repurchase intention.

latest.title: Digital transformation and customer loyalty: The mediating role of co-created service experience in Indonesian banking
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractBanks invest in digital platforms expecting stronger loyalty. Yet, it remains unclear why some investments build durable relationships while others do not, because prior research conflates what customers do with how they experience it. This study tests whether co-created service experience mediates the relationship between customer-perceived digital transformation and customer loyalty among digital banking customers in Indonesia. Survey data were collected in 2025 from 360 customers of five banks in Medan, Indonesia, who had used mobile or internet banking for at least six months, ensuring direct experience with digital banking, and were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapping. All four hypotheses were supported: digital transformation was strongly associated with co-created service experience (β = 0.659, p < 0.001) and significantly associated with loyalty directly (β = 0.425, p < 0.001); co-created service experience was significantly associated with loyalty (β = 0.478, p < 0.001) and partially mediated the digital transformation–loyalty relationship (indirect effect β = 0.315, p < 0.001; VAF = 42.6%), with the model explaining 67.8% of the variance in loyalty. Digital transformation is thus associated with loyalty through two distinct routes, only one of which depends on customers feeling like genuine participants. Institutional trust was not measured directly in this study, so the link between this pattern and Indonesia's institutional trust conditions is interpretive and requires further testing. Because the sample is limited to a single city, findings apply to this market and should not be generalized to Indonesian banking as a whole.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Effect of past relationship quality on brand hate: a serial mediation effect of perceived betrayal and blame attribution
latest.venue: The Journal of Marketing Theory and Practice
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine how past relationship quality with a brand can influence the development of brand hate and its outcomes. Drawing on an appraisal-based perspective, the study examines perceived betrayal as an affective response to violated relational expectations and blame attribution as a subsequent cognitive evaluation through which previously positive consumer–brand relationships can escalate into brand hate. Using the hierarchical brand hate dimensions, a serial mediation model is proposed between past relationship quality and hot, cool, and cold brand hate, through perceived betrayal and blame attribution. A cross-sectional survey was conducted to collect data from N = 560 Indian consumers. The model was tested using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The findings reveal that the effect of past relationship quality on the three brand hate dimensions is serially mediated by perceived betrayal and blame attribution. Hot brand hate affects consumers’ engagement in negative e-Word-of-Mouth (eWOM), cool and cold brand hate lead to reduced patronage, but only cold brand hate predicts brand avoidance. This study integrates affective and cognitive processes within an appraisal-based framework and empirically validates the hierarchical structure of brand hate. The findings provide support for the “love-becomes-hate” effect and highlight the importance for brands of recognizing customers with strong past relationships and proactively mitigating perceptions of betrayal.

latest.title: An Empirical Analysis of Factors Influencing Brand Equity in Coffee Shops: A Study of Jakarta, Indonesia
latest.venue: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON BUSINESS AND ECONOMICS
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of the coffee shop industry in Jakarta is a direct consequence of Indonesia’s strong contribution to global coffee production as the world’s fourth-largest coffee producer. The number of coffee shops in Indonesia has reached 10,000 outlets. Due to increased competition among coffee shops, businesses are offering better service quality, innovative products, and improved ambiance and atmosphere to enhance brand loyalty, which eventually contributes to brand equity. However, limited studies have investigated the brand equity factors of coffee shop brands in Jakarta, despite the intense market competition among them. This study investigates how various brand-related factors, such as brand awareness, perceived quality, brand association, and brand loyalty, influence the overall brand equity of coffee shop brands in this highly competitive market. This study adopted a descriptive, explorative, and cross-sectional design with quantitative methods to analyze data collected from a representative sample of coffee shop consumers in Jakarta. Data were collected from 390 respondents from Jakarta city of Indonesia from 390 respondents from Jakarta, Indonesia, and were analyzed using SmartPLS. The statistical analysis confirms that there is a significant relationship between the four factors and brand equity, with perceived quality being the most influential factor among the study variables. This study provides strategic managerial recommendations for coffee shop businesses in Jakarta to enhance brand equity, underscoring the vital role of superior perceived quality while supporting sustainable business growth.

latest.title: From sole to soul: modes of meaning-making in contemporary sneaker collecting
latest.abstract: How does collecting remain meaningful in a relatively sterile, transparent marketplace driven by disenchanted financial logic and seamless, frictionless consumption options? This study explores how sneaker collectors sustain and create new meanings for contemporary sneaker collecting in response to the convenience and saturation of online (re)sell marketplaces. Drawing on in-depth interviews with Dutch sneaker collectors (n = 20), we identify five collector orientations based on the strategies they employ to make the practice meaningful: (1) expressionists, (2) social connectors, (3) aesthetes, (4) completionists, and (5) hunters. Each represents a different mode of engagement with sneaker collecting, whether through identity work, aesthetic appreciation, or strategic navigation of market dynamics. Expressionists use sneakers to construct biographical narratives, while social connectors prioritize shared belonging and community. Aesthetes are guided by aesthetic and cultural value, and completionists and hunters create meaning either by achieving closure or constantly extending the thrill of the hunt. These findings suggest that contemporary collecting cannot be reduced to ‘shallow’ consumerism, nor can it be understood as an individual and isolated practice. Instead, collecting acquires meaning through the interplay between producers, consumers, and the digital and physical spaces in which it takes place.

latest.title: Socio Technical Drivers of Impulse Buying in Live Streaming Fashionpreneurship
latest.abstract: This study addresses the rapid growth of live-streaming commerce in Indonesia and its impact on impulse buying behavior within emerging digital economies. Integrating the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework with Socio-Technical Systems (STS) theory, this research aims to examine how socio technical stimuli streamer factors, platform affordances, and perceived brand value, influence consumers’ emotional (shopping happiness) and cognitive (ongoing trust) states, which subsequently drive impulse buying. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data from 300 consumers who purchased local fashion products via Shopee Live and TikTok Shop. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess measurement validity and structural relationships. The results indicate that all hypothesized relationships are statistically significant. Socio-technical stimuli significantly influence both shopping happiness and ongoing trust, which in turn positively affect impulse buying, with shopping happiness emerging as the strongest predictor. This study contributes by offering an integrated socio-technical perspective on consumer behavior in live commerce and provides practical implications for enhancing engagement and trust. It also supports the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 8 and SDG 9, by promoting sustainable digital commerce and empowering local fashion businesses through technology-driven innovation.

latest.title: From green claims to guest trust: Unravelling communication dynamics, brand perception, and self-image in sustainable hotels
latest.venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management
latest.abstract: As sustainability becomes an increasingly strategic priority in the hospitality industry, hotels are intensifying their efforts to showcase their commitment to environmentally conscious practices. However, the proliferation of hotels' green marketing communications has exposed hotel guests to an unprecedented volume of environmental claims, increasing skepticism regarding their credibility and authenticity. This paper examines how hotels' green marketing communications shape guest perceptions and trust during the pre-purchase stage, particularly in the hotel selection decision-making process. Drawing on a systematic literature review, five key themes are identified, highlighting the importance of clear, transparent, and consistent communication in strengthening a hotel's reputation and perceived trustworthiness. Beyond external marketing strategies, guests' internal psychological states, environmental values, and self-perceptions also significantly influence their willingness to trust and support hotels' green initiatives. This paper proposes a conceptual framework that integrates and extends Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) theory and self-congruity theory. The framework contributes to the green marketing and hospitality literature by providing a more nuanced understanding of how external green marketing stimuli interact with guests' internal perceptions to shape trust. It also offers practical implications for hotels and other organizations across the tourism and hospitality sector seeking to develop more credible green marketing strategies while strengthening customer trust.

latest.title: Party Failure, Voter Emotions and Retaliation Intentions in the Context of Digitalization
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping the value relationship that political parties, like firms, maintain with their stakeholders; voters’ reactions are now visible not only at the ballot box but also on social media and in interpersonal networks. This study adapts concepts from the consumer-brand relationship and consumer retaliation literature to political parties and examines the effect of perceived party failure severity on three response intentions (direct complaining to the party, public complaining on social media and negative word of mouth) through voters’ anger and perceived betrayal. The effects of perceived justice and inferred benevolence on negative emotions and the moderating roles of party love and party trust are also tested. Data from 383 eligible voters in Türkiye, collected through an online survey, were analysed using confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modelling, bootstrapping and moderation analyses. Failure severity strongly increases anger and perceived betrayal, which are linked to different response channels: anger to direct complaining, which functions as voice directed at the party, and betrayal to public complaining on social media and negative word of mouth. At the level of total indirect effects, however, failure severity increases only direct complaining; its total indirect effect on social media is non-significant and that on negative word of mouth is negative, so failure translates into indirect retaliation only to the extent that it is experienced as betrayal. Hypotheses regarding perceived justice, inferred benevolence, party love and party trust were not supported. Interpreted through a value co-destruction lens, the findings contribute to the political marketing literature on the dark side of the voter-party relationship
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Digital Experience and Customer Loyalty: The Mediating Role of Trust and Customer Satisfaction Among Wondr BNI Users
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen Pemasaran dan Perilaku Konsumen.
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study aims to examine the effect of Digital Experience on Customer Loyalty through the mediating roles of Trust and Customer Satisfaction among Wondr BNI users in East Java, Indonesia. Design/Methodology/Approach – This study employed an explanatory quantitative design using a cross-sectional survey. Data were collected from active Wondr BNI users in East Java selected through purposive sampling. A structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale was administered to the respondents, and the data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.1. Findings – The results indicate that Digital Experience positively and significantly influences Customer Loyalty, Trust, and Customer Satisfaction. Furthermore, Trust and Customer Satisfaction significantly mediate the relationship between Digital Experience and Customer Loyalty, with Trust demonstrating a stronger mediating role than Customer Satisfaction. These findings highlight the importance of both psychological mechanisms in fostering customer loyalty in digital banking. Originality/Value – This study extends Expectation Confirmation Theory (ECT) in the digital banking context by demonstrating the complementary mediating roles of Trust and Customer Satisfaction in the relationship between Digital Experience and Customer Loyalty. The findings provide practical insights for digital banking providers to enhance customer loyalty by improving digital experiences, strengthening customer trust, and increasing customer satisfaction.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Employee Brand Equity and Decent Work in Chinese Hospitality
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Drawing on extended‐self theory, this study examines how employee brand equity relates to decent work in Chinese branded hospitality organizations. Data were collected from 440 employees across 25 branded hospitality organizations in Hainan, China. The results indicate that brand endorsement, brand allegiance, and brand consistent behavior each have significant positive direct effects on decent work, as well as indirect effects through brand psychological ownership. Brand psychological ownership partially mediates these relationships, while perceived brand value fit positively moderates the relationship between brand psychological ownership and decent work. These findings extend employee brand equity research by identifying decent work as an employee‐centered outcome and by clarifying the mediating role of brand psychological ownership and the boundary role of perceived brand value fit. The study also offers practical insights into how branded hospitality organizations may support more positive employee work experiences.

latest.title: Understanding Consumer Repurchase Intention in Blind Box Products: A Theory of Planned Behavior Approach
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen Pemasaran dan Perilaku Konsumen.
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study aims to examine the effects of attitude toward behavior, subjective norm, and perceived behavioral control on Generation Z’s repurchase intention toward Pop Mart blind box products in Indonesia. Design/Methodology/Approach – The study employed an explanatory quantitative approach. The population consisted of Generation Z consumers who had purchased Pop Mart blind box products, with 150 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using an online Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS Version 3.0. Findings – The findings show that attitude toward behavior and perceived behavioral control have positive and significant effects on repurchase intention, whereas subjective norm does not have a significant effect on Generation Z’s repurchase intention toward Pop Mart blind box products. Originality/Value – The study contributes a novel application of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to the context of uncertainty-based and emotionally driven products, particularly blind box products. The findings suggest that marketing strategies should focus on strengthening consumers’ personal experiences, positive attitudes, and perceived behavioral control rather than relying primarily on social pressure to encourage repurchase intention.

latest.title: Transforming cultural heritage into modern marketing narratives: A thematic analysis of HEPA Coffee’s brand archetypes through a Gen Z perspective
latest.abstract: Makale Türü: Araştırma makalesiBu çalışma, HEPA Coffee'nin Puduhepa figürü üzerinden inşa ettiği marka kimliğini ve bu anlatının Z kuşağı tarafından nasıl algılandığını incelemektedir.Nitel araştırma tasarımında marka kurucusuyla derinlemesine mülakat ve Z kuşağı katılımcılarıyla odak grup görüşmeleri gerçekleştirilmiştir. Bulgular, markanın stratejik olarak Hükümdar ve Kahraman arketipleri etrafında kurgulandığını ve Puduhepa figürünün güçlü bir anlatı unsuru olarak işlev gördüğünü ortaya koymaktadır.Bununla birlikte, Z kuşağı açısından doğallık (Masum arketipi) artık temel bir beklenti düzeyine karşılık gelirken; daha gizemli ve sembolik (Sihirbaz arketipi) bir görsel dil talep edilmektedir.Araştırma, kültürel sermayenin etkili bir marka deneyimine dönüşebilmesi için görsel anlatı tutarlılığı ile dijital mikroanlatıların kritik bir rol oynadığını göstermektedir.

latest.title: Relationship Quality toward Sufficiency Economy-Aligned Sustainable Brands: Evidence from Thailands Generation Z
latest.abstract: Purpose: This research aims to capture the dimensions of consumer-brand relationship quality between young adult Gen Z consumers and Sufficiency Economy Philosophy (SEP)-aligned sustainable brands by applying the Investment Model. While previous studies have primarily examined individual dimensions of sustainable brand relationship quality, this study integrated multiple motivational dimensions of brand relationship quality within the Investment Model for SEP-aligned sustainable brands. Research design, data and methodology: A mixed-method approach was employed, beginning with qualitative exploration followed by quantitative research. Data were collected through an online questionnaire survey, yielding 277 usable responses, predominantly from university students, representing young adult Gen Z consumers in Thailand. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was conducted to test a second-order reflective measurement model of brand relationship quality. Results: The results indicate that the Gen Z consumers perceive SEP alignment as an integral aspect of sustainable corporate brands. Brand relationship quality in this context is a multidimensional construct comprising economic satisfaction, trust, pride, self-connection, all of which demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity, with trust as the strongest reflection (β = 0.870), followed by pride (β = 0.783). Major Findings: Trust emerged as the strongest reflective construct, followed by pride, economic satisfaction, and self-connection, highlighting the importance of SEP-aligned sustainable branding.

latest.title: Cultural Identity and Sustainability in Airline Service Quality: Thai Airways Case Study
latest.abstract: This study examines how cultural identity and environmental sustainability can be integrated into airline service quality in the specific context of Thai Airways. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was administered to international passengers who had flown with the airline within the previous six months; 596 usable questionnaires were obtained from 650 distributed at Suvarnabhumi Airport between January and March 2024. The instrument combined SERVQUAL, sustainability perception, cultural service value, satisfaction, loyalty, and travel-characteristic measures. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling were used as the principal analytical procedures. The model showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.962, TLI = 0.958, RMSEA = 0.044, SRMR = 0.038), while scale reliability ranged from 0.78 to 0.94. Service expectations were associated with satisfaction both directly and indirectly through service quality, with a reported total effect of 0.610. Behavioral patterns also showed significant relationships with satisfaction, and visible environmental initiatives were the strongest sustainability-related predictor of service perceptions. The findings indicate that service quality in a national carrier is best understood as an integrated configuration of core service performance, culturally distinctive delivery, and credible sustainability practices rather than as independent service attributes. This integrated perspective provides the empirical basis for the proposed SSQ framework.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Brand forgiveness: a scoping review and agenda for future research
latest.abstract: Purpose Brand forgiveness reflects consumers’ willingness to maintain or restore relationships with brands following service failures, ethical controversies and marketplace transgressions. The purpose of this study is to conduct a scoping review of the theoretical development, conceptual foundations and future directions of brand forgiveness research. Design/methodology/approach The review synthesizes 80 studies published between 2009 and 2025 using scoping review guidelines and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-analyses reporting procedures. The analysis examines theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, antecedents, mediators, moderators and outcomes. Findings Brand forgiveness literature is grounded in coping, attribution and justice-based theories of post-transgression evaluation, while relational and identity-based processes remain less developed. The literature identifies firm-, consumer- and brand/communication-related antecedents, along with cognitive, emotional and social mechanisms shaping forgiveness. Methodologically, the field relies largely on experiments and cross-sectional surveys, limiting understanding of forgiveness as a dynamic process. Research limitations/implications The review identifies theoretical, methodological and contextual gaps and proposes directions for advancing brand forgiveness research. Originality/value This review synthesizes fragmented brand forgiveness research and conceptualizes forgiveness as a process involving cognitive interpretation, emotional regulation, moral evaluation and relationship repair.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Examining The Relationships Between The Need For Social Approval And Sustainable Consumption Behavior
latest.venue: Türkiye Mesleki ve Sosyal Bilimler Dergisi
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the relationships between individuals’ need for social approval and sustainable consumption behaviors. Accordingly, the need for social approval is conceptualized in terms of three dimensions—sensitivity to others’ judgments, social withdrawal, and leaving a good impression—and the relationships between these dimensions and four dimensions of sustainable consumption behavior, namely environmental sensitivity, reusability, saving, and unneeded consumption, are examined. Within the scope of the study, data were collected through an online survey from 393 university students with different levels of educational attainment who were selected using a convenience sampling method. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, confirmatory factor analyses, and multiple regression analyses. The findings indicate that social motivations may be associated with sustainable consumption behaviors and that the nature of these relationships may vary across the dimensions of the need for social approval. The findings further suggest that social approval may serve as a functional mechanism for promoting sustainable consumption. Accordingly, the study offers implications for businesses and policymakers regarding the use of social norms to encourage more sustainable consumption practices.

latest.title: Identidade em cena: cultura pop, pertencimento e decisões de compra
latest.venue: Contextus - Revista Contemporânea de Economia e Gestão
latest.abstract: Contextualização: As decisões de compra de itens vinculados à cultura POP frequentemente ultrapassam a lógica estritamente funcional, sendo orientadas por significados simbólicos, identificação com universos narrativos e vínculos afetivos. Objetivo: Esta pesquisa investigou de que modo o uso das redes sociais (URS), a nostalgia (NOST), a formação de comunidade (FC) e o vínculo com a cultura POP (VCP) influenciam o comportamento de compra (CC). Método: Os dados foram coletados por questionário online entre os meses de setembro e dezembro de 2024. A amostra foi composta por 388 respondentes válidos. Para a análise, optou-se pela Modelagem de Equações Estruturais via Mínimos Quadrados Parciais (PLS-SEM), tendo como ferramenta de apoio o software SmartPLS4. Resultados: Os resultados indicaram que o uso das redes sociais influencia positivamente a formação de comunidade e, principalmente, o vínculo com a cultura POP, enquanto o vínculo com a cultura POP se destacou como o preditor mais forte do comportamento de compra. Adicionalmente, verificou-se que o uso das redes sociais influencia o comportamento de compra tanto de forma direta quanto indiretamente por meio do vínculo com a cultura POP, ao passo que a nostalgia apresentou influência direta de menor magnitude e não sustentou efeitos indiretos via formação de comunidade ou vínculo com a cultura POP. Conclusões: Os achados reforçam a centralidade do vínculo com a cultura POP como mecanismo explicativo do consumo em ambientes digitais, ao evidenciar que o uso das redes sociais contribui para a compra principalmente quando fortalece a identificação simbólica com esse universo.

latest.title: Pazarlama İletişiminde Teknolojik Nostaljinin Yeniden İnşası: Ülker Albeni ‘Ajda Pekkan’ Reklamı Üzerine Hiper-Gerçeklik ve Restoratif Nostalji Eksenli Bir İnceleme
latest.abstract: Bu çalışma, Ülker Albeni’nin Ajda Pekkan temalı reklamını teknolojik nostaljinin pazarlama iletişimindeki inşası bağlamında, Svetlana Boym’un restoratif nostalji ve Jean Baudrillard’ın hiper-gerçeklik kuramları ekseninde analiz etmektedir. Kuramsal düzlemde restoratif nostalji, geçmişin doğrusal gerçekliğini ve zamanın getirdiği tahribatı yapay zekâ gibi araçlarla ‘telafi edilmesi gereken bir boşluk’ olarak görürken; bu süreç Baudrillardcı perspektifte gerçeğin yerini alan ve orijinalinden daha ‘otantik’ algılanan hiper-gerçek bir simülasyon üretmektedir. Roland Barthes’ın göstergebilimsel yöntemiyle yapılan çözümlemede; Ajda Pekkan’ın 1990, 2000 ve 2025 yıllarını temsil eden figürleri ile ürünün çikolata, karamel ve bisküvi katmanları arasında kurulan ritmik uyumun, tüketici belleğinde ‘değişmeyen öz’ mitini yapılandırdığı saptanmıştır. Yapay zekâ destekli gençleştirme (de-aging) teknolojisinin Ajda Pekkan’ın kültürel ikonluğuyla birleşmesi, sanatsal bir ‘aura’nın sentetik olarak yeniden üretilmesine ve markanın zamanın aşındırıcı etkisinden arındırılmış, zamansız bir otorite olarak mühürlenmesine olanak tanımıştır.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. hot.title: Cyber Shopping Beyond Boundaries: The Metaverse Revolution in e‐Commerce and Consumer Behavior
hot.abstract: The metaverse is swiftly flattering an important player in the e‐commerce domain. It provides innumerable opportunities and indicates a revolutionary paradigm shift in e‐commerce. Online businesses can now create virtual storefronts that enable immersive, lifelike product exploration within the metaverse, in contrast to traditional brick‐and‐mortar stores that cater to local customers. Current research offers a novel conceptual framework based on theories of interactive media effects and the stimulus–organism–response paradigm to understand consumer purchase intentions in the metaverse. Carefully gathered data from 342 survey participants were then examined using the analytical tools of structural equation modelling (SEM) and importance–performance map analysis (IPMA). The results of the study shed light on how much perceived augmentation and interaction affect consumers’ cognitive and emotive reactions, including feelings of realism, immersion, and telepresence. Remarkably, these reactions have a significant influence on how customers behave. The study’s distinctive worth is found in its creative recommendations, which can help tech firms and metaverse developers improve the purchasing experience in this dynamic digital environment.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.
