latest.title: Pengaruh Persepsi Harga Paket Data terhadap Kepuasan Pengguna Dalam Komunikasi Penawaran Telkomsel Prabayar pada Mahasiswa Pendidikan Fisika Universitas Sriwijaya
latest.venue: Journal of Communication and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh harga paket internet Telkomsel Prabayar terhadap kepuasan pelanggan pada mahasiswa Pendidikan Fisika Universitas Sriwijaya angkatan 2022–2024. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei. Populasi berjumlah 266 mahasiswa dan sampel terdiri atas 111 responden pengguna Telkomsel Prabayar. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner dan dianalisis menggunakan uji validitas, reliabilitas, uji asumsi, serta regresi linear sederhana. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa instrumen penelitian valid dan reliabel. Persamaan regresi yang diperoleh adalah Y = 1,826 + 0,717X, dengan pengaruh harga paket internet yang signifikan terhadap kepuasan pelanggan (p = 0,002). Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa penilaian mahasiswa terhadap harga paket internet berkaitan dengan kepuasan mereka terhadap layanan Telkomsel Prabayar. Abstract This study examines the effect of Telkomsel prepaid internet package prices on customer satisfaction among Physics Education students at Universitas Sriwijaya from the 2022–2024 cohorts. A quantitative survey was conducted among 111 Telkomsel prepaid users from a population of 266 students. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through validity and reliability tests, assumption tests, and simple linear regression. The instruments met the reported validity and reliability criteria. The regression equation was Y = 1.826 + 0.717X, and the reported significance value was p = 0.002, indicating a statistically significant relationship between internet package prices and customer satisfaction. The findings indicate that students’ evaluations of internet package prices are associated with their satisfaction with Telkomsel prepaid services.

latest.title: Statistical Analysis Of Consumer Purchase Intention For Managerial Decision-Making In Commodity Markets: Evidence From The Indian Steel Industry
latest.abstract: In Indian retail steel market, managerial decisions to position the brand, quality communication, price and access to the market require evidence on the factors associated with consumer purchase intention. This study delves into the same relationship with the help of structured questionnaire response from consumers of the Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities of Karnataka and Maharashtra. This difference between the number of observations (152 in SPSS tables; 150 in sampling description) needs to be checked against the original data set. Pearson correlations, multiple linear regressions and a brand-logo comparison were employed in the analysis of purchasing intentions. The model with five predictors explained 58.7% of the variance (with R² = 0.587). None of the adjusted non-significant variables were brand awareness, perceived quality and price perception. In the reported Logo comparison, the purchase intention was found to be lower in the Logo group (ArcelorMittal) when compared with the No Logo (control) group. Sustainability and digital communication are still important, proposed considerations but were not demonstrated to have independent impact by the regression outputs displayed. How the study has interpreted these findings are used as evidence for assessing priorities within marketing rather than causal sales or resource optimisation gains.

latest.title: DRIVING LOYALTY THROUGH SERVICE-QUALITY: DO AGE AND INCOME MATTER? EVIDENCE FROM MALAYSIA’S AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: Customer loyalty is essential for sustaining competitive advantage in the automotive service industry, where repeated post-sales interactions strongly influence long-term customer relationships. This study examines the relationship between service quality and customer loyalty in Malaysia's automotive service industry and investigates whether age and income moderate this relationship. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted using data collected from 385 customers of authorised automotive service centres in Malaysia. The data were analysed using multiple regression analysis. The findings reveal that service quality has a significant positive effect on customer loyalty, confirming that customers who perceive higher levels of service quality are more likely to remain loyal to their service providers. Although age exhibited a significant direct relationship with customer loyalty, neither age nor income significantly moderated the relationship between service quality and customer loyalty. These findings suggest that the influence of service quality on customer loyalty remains consistent across different demographic groups. This study contributes to the service marketing literature by providing evidence from an emerging market and offering practical implications for automotive service providers, highlighting the importance of consistently delivering high-quality services to strengthen customer loyalty rather than relying on demographic-based service differentiation.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Online Advertising Personalization, Price Perception, and Purchase Intention: Evidence from Prospective Tokopedia Customers in Mataram
latest.venue: International Journal of Business and Quality Research
latest.abstract: This study investigates how perceived online advertising personalization and price perception are associated with purchase intention toward Tokopedia among consumers in Mataram, Indonesia, who actively shop on competing e-commerce platforms but have never completed a purchase on Tokopedia. Grounded in the stimulus–organism–response perspective, a quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 100 purposively selected respondents. Data collected through a five-point Likert questionnaire were analyzed using multiple linear regression in IBM SPSS Statistics. Reanalysis of the item-level data confirmed significant positive relationships between online advertising personalization and purchase intention (B = 0.520, standardized β = 0.692, t = 11.231, p < .001), and between price perception and purchase intention (B = 0.245, β = 0.523, t = 8.492, p < .001). The two predictors jointly explained 64.0% of the observed variation in purchase intention (adjusted R² = 0.633). Both predictor constructs and purchase intention received mean ratings close to the neutral point, indicating scope for improving initial platform appeal. Advertising personalization was the stronger standardized predictor within this model. These findings suggest that relevance, credibility, and usefulness of advertising, alongside transparent price–value communication, may help Tokopedia engage prospective customers. The nonprobability design and self-reported intentions limit population generalization and causal interpretation.

latest.title: PENGARUH KUALITAS PRODUK, PROMOSI, PERSEPSI HARGA, KEPERCAYAAN PELANGGAN TERHADAP KEPUASAN PELANGGAN DAN LOYALITAS KONSUMEN PADA PUSAT OLEH-OLEH DAN KERIPIK BALADO
latest.venue: Journal of Practice Learning and Educational Development
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effects of: (1) product quality on customer satisfaction; (2) product quality on consumer loyalty; (3) promotion on customer satisfaction; (4) promotion on consumer loyalty; (5) price perception on customer satisfaction; (6) price perception on consumer loyalty; (7) customer trust on customer satisfaction; (8) customer trust on consumer loyalty; and (9) customer satisfaction on consumer loyalty. The results indicate that product quality has a significant effect on customer satisfaction and consumer loyalty. Promotion also has a significant effect on customer satisfaction and consumer loyalty. Price perception has a significant effect on both customer satisfaction and consumer loyalty. In contrast, customer trust has no significant effect on customer satisfaction or consumer loyalty. Furthermore, customer satisfaction has a significant effect on consumer loyalty. These findings indicate that product quality, promotion, price perception, and customer satisfaction play an important role in strengthening consumer loyalty, while customer trust does not have a direct significant effect in this research context.

latest.title: PENGARUH CURRENT RATIO, PRICE TO BOOK VALUE DAN RETURN ON ASSET TERHADAP RETURN SAHAM
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of Current Ratio (CR), Price to Book Value (PBV), and Return on Assets (ROA) on stock returns in telecommunication sub-sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The background of this study is based on fluctuations in companies' financial performance, which are assumed to influence the level of returns obtained by investors. The research method used is quantitative with an associative approach. The population consists of 22 telecommunication sub-sector companies, with a sample of 3 companies selected using purposive sampling technique. The research data includes 18 observations during the period 2019–2024. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with the help of SPSS version 26, including classical assumption tests, regression analysis, coefficient of determination test, t-test, and F-test. The results show that partially, CR and ROA have no significant effect on stock returns, with significance values of 0.506 and 0.316, respectively. Meanwhile, PBV has a significant effect on stock returns with a significance value of 0.044. Simultaneously, CR, PBV, and ROA do not have a significant effect on stock returns (Sig. 0.144). The coefficient of determination (R²) is 0.312, indicating that 31.2% of stock return variation can be explained by the model, while 68.8% is influenced by other factors outside the research model.

latest.title: Behavioural Biases and Pension Investment Decisions: Evidence from Employees in Kerala
latest.venue: ANUSANDHAN – NDIM s Journal of Business and Management Research
latest.abstract: Pension investment decisions are often influenced by psychological tendencies rather than purely rational financial reasoning. This study examines the role of five key behavioural biases overconfidence, loss aversion, present bias, anchoring, and herding in shaping pension investment behaviour among employees in Kerala. Using a structured questionnaire and responses from 100 participants, the study employs descriptive statistics and correlation analysis used to analyse the relationship between these biases and pension investment behaviour, including contribution levels, plan participation, and fund selection. The findings reveal that all five behavioural biases overconfidence, loss aversion, present bias, anchoring, and herding are significantly present among employees in Kerala with respect to pension investment decisions. However, among individual predictors, present bias showed a significant negative impact on pension investment behaviour, while overconfidence, loss aversion, anchoring, and herding biases were not significant. The results further reveal a significant variation in the strength of behavioural biases, with overconfidence and herding emerging as the most dominant factors influencing pension investment decisions among employees in Kerala.

latest.title: From Free to Paid: Public Attitude Change and Mechanism Evidence around Doubao's Charging Announcement
latest.abstract: As generative AI moves from free access to paid subscription, how charging shapes public attitude bears on platform commercialization. Taking Doubao's monthly subscription as the setting, this paper builds a dual-path framework of “product experience - price perception”. Using the announcement date (May 4, 2026) as the breakpoint, we collect public Weibo discussions from 30 days before to 30 days after it (2-day periods; the 14 days on each side form the main window), measure attitude with aspect-based sentiment analysis, and test changes at the breakpoint by regression discontinuity in time. Negative evaluation is robust in direction for Payment Willingness (τ = +0.751, p < 0.001) and Corporate Brand (τ = +0.647, p = 0.011), but rests on only 27 and 7 pre-breakpoint texts, so the magnitudes are read as direction only. The negative share for Price & Charging shows no significant increase (τ = -0.161, p = 0.123), so the price-fairness path is not supported. The difference between the two aspect jumps is -0.532 (clustered SE 0.437, p = 0.245), opposite to expectation and underpowered given the small pre-breakpoint sample; we report only that no larger negative change was found for the price path than for the feature path. The overall negative share rises by 0.317 (p = 0.041) but depends on a pre-breakpoint period with 3 relevant texts and falls to 0.043 (p = 0.517) without it, so it is not robustly supported. The conclusions are limited to a marked change in attitude, with no persistent shift and no strict causal claim.

latest.title: Beyond bias: How behavioral biases shape investment decision-making and perceived financial well-being
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study examines the associations among behavioral biases, Investment Decision-Making, and Perceived Financial Well-Being among individual investors in Indonesia. It distinguishes respondents’ involvement in the investment decision-making process from decision quality and investment performance.A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed using survey data from 505 Indonesian investors. The relationships among Anchoring Bias, Confirmation Bias, Loss Aversion, Overconfidence, Investment Decision-Making, and Perceived Financial Well-Being were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Permutation-based multi-group analysis was conducted to compare female and male respondents.Anchoring Bias, Confirmation Bias, Loss Aversion, and Overconfidence were positively associated with Investment Decision-Making, with path coefficients ranging from 0.144 to 0.215 (p < 0.05). Investment Decision-Making was positively associated with Perceived Financial Well-Being (β = 0.527, p < 0.001). The significant specific indirect effects further indicated that Investment Decision-Making statistically mediated the associations between each behavioral bias and Perceived Financial Well-Being. The multi-group analysis showed that only the relationship between Investment Decision-Making and Perceived Financial Well-Being differed significantly by gender and was stronger among female respondents.The findings contribute to behavioral finance research by showing that behavioral biases are associated with greater self-reported involvement in evaluating, selecting, and monitoring investments. latest.title: Determining Household Savings Preferences: The Case of Türkiye
latest.venue: Namık Kemal Üniversitesi Sosyal Bilimler Meslek Yüksek Okulu Dergisi
latest.abstract: This study examines the socio-demographic factors that influence household saving preferences in Türkiye. A multinomial logit model was used to analyse data from 3354 households with complete information in the Turkish Statistical Institute’s 2020 Household Budget Survey micro-dataset. Savings preferences were categorized into four groups: real estate, gold/foreign currency, bank accounts, and capital market instruments. The findings suggest that families with children are more likely to prefer real estate and capital market instruments, while families without children are less likely to choose gold or foreign currency and bank accounts. Spending amount did not significantly affect preferences for real estate or gold/foreign currency but increased the likelihood of choosing a bank account and decreased the likelihood of choosing capital market instruments. Tenants were more likely to prefer gold, foreign currency, bank accounts, and capital market instruments, while homeowners tended to prefer real estate. Those with private insurance preferred capital market instruments, while those without preferred real estate, gold, foreign currency, and bank accounts. As household size increased, the likelihood of choosing real estate or gold/foreign currency increased, while the likelihood of having a bank account decreased. These results are informative for policymakers.

latest.title: CÁC YẾU TỐ ẢNH HƯỞNG ĐẾN HÀNH VI QUẢN LÝ TÀI CHÍNH CÁ NHÂN CỦA SINH VIÊN TRONG BỐI CẢNH CHUYỂN ĐỔI SỐ
latest.venue: Journal of Thu Dau Mot University
latest.abstract: Bài viết đo lường mức độ tác động của bảy yếu tố đến hành vi quản lý tài chính cá nhân của sinh viên Trường Đại học Thủ Dầu Một. Khung phân tích kết hợp Lý thuyết Hành vi có kế hoạch, mô hình Kiến thức – Thái độ – Hành vi, khung Năng lực tài chính và Tài chính hành vi. Khảo sát trực tuyến sử dụng thang Likert 5 mức thu về 494 phiếu, trong đó 409 phiếu hợp lệ và được xử lý bằng SPSS 26.0. Tám thang đo có hệ số Cronbach's Alpha từ 0,761 đến 0,869; Kết quả EFA cho KMO = 0,903 và phương sai trích 61,270% với 32 biến quan sát; hồi quy đạt R² = 0,656 (F = 109,003; Sig. = 0,000). Bảy hệ số hồi quy đều dương và có ý nghĩa thống kê, giảm dần từ kiến thức tài chính (β = 0,273), tự tin tài chính (0,179), phong cách chi tiêu (0,164), ảnh hưởng gia đình (0,152), thái độ tài chính (0,146), hiểu biết tài chính (0,127) tới công nghệ tài chính (0,102). Sáu giả thuyết được chấp nhận; riêng hiểu biết tài chính chỉ được chấp nhận có điều kiện vì không tương quan đơn biến với biến phụ thuộc (r = 0,027; Sig. = 0,587). Trên cơ sở đó, nghiên cứu đề xuất một số khuyến nghị.

latest.title: ‘Emotional Intelligence Is Not Just an Asset; It Is a Necessity’: Shaping Financial Behaviours and Overcoming Biases in Women Entrepreneurs
latest.abstract: The role of emotional intelligence (EI) in shaping the behavioural biases of women in financial decision-making remains underexplored in the literature. The current study addressed this gap by investigating how women entrepreneurs’ financial literacy influences their financial decisions, with EI serving as a mediator. A cross-sectional descriptive survey design was employed for data collection from 210 Pakistani women entrepreneurs. A proportional stratified sampling technique was used to collect data, and analysis was conducted using structural equation modelling (SEM) via AMOS 26. Findings reveal that financial literacy has significant positive impacts on EI and self-control and helps reduce loss aversion bias, but no significant relationship was found between financial literacy and regret aversion or mental accounting. Moreover, EI acts as a strong mediator between financial literacy and biases such as mental accounting, regret aversion and loss aversion, but not between financial literacy and self-control. This study’s findings underscore the critical role of EI in reducing biases and complementing financial literacy to empower women entrepreneurs to make rational financial decisions. Moreover, it also emphasizes the need to integrate EI into financial literacy programmes to foster more effective decision-making and advance entrepreneurship among women.

latest.title: Executive Personal Jet Use and Agency Costs: The Practice of Time‐Share Reimbursement
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Time‐share agreements (time‐shares) are an unexplored form of executives' personal use of corporate aircraft. Relative to jet perquisites (jet perks), time‐shares require reimbursement yet have limited disclosure, which practitioners promote to reduce scrutiny. This trade‐off engenders ambiguity and agency concerns about the associated effort managers devote to maximize shareholder wealth. Among S&P 500 firms from 2004 to 2017, we find that time‐share use, alone or combined with jet perks, has grown. Further, from 2007 to 2017, our primary empirical analysis shows that lower future firm profitability and value coincide with time‐shares, but only when combined with jet perks; these outcomes are higher for firms that offer only time‐shares. Changes analysis also supports that higher (lower) shareholder wealth coincides with a switch to time‐shares (jet perks). To further disentangle time‐shares from jet perks, we examine variation in time‐share disclosure attributes; consistent with initial inferences, more robust time‐share disclosure coincides with higher shareholder wealth. Finally, we explore the possibility that shareholders bear some costs that offset reimbursement and find only modest increases in cash compensation following time‐share initiation. Collectively, our findings imply that agency issues are lower for company stakeholders when firms do not award jet perquisites and instead use time‐share agreements.

latest.title: The Impact of Shopee PayLater Feature Usage and Financial Literacy on Consumptive Behavior among Generation Z
latest.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
latest.abstract: Shopping through TikTok has reshaped how people look at and decide on beauty products. Brands can no longer rely on one tactic alone; they have to blend promotion that happens in real time, content that people actually want to watch, and offers that feel worth the money. This study looks at whether live streaming, content marketing, and product bundling, taken one by one and together, shape the intention to buy Wardah products on TikTok. We used a quantitative design and gathered answers from 100 TikTok users through a questionnaire on a five-point Likert scale, with respondents chosen by accidental sampling. Multiple linear regression was then used to test the data. Each of the three variables turned out to have a positive and significant effect on purchase intention, and the three of them together were also significant, with an Adjusted R2 of 0.729. Product bundling carried the most weight, ahead of live streaming and content marketing. In practical terms, digital marketing on TikTok does push people closer to buying. For Wardah, the clearest lesson is to offer more bundle packages, which can support upselling and lift buying interest among consumers who now shop mostly online.

latest.title: Effect of Strategic Resource Management, Financial Literacy, and Institutional Support on Small Business Sustainability in Katsina State, Nigeria
latest.venue: Jurnal Aplikasi Manajemen Ekonomi dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: Small business sustainability remains a critical challenge in resource-constrained environments, particularly in northern Nigeria where institutional support has intensified but participation gaps persist. This study examines the effect of strategic resource management, financial literacy, and institutional support on small business sustainability in Katsina State, Nigeria. Drawing on the Resource-Based View, Human Capital Theory, and Institutional Theory, the study adopts a quantitative cross-sectional survey design targeting 384 registered small businesses across the three senatorial districts of Katsina State. Data were collected through structured questionnaires and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that strategic resource management, financial literacy, and institutional support each exert significant positive effects on business sustainability. Financial literacy partially mediates the relationship between strategic resource management and sustainability, while institutional support moderates the financial literacy–sustainability relationship. The study contributes to management literature by integrating internal capability and external institutional perspectives in explaining SME sustainability in a developing economy context. Practical recommendations are offered for KASEDA and Katsina State policymakers to optimise training design, financing access, and programme outreach.

latest.title: Purchase Intention Formation for K-Beauty Cosmetics: The Mediating Role of Sensory Expectation and the Moderated Mediation of Cosmetic Involvement
latest.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology
latest.abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of consumers’ perception of K-beauty cosmetics in the digital consumption environment on purchase intention and to examine the mediating effect of sensory expectation and the moderated mediation effect of cosmetic involvement. An online survey was conducted from April 1 to April 28, 2026, with 305 Korean women aged 20–49 years. The collected data were analyzed using SPSS 30.0 and Hayes’ PROCESS Macro. Exploratory factor analysis, reliability analysis, multiple regression analysis, mediation analysis (Model 4), moderation analysis (Model 1), and moderated mediation analysis (Model 7) were performed. The results indicated that quality perception, price perception, and brand image all had significant positive effects on purchase intention, with quality perception showing the strongest effect. Sensory expectation partially mediated the relationships between quality perception, price perception, and brand image and purchase intention, while cosmetic involvement significantly moderated the relationships between each of these perception dimensions and purchase intention. Furthermore, moderated mediation analysis revealed that only the indirect effect of price perception on purchase intention through sensory expectation significantly varied according to the level of cosmetic involvement, with the indirect effect decreasing as cosmetic involvement increased. No significant moderated mediation effects were found for quality perception or brand image. These findings demonstrate that sensory expectation and cosmetic involvement play important roles in consumers’ purchase decision-making process in the digital consumption environment. latest.title: Hubungan Pemanfaatan Riwayat Transaksi QRIS dan Disiplin Pencatatan Keuangan dengan Pengelolaan Modal Kerja UMKM Kuliner Soppeng
latest.abstract: Digitalisasi pembayaran menyediakan riwayat transaksi yang dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai informasi keuangan, tetapi penggunaan QRIS belum tentu disertai pencatatan usaha yang disiplin. Penelitian ini menganalisis hubungan pemanfaatan riwayat transaksi QRIS dan disiplin pencatatan keuangan dengan praktik pengelolaan modal kerja UMKM kuliner di Kabupaten Soppeng. Data berasal dari kuesioner lapangan atas 120 responden yang disediakan peneliti. Variabel diukur menggunakan empat butir QRIS, lima butir pencatatan keuangan, dan lima butir pengelolaan modal kerja pada skala 1–5. Skor komposit dihitung dari jawaban tersedia; 18 responden memiliki satu jawaban item kosong. Analisis menggunakan regresi linear berganda dengan galat baku robust HC3 dan uji sensitivitas kasus lengkap. Reliabilitas Cronbach’s alpha untuk ketiga konstruk berkisar 0,817–0,854. Pemanfaatan riwayat transaksi QRIS (B = 0,2882; p = 0,0005) serta disiplin pencatatan keuangan (B = 0,4414; p < 0,001) berhubungan positif dengan pengelolaan modal kerja. Model menjelaskan 31,40% variasi skor pengelolaan modal kerja (R² = 0,3140). Hasil pada 102 responden lengkap menunjukkan arah hubungan yang sama. Temuan menekankan pentingnya pemanfaatan informasi transaksi sekaligus rutinitas pembukuan bagi pengelolaan dana operasional UMKM; desain potong lintang tidak membuktikan hubungan sebab-akibat

latest.title: The Effect of Niche Perfume Selection Attributes on the Consume Happiness: The Moderating Effect of Generation through Multi-Group Analysis
latest.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology
latest.abstract: Niche perfume has emerged as a mainstream segment of the perfume market, moving beyond mass-market offerings by reflecting Millennials and Generation Z’s strong preference for individuality and distinctive scent identities. This study aims to analyze the effects of niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. In addition, Millennials and Generation Z are proposed as a moderator affecting the niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. An online survey targeted Korean women from Millennials and Generation Z who have experience using niche perfume. A total of 296 survey responses were analyzed using structural equation modeling with AMOS 26.0 and SPSS 25.0. The results revealed that four key selection attributes emerged from the analysis: trend orientation, brand awareness, premium price perception, and scent. In addition, scent, brand awareness, and premium price perception had significant effects on consumer happiness. Furthermore, the moderating effect of generation was confirmed through multi-group analysis. Specifically, Among Millennials, trend orientation, brand awareness, and premium price perception influenced consumer happiness, whereas scent was the most influential factor among Generation Z. By identifying these causal relationships, this study contributes to expanding the advancement of research on niche perfume and provides implications for developing differentiated strategies tailored to generational characteristics of the Millennials and Generation Z.

latest.title: Market Dominance and Competitive Effects of Online Travel Platforms: A Case Study of Ctrip/Trip.com Group in China
latest.venue: Journal of Applied Economics and Social Dynamics
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of China’s digital economy has made online travel agencies (OTAs) an important intermediary between consumers and suppliers of accommodation, transport and tourism services. At the same time, platform concentration, network effects and contractual restrictions can create substantial market power. This study examines Ctrip and its parent, Trip.com Group, as a case through which to evaluate the formation and competitive effects of platform dominance. The analysis combines publicly available industry and corporate data with a June 2026 consumer questionnaire. It also incorporates a factual update based on the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) decision of July 2026. The revised analysis finds strong evidence that Trip.com Group has substantial market power, particularly in online hotel-booking platform services, but it avoids treating broad OTA gross merchandise value (GMV) shares as a legally sufficient measure of dominance. The platform’s scale can generate efficiencies through matching, standardisation, service quality and investment in digital infrastructure; however, dominance may also facilitate exclusionary contracting and restrictions on hotel pricing. The consumer survey suggests high brand salience and potential switching behaviour, but its non-probability sample and several instrument inconsistencies prevent causal or population-level inference. Overall, the evidence supports a balanced view: platform scale can improve coordination and consumer convenience, while competition policy remains necessary where contractual or algorithmic mechanisms restrict merchant autonomy or foreclose rivals.

latest.title: Inovasi Produk terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen: Studi Deskriptif Kualitatif pada Departemen Yakult Lady PT Yakult Indonesia Persada Cabang Bandung 2
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis peran inovasi produk terhadap keputusan pembelian konsumen pada Departemen Yakult Lady PT Yakult Indonesia Persada Cabang Bandung 2, dengan fokus pada produk Yakult Less Sugar dan Yakult Rasa Mangga. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif, informan terdiri atas 15 Yakult Lady dan 15 konsumen/calon konsumen, kedua kelompok informan memberikan informasi mengenai Yakult Less Sugar dan Yakult Rasa Mangga. Data diperoleh melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui tahapan pengumpulan data, reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan dan verifikasi kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kedua inovasi mampu meningkatkan perhatian dan ketertarikan konsumen, tetapi memiliki tingkat penerimaan yang berbeda. Yakult Less Sugar mendapat respons positif terutama karena kandungan gula yang lebih rendah, namun persepsi harga yang lebih tinggi menjadi salah satu kendala dalam mendorong pembelian ulang. Sementara itu, Yakult Rasa Mangga memperoleh penerimaan yang lebih kuat karena menawarkan rasa yang enak, segar, dan berbeda dari produk sebelumnya. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa inovasi produk berperan sebagai salah satu stimulus dalam keputusan pembelian, tetapi bukan merupakan satu-satunya faktor penentu. Faktor harga, selera, kebutuhan, promosi, kebiasaan konsumsi, dan daya beli turut memengaruhi keputusan konsumen.

latest.title: An Empirical Analysis of Factors Influencing Brand Equity in Coffee Shops: A Study of Jakarta, Indonesia
latest.venue: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON BUSINESS AND ECONOMICS
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of the coffee shop industry in Jakarta is a direct consequence of Indonesia’s strong contribution to global coffee production as the world’s fourth-largest coffee producer. The number of coffee shops in Indonesia has reached 10,000 outlets. Due to increased competition among coffee shops, businesses are offering better service quality, innovative products, and improved ambiance and atmosphere to enhance brand loyalty, which eventually contributes to brand equity. However, limited studies have investigated the brand equity factors of coffee shop brands in Jakarta, despite the intense market competition among them. This study investigates how various brand-related factors, such as brand awareness, perceived quality, brand association, and brand loyalty, influence the overall brand equity of coffee shop brands in this highly competitive market. This study adopted a descriptive, explorative, and cross-sectional design with quantitative methods to analyze data collected from a representative sample of coffee shop consumers in Jakarta. Data were collected from 390 respondents from Jakarta city of Indonesia from 390 respondents from Jakarta, Indonesia, and were analyzed using SmartPLS. The statistical analysis confirms that there is a significant relationship between the four factors and brand equity, with perceived quality being the most influential factor among the study variables. This study provides strategic managerial recommendations for coffee shop businesses in Jakarta to enhance brand equity, underscoring the vital role of superior perceived quality while supporting sustainable business growth.

latest.title: Pengaruh Pilihan Produk, Kelengkapan Produk dan Store Atmosphere Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Emas (Studi Kasus PT. Pegadaian UPC William Iskandar)
latest.abstract: Data nasabah emas pada PT Pegadaian UPC William Iskandar berfluktuasi selama 2022–2025, dan prasurvei menunjukkan pilihan produk yang terbatas, stok yang sering kosong, serta ruang pelayanan yang kurang nyaman. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh pilihan produk, kelengkapan produk, dan store atmosphere terhadap keputusan pembelian emas. Desain kuantitatif asosiatif diterapkan pada 108 nasabah yang dipilih dengan accidental sampling; ukuran sampel ditentukan dengan rumus Slovin (e = 10%) dari 752 nasabah dan ditambah sekitar 20%. Data kuesioner skala Likert lima poin dianalisis dengan uji asumsi klasik dan regresi linear berganda menggunakan SPSS 26. Pilihan produk (B = 0,343; β = 0,274; p = 0,001), kelengkapan produk (B = 0,391; β = 0,334; p < 0,001), dan store atmosphere (B = 0,394; β = 0,383; p < 0,001) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Secara simultan, ketiga variabel signifikan (F = 443,563 > F tabel 2,69; p < 0,001; adjusted R² = 0,925). Unit layanan perlu menjaga ketersediaan ukuran emas yang dibutuhkan nasabah dan meningkatkan kenyamanan ruang pelayanan.

latest.title: The Influence of Perceived Authenticity and Local Food Image on Purchase Intention toward Local Culinary Products in Ambon City, Indonesia
latest.venue: Jurnal Ekonomi dan Kewirausahaan West Science
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of perceived authenticity and local food image on purchase intention toward local culinary products in Ambon City, Indonesia. Local culinary products represent the cultural identity and gastronomic heritage of Maluku, yet consumers’ purchase intentions may depend on how they perceive the authenticity and overall image of these products. This study employed a quantitative approach involving 120 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using SPSS, including validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression. The correlation results indicate that perceived authenticity is positively associated with purchase intention ((r = 0.413), (p < 0.001)), while local food image demonstrates a stronger positive association with purchase intention ((r = 0.506), (p < 0.001)). Perceived authenticity and local food image are also positively correlated ((r = 0.296), (p = 0.001)). Furthermore, the regression model is statistically significant overall ((F = 29.074), (p < 0.001)) and explains 33.2% of the variation in purchase intention ((R^2 = 0.332)). These findings highlight the relevance of authenticity and local food image in understanding consumer purchase intentions. The study provides insights for local culinary businesses in Ambon to strengthen product authenticity, communicate cultural identity, and develop a favorable image of regional cuisine.

latest.title: PayLater as Financial Flexibility or Consumptive Risk? An NVivo-Assisted Qualitative Study of Convenience, Debt Awareness, and Self-Control Among Generation Z
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen Pemasaran dan Perilaku Konsumen.
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study aims to explore the qualitative experiences of Generation Z PayLater users in Indonesia, focusing on three dimensions: convenience, debt awareness, and self-control. Design/Methodology/Approach – The study employed a qualitative research approach. Data were obtained from 20 anonymized consumer interview reports and analyzed using an NVivo-assisted qualitative workflow involving source preparation, case organization, thematic coding, node grouping, selected quotation matrices, and thematic visualization. Findings – The findings show that Generation Z perceives PayLater as providing payment flexibility when funds are unavailable or urgent needs arise, while debt awareness is reflected in the recognition that PayLater constitutes a financial obligation that may generate bill-related anxiety. Self-control is demonstrated through spending limits, need prioritization, early repayment, and cautious use. Overall, PayLater is not perceived merely as a shopping solution or consumption trigger, but as an ambivalent digital credit technology whose meaning depends on the interaction between platform convenience, financial risk awareness, and consumers’ ability to regulate their spending decisions. Originality/Value – The study provides a qualitative perspective on Generation Z’s lived experiences with PayLater by integrating convenience, debt awareness, and self-control into a single analytical framework. Its value lies in showing that the impact of BNPL is not inherently positive or negative but depends on how users balance technological convenience, awareness of financial obligations, and spending self-regulation.

latest.title: When Temporal Features Reuse Data: Adjacent-Window Bias in Customer Panels
latest.venue: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
latest.abstract: Customer histories are often converted into rolling or adjacent-window features for segmentation and prediction. The same period-level estimate may then appear as an outcome in one panel row and as a predictor in the next, creating apparent dynamics even when no carryover exists. We develop and apply a validation framework combining a no-carryover benchmark, fully disjoint temporal construction, an identical-sample estimator comparison and strict temporal holdout testing. The application uses 102 weeks of grocery transactions and 9,014 household-category relationships observed under both adjacent and disjoint designs. On this identical sample, the adjacent estimator implies a 1.78-percentage-point movement toward full-price purchasing for a 10-point increase in promotional share, whereas the fully disjoint estimator implies a 1.40-point movement in the opposite direction. A 36-cell Monte Carlo grid shows that adjacent estimators can remain positive under zero carryover across panel lengths and event frequencies, while disjoint estimators recover the null; under true persistence, adjacent construction attenuates or reverses the expected sign. Recent promotional share adds only .0063 to holdout AUC. The study shows that temporal feature validation must distinguish predictive usefulness from dynamic interpretation and intervention. The proposed audit supports model governance by identifying when customer-history features are informative for forecasting but unsafe for behavioural or policy claims.

hot.title: A Glance on Changing Workplace Dynamics Post Covid-19 in India: A Review of Psychological Employee Withdrawal Behavior
hot.abstract: Advances in Consumer Research (Abbreviated as Adv. Consum. Res.) is a distinguished journal based in the United States and published by Sheridan Books. The journal is highly regarded in the academic community, particularly within the fields of Business, Management, and Accounting, with a specific focus on Marketing.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Psychology’s Theory Crisis, and why formal modelling cannot solve it
hot.abstract: In light of psychology’s ‘theory crisis’, multiple authors have argued that adopting formalization and/or formal modelling would constitute a useful or even necessary step towards stronger psychological theory. In this article, I instead argue that formal modelling cannot solve the core problem the psychological ‘theory crisis’ refers to, which are the currently high degrees of contrastive and holistic underdetermination of our theories by our data. I do so by first introducing underdetermination as an explanatory framework for determining the evidential import of research findings for theories, and showing how both broader theoretical considerations and informal assumptions are key to this process. Then, I derive the aforementioned core problem from the current ‘theory crisis’ literature and tentatively explore its possible solutions. Lastly, I show that formal modelling is neither a necessary nor sufficient solution for either contrastive or holistic underdetermination, and that its uncritical adoption might instead worsen the crisis.

hot.title: From Asymmetry to Satisfaction: The Dynamic Role of Perceived Value and Trust to Boost Customer Satisfaction in the Tourism Industry
hot.abstract: The study investigates how information asymmetry affects customer satisfaction in the tourism industry by examining trust and perceived value as mediating factors. The research implements an integrated model to test and prove information asymmetry’s direct and mediating effects on customer satisfaction by examining the literature gap. The research used a quantitative approach based on opinion polls distributed to 408 customers of hotels, tourism companies, and travel agencies who were in Egypt. SmartPLS 3 software implemented the data analysis process using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Previous studies have developed scales to measure information asymmetry and its related constructs, including customer trust, perceived value, and customer satisfaction. Multiple tests showed that the measurement tools possess both reliability and validity. Results strongly support all hypotheses: information asymmetry demonstrated significant direct negative effects on customer satisfaction (β = −0.187), trust (β = −0.520), and perceived value (β = −0.453). Conversely, customer satisfaction received significant positive direct effects from both trust (β = 0.273) and perceived value (β = 0.263). Importantly, trust (indirect effect β = −0.142) and perceived value (indirect effect β = −0.119) acted as powerful mediators, confirming that information asymmetry diminishes satisfaction largely by eroding these crucial factors. Crucially, the results demonstrate that the negative impact of information asymmetry on customer satisfaction is significantly mediated jointly through two parallel pathways: the erosion of customer trust and the impairment of perceived value. hot.title: Factors influencing Generation Z’s intention to purchase sustainable clothing products in Vietnam
hot.abstract: The increasing awareness of environmental challenges has significantly influenced consumer behavior, with sustainable products, particularly sustainable clothing, becoming a top priority for Generation Z consumers. This study aims to investigate the factors influencing Generation Z's purchase intentions toward sustainable clothing in Vietnam, guided by the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model and Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) frameworks. Specifically, it examines the effects of green perceived value, green perceived quality, perceived price, social influence, product design, environmental concern, and environmental knowledge on purchase intentions. The study also explores the mediating roles of environmental attitude and product attitude in these relationships. The research employed a quantitative approach, using a Likert scale questionnaire to gather data from 641 Vietnamese Generation Z consumers. The study utilized exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM) to analyze the data. The results revealed that all proposed hypotheses were supported, indicating that all factors significantly impact environmental attitude and product attitude, which, in turn, influence purchase intention. The results emphasize the strong mediating role of environmental attitude and product attitude, suggesting that consumers with positive attitudes toward the environment and products are more likely to intend to purchase sustainable clothing. This research provides valuable insights into the psychological and contextual factors that influence Generation Z's sustainable consumption behavior. hot.title: Obstacles and opportunities for sustainable consumption: A comprehensive conceptual model, literature review, and research agenda
hot.abstract: Abstract Meaningful shifts in consumption habits are essential to mitigate climate change and reduce global environmental degradation. Yet, despite the climate urgency and growing consumer concerns, the widespread adoption of sustainable behaviors has proven difficult. Why is this the case? How has the growing interdisciplinary field of sustainable consumption contributed to this debate? And where are the knowledge gaps? Guided by a comprehensive conceptual model, this article (a) delves into the key market , individual , and s ocietal obstacles that hinder consumers from adopting more environmentally sustainable behaviors, (b) explores how practitioners and policymakers can help consumers minimize or circumvent these deterrents, and (c) highlights the pressing gaps in the literature, offering a roadmap for advancing our understanding of how to promote sustainable practices across the consumer journey—from search and purchase to usage and disposal.

hot.title: From perceived green product quality to purchase intention: the roles of price sensitivity and environmental concern
hot.abstract: Purpose This research seeks to address the existing gaps in the literature by rigorously investigating the influence of consumers’ perceived green product quality (PPQ), price sensitivity to green products (PRS) and environmental concern (ENC) on their intention to purchase green products (GPI) within the context of green circular economies. Furthermore, the study will explore the role of PRS as a mediator and ENC as a moderator by applying the price-expectancy model (PEM) and social exchange theory (SET). Design/methodology/approach The purposive sampling technique was employed to analyse 412 online survey responses from consumers, utilising partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The findings indicate a positive relationship between PPQ and PRS and PRS and GPI, contradicting the hypothesised negative associations. This suggests that as consumers become increasingly price-sensitive, they perceive green products to possess higher quality without diminishing their purchase intentions. Additionally, PPQ is positively associated with GPI, implying that enhanced perceptions of quality directly contribute to an increased intention to purchase green products. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that while ENC moderates the relationship between PPQ and PRS, its practical significance is limited. Practical implications This research emphasises to marketers that they should prioritise quality features while addressing PRS, particularly for environmentally concerned consumers, which can effectively shape consumers’ GPI. Originality/value This study’s originality lies in its integration of PRS and ENC within green consumerism. This offers valuable insights into green marketing and provides marketers with practical strategies to tackle the challenge

hot.title: Understanding the Role of Financial Literacy in Enhancing Economic Stability and Resilience in Montenegro: A Data-Driven Approach
hot.abstract: Financial literacy has emerged as a crucial factor in promoting economic stability and resilience, particularly in Montenegro. With the increasing complexity of financial products and the growing need for individuals to make sound financial decisions, the importance of financial literacy cannot be overstated. This study employs a quantitative, survey-based approach to explore the association between financial literacy levels and measures of economic stability, including savings rates, active debt management, and access to financial products. Data were collected through a representative, two-stage stratified sample of 1000 Montenegrin adults aged 18–79, ensuring comprehensive geographic coverage across all Montenegrin municipalities and balanced representation by gender and age. This stratification enables a detailed analysis of financial literacy trends across the population. Correlation analysis reveals that higher levels of financial literacy are associated with better financial practices, such as increased savings and responsible credit use, thereby enhancing economic resilience at the household level. Moreover, improved financial literacy contributes to sustainability by fostering long-term financial stability, reducing inequalities, and promoting inclusive economic growth. The findings suggest that financial literacy can mitigate the impact of economic shocks, emphasizing the need for policies that promote financial education as a tool for sustainable development. This study contributes to the literature on financial literacy in emerging economies and offers actionable insights for policymakers in Montenegro and similar contexts, highlighting financial education as a pathway to individual and national economic resilience.

hot.title: The Mediating Role of Service Quality in the Relationship Between Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainable Competitive Advantages in an Emerging Economy
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The Bank of Ghana and Companies Act provides a robust and secure framework for corporate social responsibility efforts by fostering openness and corporate accountability. The Ghana Banking Sector Code of Ethics advocates for ethical banking practices, encouraging sustainable growth. This study leveraged stakeholder theory to explore the mediating role of service quality in the relationship between corporate social responsibility and sustainable competitive advantage. A multistage sampling technique was employed to collect data from 373 employees of commercial banks in Ghana. The partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) software was used to analyze the direct and indirect relationship between the variables. The study found that corporate social responsibility had a negative and insignificant impact on the sustainable competitive advantage of commercial banks in Ghana. The findings revealed that corporate social responsibility had a positive and significant relationship with service quality. The investigation also discovered that service quality had a positive and significant impact on sustainable competitive advantage. Finally, the study highlighted that service quality fully mediates the relationship between corporate social responsibility and sustainable competitive advantage. Commercial banks in Ghana should reassess their corporate social responsibility implementation strategy by adopting a comprehensive strategy framework to transform their corporate social responsibility activities into sustainable competitive advantage. They should use their corporate social responsibility activities to foster stakeholder trust, increase customer engagement, and build brand reputation.

hot.title: Impulse buying in live streaming commerce: A literature review and research agenda
hot.abstract: Impulse buying in live streaming commerce (LSC) is an emerging phenomenon characterized by spontaneous, unplanned purchases driven by real-time social interactions. Despite increasing scholarly attention, the existing literature remains fragmented, lacking consensus on antecedents, theoretical perspectives, and outcomes. This fragmentation hinders theoretical development and accumulation of knowledge of this research stream. To address these issues, this study provides a systematic review of impulse buying in LSC, synthesizing key research trends, theoretical foundations, and methodological approaches. Drawing on the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework, we propose an integrative framework that consolidates antecedents, psychological mechanisms, and outcomes of impulse buying within LSC. This comprehensive synthesis clarifies existing inconsistencies and offers structured avenues for future research. For practitioners, our framework identifies critical platform features, streamer attributes, and consumer characteristics that influence impulse buying, enabling more effective strategies and responsible practices in LSC.

hot.title: The Impact of Visual Elements of Packaging Design on Purchase Intention: Brand Experience as a Mediator in the Tea Bag Product Category
hot.abstract: While packaging design plays a vital role in experience-oriented markets, how multiple visual elements influence purchase intention through brand experience remains unclear. This study addresses this gap by employing innovative orthogonal experiments to examine the complex relationship between the visual elements of packaging design and purchase intention for low-involvement products, integrating both design and marketing perspectives. Through orthogonal experimental design, we developed 14 packaging prototypes as stimuli by systematically manipulating five visual elements (Colour, Graphics, Logo, Typography, and Layout). The framework and prototypes were validated through expert evaluation. Data were collected via a cross-sectional survey from 490 tea bag consumers and analysed using SPSS (version 29.0) for preliminary data processing and Mplus (version 8.3) for structural equation modelling. Our results reveal the direct effects of visual packaging elements on consumer purchase intention. Notably, Colour, Graphics, Logo, and Layout significantly influence purchase intention through brand experience mediation. Importantly, our multi-level analysis of visual elements unveils distinct patterns in how different design levels (e.g., colour harmony, graphic types) affect consumer responses. This study provides novel theoretical insights into how consumers make purchase decisions based on packaging design visual elements, addressing a significant gap in existing research. Unlike previous studies focusing on isolated design elements, our systematic classification and multi-level analysis offer both theoretical insights into packaging design mechanisms and practical guidelines for designers and practitioners.

hot.title: Electroencephalography Studies on Marketing Stimuli: A Literature Review and Future Research Agenda
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to explore the application of electroencephalography (EEG) tools in examining latent consumer behavior, emphasizing emotions, attention, preferences, memory, and decision‐making in response to various marketing stimuli (e.g., products, pricing, branding, and advertising). This study adopts a thematic review approach, employing a systematic literature review methodology (e.g., Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses [PRISMA] protocol). Our investigation unearthed 155 articles from the Scopus and Web of Science databases, spanning 2010–2023. The findings reveal a marked increase in EEG‐related research, underscoring its effectiveness in examining consumers' reactions to marketing stimuli. This rise reflects a growing recognition among researchers of EEG's ability to address marketing research challenges, particularly in advertising, product development, branding, and pricing. EEG research predominantly targets advertising, followed by products, branding, and pricing, and delves deeply into consumer behavior aspects such as emotional, cognitive, and decision‐making processes. The study further highlights EEG's cutting‐edge potential to predict ad success, optimize product features, and refine pricing strategies with unprecedented accuracy. Specifically, emotion‐based ads profoundly influence decision‐making, offering novel insights into consumers' emotional engagement. This study emphasizes EEG's groundbreaking role in minimizing verbal biases and revealing consumer behavior, which is increasingly recognized as critical for developing more effective marketing strategies. This review underscores EEG's theoretical and practical contributions and offers pioneering insights into marketing effectiveness and consumer engagement

hot.title: Algorithmic pricing: Implications for marketing strategy and regulation
hot.venue: International Journal of Research in Marketing
hot.abstract: Over the past decade, a growing number of firms have delegated pricing decisions to algorithms in consumer and business markets such as travel, entertainment, and retail, as well as in platform markets such as ride-sharing. We define algorithmic pricing as “the use of programs to automate the setting of prices.” Firms adopt algorithmic pricing to optimize their prices in response to changing market conditions and to leverage the efficiency gains from automation. Advances in information technology and the increased availability of digital data have further facilitated the use of algorithm-driven pricing strategies. Yet adopting algorithmic pricing is not merely a technical upgrade — it is a strategic decision that must align with a company’s existing and future marketing strategies. Moreover, algorithmic pricing can raise various regulatory concerns regarding potential threats to competition and the legality of price discrimination. This paper discusses the implementation of algorithmic pricing in the context of firms’ marketing strategies and regulatory frameworks, while outlining an agenda for future research in this increasingly important area

hot.title: Deceptive signalling: Causes, consequences and remedies
hot.abstract: Abstract Deceptive signalling occurs when resource seekers provide communication or observable behaviour that seems to indicate high‐quality attributes yet actually misleads about the resource seekers’ attributes. Deceptive signalling is an everyday phenomenon that hurts investors, consumers and high‐quality ventures alike, leading to resource misallocation and market inefficiencies. It is also a challenge for researchers interested in signalling theory, as deceptive signalling defies signalling theory's predictions, leading to ambiguity regarding if and how deceptive signals should be analysed from a signalling theory perspective. Research on deceptive signalling has accumulated, yet it is scattered across disciplines and discourses, which hampers our ability to understand the phenomenon and obstructs progress in signalling theory. To mitigate this state of affairs, this paper provides a cross‐disciplinary integrative review, systematizing extant research on deceptive signalling, developing suggestions for the integration of deceptive signalling into signalling theory and outlining a research agenda on currently unresolved questions in signalling research pertaining to deceptive signalling. Developing a better understanding of deceptive signalling seems particularly pressing as recent advances in AI technologies, which reduce the detectability of deceptive signals as well as the costs for producing such signals, will presumably lead to an exacerbation of deceptive signalling problems.

hot.title: Conceptualizing and Measuring Customer Luxury Experience in Hotels
hot.abstract: Despite the growing significance of customer luxury experience in tourism and hospitality, research on defining and measuring it remains scarce. Existing studies fail to distinguish luxury from ordinary experiences or rely on unidimensional approaches that overlook the complexity of customer luxury experiences. To address this gap, this study develops a multidimensional six-factor, 20-item customer luxury experience scale specific to luxury hospitality. Drawing on luxury and customer experience literature, three studies are conducted to develop and validate this scale. Study 1 collected and examined a large dataset of customer reviews from the Tripadvisor website to inform the domain specification and item generation process. Study 2 involved both academic and industry experts to validate the dimensions, as well as to review, refine, and suggest new items. Study 3 was a large-scale survey to calibrate and validate the scale. Findings suggest that luxury customer experience should be based on six dimensions: service quality, authenticity, escapism, exclusivity, status , and aesthetic refinement to elevate the overall perception of luxury experience. Tourism and hospitality managers can use this scale to assess and enhance customer luxury experience. This contribution enriches luxury tourism and hospitality, offering insights into how consumers perceive and experience luxury in hotels.

hot.title: The Impact of 7Ps Green Marketing Mix on Customer Commitment and Willingness to Pay a Premium Price: Evidence from Vietnam
hot.abstract: As consumers prioritize environmental issues and sustainable development, using green elements in marketing strategy has become valuable. This research examines how the 7Ps green marketing mix influences customer commitment and willingness to pay a premium price for green products, focusing on the role of green brand loyalty, association, and perceived quality. A PLS-SEM analysis of survey data from 571 young Vietnamese consumers reveals that different green 7Ps components exert distinct effects on green consumer-based brand equity (CBBE). While prior research largely focuses on green product, price, place and promotion, limited attention has been given to green human factors, process, and physical evidence, which this study addresses. The findings of this study not only confirm the significant influence of green CBBE dimensions on consumer commitment and willingness to pay a premium price but also enriches the green marketing and consumer behavior literature. Moreover, these provide practical strategies for businesses and policymakers in emerging markets to effectively leverage green marketing, strengthen consumer commitment, implement premium pricing strategies, and contribute to advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

hot.title: The push-pull-mooring model of consumer service switching: a meta-analytical review to guide future research
hot.venue: Journal of Service Theory and Practice
hot.abstract: Purpose For nearly 2 decades, the push-pull-mooring (PPM) model has been used frequently by scholars to explain consumers’ service switching intention and behavior. However, heterogeneity and incomparability between PPM model studies are prevalent issues: The chosen predictor variables, their categorization, their measurement, reported effect sizes, and effect directions vary considerably. By addressing these issues, the present meta-analytical review enables future researchers applying the PPM model to identify relevant variables and use valid measurements. Design/methodology/approach Based on 148 empirical studies employing the PPM model, the variables used to predict consumers’ service switching intention and behavior, their frequency of use, their categorization into push, pull, and mooring factors, and their measurement are assessed. The effect sizes and directions of the relationships between these variables and consumers’ service switching intention and behavior are analyzed using meta-analytic structural equation modeling. Additionally, the predictive capacity of this model and the influence of moderators are assessed. Findings Among the 148 empirical studies, 382 different independent variables were used. The three most frequently used and distinctly categorized independent variables are dissatisfaction (push), alternative attractiveness (pull), and switching costs (mooring). Overall, 152 unique sources were cited to measure these variables and the dependent variables. Dissatisfaction and alternative attractiveness increase switching intention, which positively affects switching behavior, while switching costs decrease switching intention. The model explains 30% of the variance in switching intention and 31% of the variance in switching behavior. Originality/va

hot.title: The role of robo-advisors in behavioural finance, shaping investment decisions
hot.abstract: This study focuses on using artificial intelligence-driven financial robo-advisors in the investment decision-making domain by retail investors. Based on heuristic and prospect theory, the researcher aims to examine how AI-powered financial robo-advisors (AIPFRA), through their perceived interactivity, personalisation, autonomy, algorithm interpretation and structural assurance, influence retail investors’ loss aversion and overconfidence biases, ultimately enhancing robo-advisor usage in investment decision-making. Using purposive sampling, data from 461 retail investors were collected and analysed through structural equation modelling using SmartPLS 4.0. The results indicate that, except for structural assurance, robo-advisors’ perceived personalisation, interactivity, autonomy and algorithm transparency substantially mitigated investors’ overconfidence and loss-aversion biases, enhancing robo-advisor usage for investment decision-making. The study highlights the significance of financial literacy in moderating the relationship between biases and the use of robo-advisors. The study contributed by extending Heuristic and Prospect Theories to the AI-driven robo-advisor investment ecosystem. The study comprehensively explains how AI-powered robo-advisor design features impact investor psychology and adoption by bridging behavioural biases such as loss aversion and overconfidence with technology mechanisms like interactivity, personalisation, autonomy, algorithm interpretability and structural assurance. The results can help financial institutions implement user-centric advisory tools and help fintech developers create more bias-aware robo-advisors.

hot.title: Trends and development in green and sustainability marketing: a bibliometrics analysis using VOSviewer
hot.abstract: The recent global environmental crisis and climate change have prompted greater interest among global citizens in sustainability issues. Consumers are demanding more to be done by product and service suppliers to ensure sustainability. This has sparked research and academic interest in understanding how various organisations position themselves from a sustainability perspective. This study emerges from the need to understand trends and developments in sustainability marketing. To this end, this study uses bibliometric data from the Scopus database to examine this development. The data were analysed using Microsoft Excel and VOSviewer. The study found significant growth in the literature on green and sustainable marketing which is indicative of the subject over the past couple of years. In many respects green marketing is seen by many enterprises as playing a central role in shaping consumer perceptions and brand loyalty in many markets. However, green marketing and sustainability face various challenges such as misleading claims and greenwashing which threaten consumer confidence in sustainability efforts. Overall, this study found that integrating sustainability into marketing strategies fosters environmental responsibility, builds consumer trust, and enhances business performance. In addition, frameworks such as the theory of planned behaviour (TPB) provide a foundation for understanding consumers’ green attitudes and adoption behaviour. Greenwashing can be addressed by transparency, education, and regulatory compliance. Finally, practical recommendations include fostering international cooperation, developing targeted capacity-building initiatives, and leveraging sustainability marketing to achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
